children.title: Equality-Constrained Convex QP
children.top_down_role: Convex quadratic optimization over an affine subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional convex quadratic program over an affine subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An equality-constrained convex quadratic program has the form 
\[\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{q(x):=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\;\middle|\;Ax=b\right\},\]
where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Its feasible set is the affine subspace \(F=\{x:Ax=b\}\). If \(x_0\in F\) and the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\), every feasible point is represented as \(x=x_0+Zp\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic objective is minimized over a linear-equation-defined affine subspace, whose feasible points admit a null-space parametrization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=x_0+\ker A\), and the displayed problem is a convex optimization problem.

notation.meaning: Matrix whose columns form a basis of the null space of A.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consistency of the Equality System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent exact feasibility tests for the affine constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The equality system \(Ax=b\) is feasible if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), equivalently
\[\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}([A\ b]).\]
Equivalently, \(y^\top b=0\) for every \(y\in\ker(A^\top)\). If these conditions fail, the equality-constrained QP is infeasible independently of \(Q,c,\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine constraints are feasible exactly when the right-hand side lies in the range of the constraint matrix, with equivalent rank and left-null-space tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\iff b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}([A\ b]).

notation.meaning: Matrix obtained by appending b as a column to A.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistency of the Equality System

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced-Space Boundedness, Attainment, and Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete existence classification after null-space reduction of a feasible equality-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_0\) satisfy \(Ax_0=b\), let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\), and define
\[H=Z^\top QZ\succeq0,\qquad g=Z^\top(Qx_0+c).\]
The reduced objective is \(\tfrac12p^\top Hp+g^\top p+q(x_0)\). It is bounded below if and only if \(g\in\operatorname{range}(H)\). In that case the minimum is attained and
\[\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}q(x)=\{x_0+Zp:Hp=-g\}.\]
If \(g\notin\operatorname{range}(H)\), the QP is unbounded below. The primal minimizer is unique if and only if \(H\succ0\), equivalently \(d^\top Qd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Null-space reduction completely classifies a feasible equality-constrained convex QP: a range condition gives boundedness and attainment, its failure gives unboundedness, and positive reduced curvature gives uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{Ax=b}q(x)>-\infty\iff g\in\operatorname{range}(H),\qquad g\in\operatorname{range}(H)\Longrightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}q(x)=\{x_0+Zp:Hp=-g\}.

notation.meaning: Reduced Hessian on the equality-constraint null space.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Boundedness, Attainment, and Uniqueness

children.title: Polyhedrally Constrained Convex QP
children.top_down_role: The general mixed equality-inequality model and its active-face geometry.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is a convex polyhedron, and \(F_P(x)=\{y\in P:G_i y=h_i\text{ for every }i\in I(x)\}\) is the unique minimal face of \(P\) whose relative interior contains \(x\).

notation.meaning: Set of inequality indices active at x.
Unique minimal face of P containing x.
Row i of the inequality matrix G.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed linear equalities and inequalities, including the exact active-face description at a feasible point.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) with \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{s\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^s\). A polyhedrally constrained convex quadratic program is
\[\inf_{x\in P}q(x),\qquad q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha,\qquad P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\;Gx\le h\}.\]
For \(x\in P\), define \(I(x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,s\}:G_i x=h_i\}\). The unique minimal face of \(P\) containing \(x\) in its relative interior is
\[F_P(x)=\{y\in P:G_i y=h_i\text{ for every }i\in I(x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedrally constrained convex quadratic program minimizes a convex quadratic over mixed linear equalities and inequalities. At a feasible point, the inequalities tight there determine the unique minimal face whose relative interior contains that point.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedrally Constrained Convex QP

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent and Recession Cones of the Mixed Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction-cone formulas intrinsic to the general mixed equality-inequality feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\;Gx\le h\}\), let \(x\in P\), and define \(I(x)=\{i:G_i x=h_i\}\). Then
\[T_P(x)=\{d:Ad=0,\;G_i d\le0\ \forall i\in I(x)\},\qquad P^\infty=\{d:Ad=0,\;Gd\le0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangent cone is determined by the equality rows and inequalities active at the point; the recession cone satisfies the homogeneous form of every constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_P(x)=\{d:Ad=0,\ G_i d\le0\ (i\in I(x))\}\) and \(P^\infty=\{d:Ad=0,\ Gd\le0\}\).

notation.meaning: Tangent cone of P at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent and Recession Cones of the Mixed Polyhedron

children.title: Bound-Constrained Convex QP
children.top_down_role: The specialized box and one-sided-bound model family.

assumptions_latex: \(\ell_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\), \(u_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(\ell_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\in\{1,ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron under the stated extended-endpoint convention.

notation.meaning: Lower and upper endpoints for coordinate i, with infinite endpoints representing absent bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise finite, one-sided, and absent bounds for a finite-dimensional convex quadratic program.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) with \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\). A bound-constrained convex quadratic program is
\[\inf_{x\in B}\left\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\right\},\qquad B=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i,\ i=1,\ldots,n\},\]
where \(\ell_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\), \(u_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(\ell_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\). A finite lower endpoint or finite upper endpoint defines a one-sided bound, two finite endpoints define a box constraint, and two infinite endpoints leave the coordinate unbounded. At \(x\in B\), a lower-bound index is active when \(\ell_i\in\mathbb R\) and \(x_i=\ell_i\), and an upper-bound index is active when \(u_i\in\mathbb R\) and \(x_i=u_i\). Under these conventions, \(B\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound-constrained convex quadratic program minimizes a convex quadratic subject only to componentwise bounds. Finite endpoints impose lower or upper bounds, while infinite endpoints represent absent bounds; the resulting feasible set is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constrained Convex QP

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinatewise First-Order Optimality Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality certificate specialized to componentwise bounds, including fixed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha\), where \(Q\succeq0\), and let \(x^*\in B\). Then \(x^*\) is globally optimal if and only if every coordinate satisfies
\[\begin{array}{ll}(Qx^*+c)_i=0,&\ell_i<x_i^*<u_i,\\(Qx^*+c)_i\ge0,&x_i^*=\ell_i<u_i,\\(Qx^*+c)_i\le0,&\ell_i<x_i^*=u_i.\end{array}\]
If \(\ell_i=u_i=x_i^*\), no sign restriction is imposed on that gradient component. Equivalently, \(0\in Qx^*+c+N_B(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is optimal exactly when free gradient components vanish, lower-active components are nonnegative, and upper-active components are nonpositive; fixed coordinates impose no gradient sign.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in B}q(x)\iff0\in Qx^*+c+N_B(x^*).

notation.meaning: Convex-analytic normal cone of the bound set at the candidate point.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise First-Order Optimality Conditions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Box Attainment and Strict-Convexity Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence guarantee specific to finite boxes and uniqueness under positive-definite curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every \(\ell_i,u_i\) is finite, then \(B\) is compact, so every continuous convex quadratic \(q\) attains its minimum on \(B\). If additionally \(Q\succ0\), the minimizer is unique. When an endpoint is infinite, compactness is lost and attainment requires a separate recession or coercivity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic attains a minimum on a nonempty finite box, and positive-definite curvature makes the minimizer unique; infinite endpoints remove the compactness guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in B}q(x)\ne\varnothing,\qquad Q\succ0\Longrightarrow\left|\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in B}q(x)\right|=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Box Attainment and Strict-Convexity Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinatewise Projection onto the Bound Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Euclidean projection for finite, one-sided, and absent bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), with extended endpoints allowed, the Euclidean projection is separable:
\[\bigl(P_B(v)\bigr)_i=\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,v_i\}\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n,\]
where an absent endpoint leaves the corresponding minimum or maximum inactive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible set is a Cartesian product of intervals, and its Euclidean projection clips each coordinate independently.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_i\le u_i\) under the extended-real endpoint convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(P_B(v)\bigr)_i=\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,v_i\}\}\quad\text{for every }i.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the bound-defined feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise Projection onto the Bound Set

children.title: Positive-Definite Curvature
children.top_down_role: The strictly convex regime with globally unique primal solutions when an optimum exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global strict-curvature regime for finite-dimensional convex quadratic programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\) with \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succ0\). Then \(q\) is strongly convex and coercive on \(\mathbb R^n\). Consequently, for every nonempty closed convex set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), the problem \(\inf_{x\in F}q(x)\) attains its infimum at exactly one point. More precisely, if \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)>0\), then
\[q(y)\ge q(x)+\nabla q(x)^{\mathsf T}(y-x)+\tfrac12\lambda_{\min}(Q)\lVert y-x\rVert^2\]
for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite Hessian makes the quadratic strongly convex and coercive, yielding a unique minimizer on every nonempty closed convex feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}q(x)\) is a singleton.

source_refs.locator: 2.11 Extremal Values of Convex Functions p. 69

children.title: Positive-Semidefinite Curvature
children.top_down_role: Convex quadratic curvature without a full-space strict-curvature requirement.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix condition characterizing convex, possibly non-strict quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\) with symmetric \(Q\), positive-semidefinite curvature means
\[Q\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d^{\mathsf T}Qd\ge0\ \text{for every }d\in\mathbb R^n.\]
This condition is equivalent to convexity of \(q\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). It permits nonzero directions \(d\) satisfying \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\); hence it does not by itself imply strict convexity, coercivity, existence of a minimizer, or uniqueness over a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric Hessian is positive semidefinite exactly when every directional quadratic curvature is nonnegative; zero-curvature directions may remain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if \(q\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Arbitrary direction in the ambient space.

children.title: Singular Hessian Structure
children.top_down_role: Rank-deficient quadratic forms viewed through their range-null decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Hessian Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal range-null-space decomposition of a singular positive-semidefinite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) be singular. Then
\[\mathbb R^n=\operatorname{range}(Q)\oplus\ker(Q),\qquad \operatorname{range}(Q)=\ker(Q)^{\perp}.\]
There is an orthogonal matrix \(U=[U_+,U_0]\) such that
\[Q=U_+\Lambda_+U_+^{\mathsf T},\qquad \Lambda_+\succ0,\qquad QU_0=0.\]
Thus every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) has a unique decomposition \(x=U_+y+U_0z\); the quadratic term depends only on \(y\), since \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=y^{\mathsf T}\Lambda_+y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular positive-semidefinite Hessian splits the space orthogonally into positive-curvature range directions and zero-curvature null directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R^n=\operatorname{range}(Q)\oplus\ker(Q)\), with positive curvature only on \(\operatorname{range}(Q)\).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis for the positive-eigenvalue subspace.
Orthonormal basis for the null space of Q.

children.title: Curvature Null Directions
children.top_down_role: Directions along which the quadratic contribution is flat.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Null Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective behavior along directions annihilated by a positive-semidefinite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\) with \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). For any direction \(d\),
\[d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Qd=0.\]
Along such a null direction,
\[q(x+td)=q(x)+t\,c^{\mathsf T}d\]
for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\). Hence the objective is constant on the line when \(c^{\mathsf T}d=0\), and is affine with nonzero slope when \(c^{\mathsf T}d\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a Hessian null direction, the quadratic term is constant and the full objective varies only through the linear term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Qd=0\) implies \(q(x+td)=q(x)+t c^{\mathsf T}d\).

children.title: Solution Multiplicity under Singular Curvature
children.top_down_role: Nonuniqueness regimes attributable to feasible flat directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Multiplicity under Singular Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimal-set characterization relative to one minimizer of a convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), and suppose \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}q(x)\), where \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\). Then
\[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}q(x)=\left\{x^\star+d\in F:Qd=0,\;\nabla q(x^\star)^{\mathsf T}d=0\right\}.\]
Consequently, the minimizer is nonunique exactly when a nonzero feasible displacement satisfying both equalities exists. In that event, convexity of \(F\) makes every point \(x^\star+td\), with \(0\le t\le1\), optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple minimizers occur exactly when a nonzero feasible displacement has zero quadratic curvature and is orthogonal to the gradient at an optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal set equals \(\{x^\star+d\in F:Qd=0,\ \nabla q(x^\star)^{\mathsf T}d=0\}\).

children.title: Reduced-Cone Curvature Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Curvature restricted to feasible or critical directions rather than the full variable space.

children.title: Reduced-Space Curvature
children.top_down_role: Quadratic curvature restricted to a feasible subspace induced by active equalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature restricted to the null space of active linear equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the equality-constrained quadratic program with constraint \(Ax=b\), let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have full column rank and satisfy \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\). Its reduced-space curvature is the reduced Hessian
\[H_R:=Z^{\mathsf T}QZ.\]
Every feasible direction is uniquely expressible as \(d=Zp\), and
\[d^{\mathsf T}Qd=p^{\mathsf T}H_Rp.\]
Thus \(Q\) is positive definite on nonzero feasible directions exactly when \(H_R\succ0\). Under a change of null-space basis \(\widetilde Z=ZT\) with nonsingular \(T\), the reduced Hessian changes by congruence: \(\widetilde H_R=T^{\mathsf T}H_RT\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced Hessian represents quadratic curvature in null-space coordinates for directions preserving the active equalities.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\) and \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=p^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ)p\) whenever \(d=Zp\).

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

children.title: Critical-Cone Curvature
children.top_down_role: Quadratic curvature restricted to first-order critical directions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical-Cone Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict quadratic curvature restricted to first-order neutral feasible directions at a convex-QP optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) minimize \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) over a polyhedron \(P\), and define \[C(x^*):=\{d\in T_P(x^*):\nabla q(x^*)^\top d=0\}.\] Strict critical-cone curvature means \[d^\top Qd>0\qquad\text{for every }d\in C(x^*)\setminus\{0\}.\] Equivalently, there is \(\mu>0\) such that \(d^\top Qd\ge\mu\lVert d\rVert^2\) for all \(d\in C(x^*)\). For \(Q\succeq0\), this condition is also equivalent to \(C(x^*)\cap\ker Q=\{0\}\), and hence to uniqueness of \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict critical-cone curvature requires uniformly positive quadratic curvature on every nonzero feasible direction with zero first-order objective change; for a convex QP it is equivalent to uniqueness of the optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[d^\top Qd>0\ \forall d\in C(x^*)\setminus\{0\}\bigr]\iff C(x^*)\cap\ker Q=\{0\}\iff x^*\text{ is unique}.

notation.meaning: Tangent cone of the feasible polyhedron at the optimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Curvature

children.title: Reduced-Space versus Critical-Cone Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Geometric distinctions between equality-based reduction and activity-sensitive restriction.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive definiteness of the quadratic form on \(L\setminus\{0\}\) implies positive definiteness on \(C\setminus\{0\}\); the restrictions are equivalent when \(C=L\).

notation.meaning: Critical cone assumed to be contained in L.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic comparison of curvature restricted to an equality-feasible subspace and to a critical cone contained in that subspace.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), define \(L:=\ker A\), and let \(C\subseteq L\). Then
\[d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\text{ for every }d\in L\setminus\{0\}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\text{ for every }d\in C\setminus\{0\}.\]
The converse need not hold when \(C\) is a proper subset of \(L\). If \(C=L\), the two curvature restrictions are identical. Moreover, if \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=L\), positivity on \(L\setminus\{0\}\) is equivalent to \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive curvature on an equality-feasible linear subspace implies positive curvature on every critical cone contained in that subspace. The two restrictions coincide when the cone equals the subspace, and subspace positivity is equivalently represented by a positive-definite reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space versus Critical-Cone Restrictions

children.title: Convex QP Optimal-Set Regime Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: The geometric alternatives preceding optimality and dual certification.

children.title: Finite-Optimum Attainment Regimes
children.top_down_role: Feasible regimes in which the convex quadratic objective has an attained finite minimum.

children.title: Finite Optimal Values
children.top_down_role: Feasible convex QPs whose objective infimum is a finite scalar.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Optimal Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-based classification distinct from feasibility, attainment, and boundedness of the optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex quadratic objective \(q:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and a nonempty feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), define
\[p^\star:=\inf_{x\in F}q(x).\]
The problem has a finite optimal value when \(p^\star\in\mathbb R\), equivalently when \(q\) is bounded below on \(F\). This condition concerns only the infimum: it does not, without an additional attainment result, assert the existence of \(x^\star\in F\) satisfying \(q(x^\star)=p^\star\), nor does it assert that the set of minimizers is bounded or unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite optimal value is a real-valued infimum; finiteness alone is logically distinct from attainment, uniqueness, and boundedness of minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^\star\in\mathbb R\) if and only if there exists \(\beta\in\mathbb R\) such that \(q(x)\ge\beta\) for every \(x\in F\).

source_refs.locator: 2.11 Extremal Values of Convex Functions p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recession-Cone Criterion for a Finite Optimal Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bounded-below test for a convex quadratic over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\), where \(Q\succeq0\), and let \(P\neq\varnothing\) be a polyhedron with recession cone \(P^\infty\). Then
\[\inf_{x\in P}q(x)>-\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\quad\forall d\in P^\infty\cap\ker Q.\]
Equivalently, unboundedness below occurs exactly when some \(d\in P^\infty\) satisfies \(Qd=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic has a finite infimum over a nonempty polyhedron exactly when every zero-curvature recession direction has nonnegative linear slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in P}q(x)\in\mathbb R\iff c^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\) for every \(d\in P^\infty\cap\ker Q\).
knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Cone Criterion for a Finite Optimal Value

children.title: Attained Optimal Values
children.top_down_role: Regimes where an optimizer realizes the objective infimum.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q^*\) is attained exactly when \(S^*\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value, possibly an extended real number.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment for a finite-dimensional convex quadratic program over a nonempty polyhedron.

source_refs.locator: 2.11 Extremal Values of Convex Functions p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q^*:=\inf_{x\in P}q(x)\). The optimal value is called attained if there exists \(x^*\in P\) such that \(q(x^*)=q^*\). Equivalently, the optimal set \(S^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}q(x)\) is nonempty. When \(q^*\in\mathbb R\) and \(S^*\ne\varnothing\), every \(x^*\in S^*\) is an optimal solution and all elements of \(S^*\) have the same attained value \(q^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex QP value is attained precisely when some feasible point realizes the infimum, equivalently when the global minimizer set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Attained Optimal Values

children.title: Finite Attainment Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric circumstances supporting both value finiteness and optimizer existence.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d\}\) is a nonempty closed polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x^*\in P\) with \(q(x^*)=q^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frank-Wolfe attainment theorem for convex quadratic objectives on closed polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex quadratic program \(\inf\{q(x):x\in P\}\), assume that the feasible polyhedron \(P\) is nonempty and that the infimum \(q^*\) is finite. Then the infimum is attained: there exists \(x^*\in P\) satisfying \(q(x^*)=q^*\). Thus, within finite-dimensional convex quadratic programming over closed polyhedra, the finite-value regime coincides with the finite-attainment regime; compactness or coercivity is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic bounded below on a nonempty closed polyhedron always has an optimal solution, even without compactness or coercivity.

children.title: Finite Nonattainment Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundary cases separating finite infima from realized minima.

assumptions_latex: The usual feasible region is a nonempty closed polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite nonattainment is impossible for closed polyhedral \(P\), but can occur after closedness is removed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating closed-polyhedral convex QPs from models permitting finite nonattainment.

source_refs.locator: 2.11 Extremal Values of Convex Functions p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P\) is a nonempty closed polyhedron and \(q\) is convex quadratic, then \(\inf_{x\in P}q(x)\in\mathbb R\) implies attainment, so no finite-nonattainment regime exists in this model class. Closedness is essential to that conclusion: for \(P=(0,\infty)\subset\mathbb R\) and the affine, hence convex quadratic, objective \(q(x)=x\), one has \(\inf_{x\in P}q(x)=0\), but no feasible point attains the value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite nonattainment cannot occur over a closed polyhedron. Removing closedness permits it, as minimizing x over the positive open half-line shows.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Nonattainment Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Nonpolyhedral Finite-Nonattainment Example
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nonattainment after polyhedrality is removed while closedness and convexity are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[C=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:u>0,\ v\ge u^{-1}\}\]
and minimize the affine objective \(q(u,v)=v\) over \(C\). The set \(C\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and nonpolyhedral. One has
\[\inf_{(u,v)\in C}q(u,v)=0,\]
but every feasible point has \(v>0\), so the infimum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closedness alone does not ensure attainment outside the polyhedral class: minimizing the second coordinate over the epigraph of 1/u has finite value zero but no optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is closed and convex, but \(\inf_C q=0\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_C q=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Nonpolyhedral Finite-Nonattainment Example

children.title: Optimal-Face Geometry
children.top_down_role: Facial structure of the feasible region supporting optimal solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), and \(P\) is a nonempty polyhedron.

notation.meaning: Objective gradient at the reference optimizer.
Exposed feasible face supported by the optimal gradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of the optimal set inside the gradient-exposed feasible face.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The optimal set has the representation \[S^*=P\cap(x^*+\ker Q)\cap\{x\in\mathbb R^n:(g^*)^\top(x-x^*)=0\}.\] The set \(F^*:=P\cap\{x:(g^*)^\top(x-x^*)=0\}\) is an exposed face of \(P\), and \(S^*=F^*\cap(x^*+\ker Q)\) is a convex polyhedron. The optimal set need not itself be a face of \(P\); for example, a strictly convex quadratic may have an interior singleton minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal set is the intersection of a gradient-exposed feasible face with an affine translate of the quadratic form's kernel; it need not itself be a face.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recession Geometry and Boundedness of the Optimal Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession-cone consequence of the kernel-slice representation of the optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the seed assumptions,
\[(S^*)^\infty=P^\infty\cap\ker Q\cap(g^*)^\perp.\]
Consequently, the nonempty polyhedral optimal set \(S^*\) is bounded if and only if
\[P^\infty\cap\ker Q\cap(g^*)^\perp=\{0\}.\]
A nonzero vector in this intersection generates an optimal ray \(x^*+td\), \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal set is unbounded exactly when the feasible recession cone contains a nonzero zero-curvature, zero-slope direction; such a direction generates an optimal ray.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), \(P\) is a nonempty polyhedron, and \(x^*\in S^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((S^*)^\infty=P^\infty\cap\ker Q\cap(g^*)^\perp\), and \(S^*\) is bounded iff this cone is \(\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the optimal set.
Recession cone of the feasible polyhedron.

children.title: Unique Optimal Solutions
children.top_down_role: Singleton optimal sets under sufficient feasible curvature.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is polyhedral, and \(x^*\) minimizes \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) over \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is unique if and only if \(T_P(x^*)\cap\ker Q\cap(g^*)^\perp=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedral tangent cone at the optimizer.
Orthogonal complement of the optimal gradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-cone criterion for uniqueness of an attained convex QP solution.

source_refs.locator: 2.11 Extremal Values of Convex Functions p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(T_P(x^*):=\{d:\exists\epsilon>0,\ x^*+td\in P\text{ for all }t\in[0,\epsilon]\}\), which equals the tangent cone because \(P\) is polyhedral. Then \(x^*\) is the unique optimal solution if and only if \[T_P(x^*)\cap\ker Q\cap\{d:(g^*)^\top d=0\}=\{0\}.\] Equivalently, no nonzero feasible first-order direction from \(x^*\) is simultaneously flat for both the quadratic curvature and the supporting linear term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimizer is unique exactly when no nonzero tangent direction is both Hessian-null and orthogonal to the objective gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Unique Optimal Solutions

children.title: Multiple Optimal Solutions
children.top_down_role: Positive-dimensional or otherwise non-singleton optimal sets.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is polyhedral, and \(x^*\) minimizes \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) over \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are multiple optimizers if and only if \(T_P(x^*)\cap\ker Q\cap(g^*)^\perp\) contains a nonzero vector.

notation.meaning: Tangent cone of the feasible polyhedron at the optimizer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat feasible-direction criterion for multiplicity of convex QP minimizers.

source_refs.locator: 2.11 Extremal Values of Convex Functions p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The program has more than one optimal solution if and only if there exists \(d\ne0\) such that \(d\in T_P(x^*)\), \(Qd=0\), and \((g^*)^\top d=0\). For every sufficiently small \(t>0\), the point \(x^*+td\) is then feasible and optimal. Conversely, if \(y^*\ne x^*\) is optimal, then \(d=y^*-x^*\) satisfies these three conditions, and the entire segment \([x^*,y^*]\) lies in \(S^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple minimizers exist exactly when a nonzero feasible tangent direction has zero quadratic curvature and zero gradient slope; it then generates an optimal segment.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Optimal Solutions

children.title: Face Dimension versus Solution Multiplicity
children.top_down_role: How optimal-set dimension reflects feasible flatness and active-face structure.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is polyhedral, and the optimal set \(S^*\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|S^*|=1\) if and only if \(\dim S^*=0\); otherwise \(\dim S^*\ge1\) and \(S^*\) is uncountable.

notation.meaning: Dimension of the affine hull of the optimal set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity classified by affine dimension of the nonempty polyhedral optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(S^*\) is a nonempty convex polyhedron, \(\dim S^*=0\) holds exactly when \(S^*\) is a singleton. If \(S^*\) contains two distinct points, it contains their full line segment, so \(\dim S^*\ge1\) and there are uncountably many optimal solutions. More generally, \(\dim S^*=k\) means that the affine hull of all optimal solutions has \(k\) independent directions; finite multiplicity greater than one cannot occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty convex QP optimal set is either one point or uncountably infinite. Its affine dimension is zero exactly in the unique-solution case.
knowledge_statements.title: Face Dimension versus Solution Multiplicity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimension from Flat Tangent Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relation between optimal-set dimension and locally feasible zero-curvature directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the seed assumptions, let \(g^*=Qx^*+c\). Then
\[T_{S^*}(x^*)=T_P(x^*)\cap\ker Q\cap(g^*)^\perp,\]
and hence
\[\dim S^*=\dim\operatorname{span}\bigl(T_P(x^*)\cap\ker Q\cap(g^*)^\perp\bigr).\]
Thus the affine dimension of the optimal set is the number of independent locally feasible directions that are flat for both the quadratic curvature and the first-order slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dimension of the optimal set equals the span dimension of the feasible tangent directions having zero curvature and zero objective slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim S^*=\dim\operatorname{span}(T_P(x^*)\cap\ker Q\cap(g^*)^\perp)\).

notation.meaning: Tangent cone of the optimal set at x star.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension from Flat Tangent Directions

children.title: Feasible Recession Geometry
children.top_down_role: Recession directions admitted by the affine feasible region.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{h\in\mathbb R^n:Ah\le0,\ Eh=0\}\).

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession cone of a linearly constrained feasible polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasible recession cone is \[\operatorname{rec}P:=\{h\in\mathbb R^n:x+th\in P\text{ for every }x\in P\text{ and }t\ge0\}.\] For the linear representation \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d\}\), it is the polyhedral cone \[\operatorname{rec}P=\{h:Ah\le0,\ Eh=0\}.\] Thus \(h\in\operatorname{rec}P\) identifies a ray that remains feasible from every feasible base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible recession direction preserves every linear inequality and equality along its nonnegative ray; these directions form a polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Recession Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundedness from the Recession Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundedness criterion for a nonempty feasible polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. Then \[P\text{ is bounded}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{rec}P=\{0\}.\] Thus every unbounded nonempty polyhedron admits a nonzero recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron is bounded exactly when its recession cone contains only zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\text{ is bounded}\iff\operatorname{rec}P=\{0\}.

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the feasible polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundedness from the Recession Cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lineality of the Feasible Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided feasible recession directions of a linearly represented polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d\}\neq\varnothing\), \[\operatorname{lin}P:=\operatorname{rec}P\cap(-\operatorname{rec}P)=\{h:Ah=0,\ Eh=0\}.\] Equivalently, \(h\in\operatorname{lin}P\) exactly when \(x+th\in P\) for every \(x\in P\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lineality space consists of recession directions feasible in both signs and equals the common null space of the constraint matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{lin}P=\operatorname{rec}P\cap(-\operatorname{rec}P)=\{h:Ah=0,\ Eh=0\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Lineality of the Feasible Polyhedron

children.title: Unbounded Descent Directions
children.top_down_role: Feasible recession directions associated with objective values decreasing without a finite minimum.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), and \(P\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Qh=0\) and \(c^\top h<0\) imply \(q(x+th)\to-\infty\) for every \(x\in P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable ray certificate for unboundedness below of a convex QP.

source_refs.locator: 2.11 Extremal Values of Convex Functions p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(h\) satisfying \(h\in\operatorname{rec}P\), \(Qh=0\), and \(c^\top h<0\) certifies unbounded descent. Indeed, for every \(x\in P\) and \(t\ge0\), feasibility is preserved and \[q(x+th)=q(x)+t c^\top h.\] Consequently \(q(x+th)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\), and \(\inf_{x\in P}q(x)=-\infty\). For \(Q\succeq0\), the check \(h^\top Qh=0\) is equivalent to \(Qh=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible recession direction with zero quadratic curvature and negative linear slope certifies that the objective tends to minus infinity along its ray.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Descent Directions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Recession Characterization of Unboundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity and sufficiency of a curvature-free negative-slope feasible recession direction for convex-QP unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), where \(Q=Q^\top\succeq0\), and let \(P\) be a nonempty polyhedron. Then \[\inf_{x\in P}q(x)=-\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists h\in\operatorname{rec}P:\ Qh=0,\ c^\top h<0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic over a nonempty polyhedron is unbounded below exactly when a feasible recession direction has zero quadratic curvature and negative linear slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in P}q(x)=-\infty\iff\exists h\in\operatorname{rec}P:\ Qh=0,\ c^\top h<0.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Recession Characterization of Unboundedness

children.title: Noncoercive Finite Regimes
children.top_down_role: Flat recession behavior compatible with a finite optimal value.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), and \(P\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) is noncoercive on \(P\) if and only if some \(0\ne h\in\operatorname{rec}P\) satisfies \(Qh=0\) and \(c^\top h=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued but noncoercive convex QPs characterized by objective-flat recession directions.

source_refs.locator: 2.11 Extremal Values of Convex Functions p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(q\) is bounded below on \(P\). Then \(q\) is noncoercive relative to \(P\), equivalently some nonempty sublevel set \(L_\alpha\) is unbounded, if and only if there exists \(0\ne h\in\operatorname{rec}P\) with \(Qh=0\) and \(c^\top h=0\). In that case, finite attainment still holds, and every optimizer \(x^*\) generates the unbounded optimal ray \(x^*+th\), \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded-below convex QP is noncoercive exactly when it has a nonzero feasible recession direction along which both curvature and linear slope vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Noncoercive Finite Regimes

children.title: Recession-Based Status Separation
children.top_down_role: Geometric separation of finite noncoercive behavior from objective unboundedness.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), and \(P\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sign of \(c^\top h\) on \(R\cap\ker Q\) separates unbounded descent, finite noncoercivity, and coercivity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete recession classification for a convex quadratic over a nonempty polyhedron.

source_refs.locator: 2.11 Extremal Values of Convex Functions p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_0:=\operatorname{rec}P\cap\ker Q\). Exactly one of the following status regimes applies. If some \(h\in R_0\) has \(c^\top h<0\), then \(\inf_Pq=-\infty\). Otherwise the optimal value is finite and attained. Within the finite regime, \(q\) is noncoercive on \(P\) exactly when some \(0\ne h\in R_0\) has \(c^\top h=0\); it is coercive on \(P\) exactly when \(c^\top h>0\) for every \(0\ne h\in R_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature-free recession directions classify status: negative slope gives unboundedness, zero slope gives finite noncoercivity, and strictly positive slope gives coercivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Based Status Separation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary and Sufficient Local Optimality Condition for a Linearly Constrained QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes local minimizers using existence of KKT multipliers and nonnegative Hessian curvature on the corresponding critical-direction cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) be feasible for \(\min Q(x)=\tfrac12x^TGx+g^Tx\) subject to \(a_i^Tx=b_i\) for \(i\in E\) and \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\) for \(i\in I\), with \(G=G^T\). Then \(x^*\) is a local minimizer if and only if there exists \(\lambda^*\) such that \[(x^*,\lambda^*)\text{ satisfies the KKT conditions}\] and \[d^TGd\ge0\qquad\forall d\in\mathcal G(x^*,\lambda^*),\] where \(\mathcal G(x^*,\lambda^*)\) consists of the nonzero directions satisfying \(a_i^Td=0\) for \(i\in E\), \(a_i^Td\ge0\) for active \(i\in I\), and \(a_i^Td=0\) for active inequalities with \(\lambda_i^*>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point of a linearly constrained QP is a local minimizer exactly when it has KKT multipliers for which the Hessian quadratic form is nonnegative on the associated nonzero critical-direction cone.
assumptions_latex: x^*\text{ is feasible for the stated linearly constrained QP}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ is a local minimizer}\iff\exists\lambda^*:\ (x^*,\lambda^*)\text{ is a KKT pair and }d^TGd\ge0\ \forall d\in\mathcal G(x^*,\lambda^*).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Optimality Conditions for a Standard-Form Linear Program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient optimality system for a standard-form LP; linearity removes any need for LICQ, even when the constraint gradients are dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). A vector \(x^*\) solves \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) if and only if there exist \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(s^*\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(A^T\lambda^*+s^*=c\), \(Ax^*=b\), \(x^*\geq0\), \(s^*\geq0\), and \(x_i^*s_i^*=0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Under nonnegativity, componentwise complementarity is equivalent to \((x^*)^Ts^*=0\), and every such triple satisfies \(c^Tx^*=b^T\lambda^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a standard-form linear program, a point is globally optimal exactly when it can be completed by equality-constraint multipliers and nonnegative dual slacks satisfying stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity. This remains necessary when the linear constraint gradients are dependent. Componentwise complementarity is equivalent to a zero primal-slack inner product, and the primal and dual objective values then agree.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad b\in\mathbb R^m,\quad c\in\mathbb R^n
\text{All constraints are linear; LICQ is not required.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ is optimal}\iff \exists(\lambda^*,s^*):\ A^T\lambda^*+s^*=c,\ Ax^*=b,\ x^*,s^*\geq0,\ x_i^*s_i^*=0\ \forall i;\quad c^Tx^*=b^T\lambda^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Slack KKT system, central-path perturbation, and Newton linearization for convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers inequality-constrained convex QPs. Equality constraints are only noted as admitting an extension and are not formulated here. Claims about a central-path trajectory are conditional on the existence of positive solutions of the perturbed equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\), with \(G=G^T\succeq0\), and introduce \(y=Ax-b\ge0\). The slack-form KKT conditions are \(Gx-A^T\lambda+c=0\), \(Ax-y-b=0\), \(\mathcal Y\Lambda e=0\), and \((y,\lambda)\ge0\); for this convex QP they are necessary and sufficient for global optimality. At a point with \((y,\lambda)>0\), define \(\mu=y^T\lambda/m\). For \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), the perturbed equations are \[F(x,y,\lambda;\sigma\mu)=\begin{bmatrix}Gx-A^T\lambda+c\\Ax-y-b\\\mathcal Y\Lambda e-\sigma\mu e\end{bmatrix}=0.\] Whenever positive solutions exist as the positive perturbation parameter varies, they define the central-path trajectory described in the extract, approaching a QP solution as \(\sigma\mu\to0\). Newton linearization gives \[\begin{bmatrix}G&0&-A^T\\A&-I&0\\0&\Lambda&\mathcal Y\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\\\Delta\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-r_d\\-r_p\\-\Lambda\mathcal Ye+\sigma\mu e\end{bmatrix},\] where \(r_d=Gx-A^T\lambda+c\) and \(r_p=Ax-y-b\); an update may use a step length preserving \((y+\alpha\Delta y,\lambda+\alpha\Delta\lambda)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an inequality-constrained convex quadratic program, nonnegative slacks express the KKT conditions as stationarity, primal feasibility, and complementarity equations. Positive semidefiniteness of the quadratic Hessian makes any KKT point globally optimal. Replacing zero complementarity by a positive target gives the perturbed KKT system; its positive solutions, when they exist, form the central-path trajectory described in the extract. Newton linearization produces the coupled primal-dual direction, and the update is restricted to preserve positive slacks and multipliers.
assumptions_latex: (y,\lambda)>0\ \text{when defining }\mu\text{ and forming the interior Newton step}
\text{The trajectory assertion is conditional on positive solutions of the perturbed system existing.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The convex-QP KKT system characterizes global solutions, and perturbing its complementarity equations yields the central-path equations and their primal-dual Newton linearization.}
knowledge_statements.title: Slack KKT system, central-path perturbation, and Newton linearization for convex QP

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT necessity for affine-constrained quadratic programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: QP-specific multiplier existence and first-order conditions at a solution, including the absence of an LICQ requirement for affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x q(x)=\tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx\) subject to \(a_i^Tx=b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Define \(\mathcal A(x^*)=\{i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I:a_i^Tx^*=b_i\}\). If \(x^*\) is a solution, then there are multipliers \(\lambda_i^*\), \(i\in\mathcal A(x^*)\), such that \(Gx^*+c-\sum_{i\in\mathcal A(x^*)}\lambda_i^*a_i=0\), \(a_i^Tx^*=b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal A(x^*)\), \(a_i^Tx^*\ge b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\setminus\mathcal A(x^*)\), and \(\lambda_i^*\ge0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\cap\mathcal A(x^*)\). No linear-independence assumption on the active constraint normals is required because all constraints are affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every solution of an affine equality- and inequality-constrained quadratic program has multipliers satisfying stationarity, primal feasibility, and nonnegativity for active inequality multipliers. Active-constraint linear independence is not required because the constraints are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\{\lambda_i^*:i\in\mathcal A(x^*)\}:\quad Gx^*+c-\sum_{i\in\mathcal A(x^*)}\lambda_i^*a_i=0,\quad \lambda_i^*\ge0\ \ (i\in\mathcal I\cap\mathcal A(x^*)).

knowledge_statements.title: Existence of Optimal Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier existence for a feasible convex QP with affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive semidefinite, \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\;Gx\le h.\] If \(x^*\) is optimal, then there exist \(y^*\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(\mu^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\) such that \[Qx^*+c+A^{\mathsf T}y^*+G^{\mathsf T}\mu^*=0,\quad Ax^*=b,\quad Gx^*\le h,\quad \mu_i^*(G_i x^*-h_i)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Thus every optimal solution of this polyhedrally constrained convex QP admits KKT multipliers without an additional constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every optimum of a convex quadratic program with affine constraints has equality and nonnegative inequality multipliers satisfying the KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists(y^*,\mu^*)\) satisfying stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity.

children.title: Polyhedral Normal-Cone Representation
children.top_down_role: The polyhedral geometric route connecting primal optimality to multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Normal-Cone Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal cone of an affine equality-and-inequality feasible set at a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^m\), and suppose \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\;Gx\le h\}\) is nonempty. For \(x\in C\), define \(I(x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:G_i x=h_i\}\) and \[N_C(x)=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\langle v,z-x\rangle\le0\ \text{for every }z\in C\}.\] Then \[N_C(x)=\left\{A^{\mathsf T}y+G_{I(x)}^{\mathsf T}\mu:y\in\mathbb R^p,\ \mu\in\mathbb R_+^{|I(x)|}\right\}.\] Equivalently, the inactive inequality multipliers are zero. The representation remains valid for redundant affine constraint systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal cone of a polyhedron is generated by equality normals and nonnegative combinations of active inequality normals.
assumptions_latex: \(C\ne\varnothing\) is represented by finitely many affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(x)=\{A^{\mathsf T}y+G_{I(x)}^{\mathsf T}\mu:y\in\mathbb R^p,\mu\in\mathbb R_+^{|I(x)|}\}\).

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to C at x

children.title: Multiplier-Existence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of multiplier conclusions outside the intended polyhedral convex setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Existence Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure after replacing affine constraints by a degenerate convex nonlinear constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Polyhedrality cannot be discarded without replacing it by an appropriate constraint qualification. For example, consider
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\ x\quad\text{subject to}\quad x^2\le0.\]
The feasible set is \(\{0\}\), so \(x^*=0\) is the unique global minimizer. A KKT multiplier would have to satisfy \(\lambda\ge0\), \(\lambda x^{*2}=0\), and
\[1+\lambda(2x^*)=0.\]
At \(x^*=0\), stationarity becomes \(1=0\), which is impossible. Thus an optimum need not possess a multiplier for a differentiable convex inequality when constraint qualifications fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outside affine constraints, multiplier existence can fail: minimizing x subject to x²≤0 has a unique optimum but no KKT multiplier.
assumptions_latex: The affine-constraint hypothesis is replaced by the convex differentiable constraint \(x^2\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*=0\) is optimal, but no \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfies KKT stationarity.

children.title: KKT Sufficiency
children.top_down_role: KKT certificates as sufficient evidence of optimality in convex QPs.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT Sufficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficiency of the complete KKT system for a convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive semidefinite, \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\;Gx\le h.\] If \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar\mu)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfies \[Q\bar x+c+A^{\mathsf T}\bar y+G^{\mathsf T}\bar\mu=0,\quad A\bar x=b,\quad G\bar x\le h,\quad \bar\mu_i(G_i\bar x-h_i)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\] then \(\bar x\) is a global minimizer, \((\bar y,\bar\mu)\) is optimal for the Lagrangian dual, and the primal and dual objective values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any feasible point and multipliers satisfying the KKT conditions of a convex QP are globally primal-dual optimal with zero duality gap.
assumptions_latex: \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar\mu)\) satisfies the displayed KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is globally optimal, \((\bar y,\bar\mu)\) is dual optimal, and the duality gap is zero.

notation.meaning: candidate primal point and KKT multipliers

If \(G\succeq0\), then \(x^*\) is a global minimizer.

children.title: Global Optimality from Convexity
children.top_down_role: The global scope of certified optima supplied by convex objective and feasible geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Optimality from Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order global-optimality mechanism underlying KKT sufficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and convex, let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(x^*\in C\). If \[\langle\nabla f(x^*),x-x^*\rangle\ge0\qquad\text{for every }x\in C,\] then \[f(x^*)\le f(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in C.\] Consequently, \(x^*\) is a global minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable convex objective, a feasible point satisfying the variational inequality is globally optimal over the convex feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and convex on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^*)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local minima are global in convex optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-optimality consequence for minimizing a convex objective over a convex feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex. If \(x^*\in C\) is a local minimizer of \(\min_{x\in C}f(x)\), then \(x^*\) is a global minimizer; equivalently, \(f(x^*)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization of a convex function over a convex feasible region, every local minimizer is a global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\in C\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x\in C,\ f(x^*)\le f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Local minima are global in convex optimization

directory_assessment.rationale: The A11 node is a legitimate convex-QP specialization of the general local-to-global theorem. Primary ownership should remain with general convex analysis or convex-programming theory, with A11 cross-indexing the specialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficiency beyond Strict Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT sufficiency requires positive semidefiniteness, not positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive semidefinite, possibly singular, and consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\;Gx\le h,\] where the constraints are affine. Any feasible \(x^*\) for which there exist multipliers \(y^*\) and \(\mu^*\ge0\) satisfying stationarity and complementarity is a global minimizer. Positive definiteness of \(Q\) is not required; singularity can permit multiple primal minimizers without invalidating KKT sufficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular positive-semidefinite Hessian still makes the KKT conditions sufficient, although it may allow multiple primal optimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal component of the KKT triple is globally optimal.

notation.meaning: Hessian of the convex quadratic objective

children.title: Primal-Solution Uniqueness
children.top_down_role: Curvature regimes yielding a singleton primal optimal set.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Solution Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A curvature condition guaranteeing uniqueness of the convex-QP primal optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\{x:Ax=b,\;Gx\le h\}\) be nonempty and suppose the convex quadratic objective \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) attains its minimum on \(C\). If
\[d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\qquad\text{for every nonzero }d\in C-C,\]
then the minimizer is unique. In particular, \(Q\succ0\) is sufficient. More locally, if \(x^*\) is optimal, positivity on every nonzero feasible chord direction \(d=x-x^*\), with \(x\in C\), excludes any second optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal optimizer is unique when the quadratic form is positive on every nonzero difference of feasible points; positive definiteness suffices.
assumptions_latex: The minimum over the nonempty polyhedron \(C\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex quadratic program has exactly one primal minimizer.

notation.meaning: set of differences of pairs of feasible points

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The curvature condition is mathematically plausible and sufficient, but the cited section on representation of convex sets does not inspectably support this uniqueness criterion. A source specifically covering strict convexity or quadratic-program solution uniqueness is required; the problem-data dimensions should also be made explicit.

children.title: Multiplier Uniqueness
children.top_down_role: Active-constraint geometry yielding a unique dual representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LICQ-based uniqueness of KKT multipliers at a fixed primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a quadratic program with equality matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) and inequality matrix \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Let \(x^*\) admit a KKT multiplier pair and define \(I(x^*)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:G_i x^*=h_i\}\). If the rows of \[\begin{bmatrix}A\\G_{I(x^*)}\end{bmatrix}\] are linearly independent, then exactly one pair \((y^*,\mu^*)\in\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfies the KKT conditions at \(x^*\). Inactive inequality multipliers equal zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed KKT point, linear independence of the equality and active-inequality gradients guarantees a unique multiplier pair.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) admits at least one KKT multiplier pair.
The rows of \(A\) together with \(G_{I(x^*)}\) are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one pair \((y^*,\mu^*)\) satisfies the KKT conditions at \(x^*\).

children.title: Unique Primal Solutions with Multiple Multipliers
children.top_down_role: Regimes separating primal uniqueness from dual uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.title: Unique Primal Solutions with Multiple Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundant active inequalities separate primal uniqueness from multiplier uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\ \tfrac12x^2-x\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\le0,\quad 2x\le0.\]
The objective is strictly convex, and its unique constrained minimizer is \(x^*=0\). For inequality multipliers \(\mu_1,\mu_2\ge0\), stationarity at \(x^*\) is
\[-1+\mu_1+2\mu_2=0.\]
Consequently every pair
\[(\mu_1,\mu_2)=(1-2t,t),\qquad 0\le t\le\tfrac12,\]
satisfies stationarity, dual feasibility, and complementarity. Thus the primal solution is unique while the multiplier set is a nontrivial line segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicated active inequalities yield infinitely many multipliers even though strict convexity makes the primal QP solution unique.
assumptions_latex: The two displayed inequalities are retained as distinct constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*=0\) is the unique primal solution, but \(\{(1-2t,t):0\le t\le\tfrac12\}\) is its multiplier set.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Primal-Dual Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient regime for uniqueness of both the primal solution and its multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite, \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^m\). Suppose the problem \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\;Gx\le h\] is feasible and attains its minimum. Its primal optimizer \(x^*\) is unique. Define \(I(x^*)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:G_i x^*=h_i\}\). If KKT multipliers exist and the rows of \(A\) together with those of \(G_{I(x^*)}\) are linearly independent, then the multiplier pair \((y^*,\mu^*)\) is unique. Consequently, the complete KKT triple \((x^*,y^*,\mu^*)\) is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite curvature plus linear independence of equality and active inequality gradients yields a unique primal-dual KKT triple.
assumptions_latex: The displayed affine-constrained QP is feasible and attains its minimum.
The rows of \(A\) and \(G_{I(x^*)}\) are jointly linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is exactly one KKT triple \((x^*,y^*,\mu^*)\).

children.title: Normal-Cone Optimality
children.top_down_role: Optimality represented through feasible-set normal geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric first-order characterization of convex-QP minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succeq0\). For \(x^*\in C\),
\[x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in Qx^*+c+N_C(x^*).\]
Equivalently,
\[-(Qx^*+c)\in N_C(x^*)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \langle Qx^*+c,x-x^*\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for every }x\in C.\]
Thus optimality is represented by opposition between the objective gradient and a feasible-set normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point minimizes a convex quadratic exactly when the negative objective gradient belongs to the feasible set's normal cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is optimal if and only if \(0\in Qx^*+c+N_C(x^*)\).

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to C at the feasible point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normal-cone characterization and its sign convention are correct, but the cited locator concerns representation of convex sets and does not inspectably support this optimality theorem. A specific normal-cone or convex optimality locator is required.

children.title: Subdifferential Optimality
children.top_down_role: Optimality represented through the subdifferential of the composite objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-value subdifferential characterization of constrained convex-QP optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, define \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succeq0\), and let \(\delta_C\) be the indicator of \(C\). For every \(x^*\in C\),
\[x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial(f+\delta_C)(x^*).\]
Because \(f\) is finite and differentiable on \(\mathbb R^n\), the sum rule yields
\[\partial(f+\delta_C)(x^*)=Qx^*+c+\partial\delta_C(x^*)=Qx^*+c+N_C(x^*).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained convex-QP optimality is equivalent to zero belonging to the subdifferential of the objective plus the feasible-set indicator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is optimal if and only if \(0\in\partial(f+\delta_C)(x^*)\).

notation.meaning: zero on C and positive infinity outside C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subdifferential characterization and sum rule are correct under the stated assumptions, but the cited section on representation of convex sets does not inspectably support subdifferential optimality or the sum rule. A specific section, theorem, or page covering these claims is required.

notation.meaning: Convex-analytic normal cone to the feasible set at x.
Indicator function of C, equal to zero on C and positive infinity outside C.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex QP with the convex-analytic normal-cone convention.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in C\), define \(N_C(x)=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\langle v,y-x\rangle\leq0\ \text{for every }y\in C\}\), and let \(\delta_C\) be the indicator of \(C\). For every \(x\in C\),
\[\partial(f+\delta_C)(x)=\nabla f(x)+N_C(x)=Qx+q+N_C(x).\]
The corresponding optimality representations are
\[\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in Q\bar x+q+N_C(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial(f+\delta_C)(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex quadratic over a closed convex set, normal-cone stationarity and subdifferential stationarity are identical and characterize global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone versus Subdifferential Representations

children.title: Feasible-Direction-Tangent-Cone Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: The directional representation of first-order optimality.

children.title: Feasible-Direction Optimality
children.top_down_role: Directional optimality expressed over directions preserving feasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) minimizes \(f\) on \(C\) if and only if \(\langle Q\bar x+q,d\rangle\geq0\) for every \(d\in D_C(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Cone of directions generating a feasible segment from x.
Gradient of the quadratic objective at x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order feasible-direction characterization for a differentiable convex quadratic.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in C\), define the feasible-direction cone by
\[D_C(x)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:\text{there exists }\varepsilon>0\text{ such that }x+td\in C\text{ for every }t\in[0,\varepsilon]\}.\]
Then
\[\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\langle Q\bar x+q,d\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }d\in D_C(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point minimizes the convex quadratic exactly when every direction supporting a feasible segment has nonnegative directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Direction Optimality

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Tangent-Cone Optimality
children.top_down_role: Directional optimality expressed through the local tangent cone.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\iff \langle Q\bar x+q,d\rangle\geq0\) for all \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone to C at x.
Convex-analytic normal cone to C at x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-cone form of first-order optimality for a closed convex feasible set.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[T_C(x)=\left\{d:\text{there exist }x_k\in C\text{ and }t_k\downarrow0\text{ with }\frac{x_k-x}{t_k}\to d\right\}.\]
For the closed convex set \(C\), the polar relation is \(N_C(x)=T_C(x)^\circ\), where \(K^\circ=\{v:\langle v,d\rangle\leq0\text{ for all }d\in K\}\). Hence
\[\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\langle Q\bar x+q,d\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }d\in T_C(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point minimizes the convex quadratic exactly when the objective gradient is nonnegative on its entire tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangent-Cone Optimality

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Feasible-Direction versus Tangent-Cone Geometry
children.top_down_role: The relationship between explicit feasible directions and their local conic closure.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and convex, and \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(x)=\overline{D_C(x)}=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(C-x)}\), so continuous linear inequalities on \(D_C(x)\) and \(T_C(x)\) are equivalent.

notation.meaning: Cone of feasible-segment directions at x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure relation for feasible directions of a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The feasible-direction cone and tangent cone satisfy
\[D_C(x)=\bigcup_{\varepsilon>0}\{d:x+td\in C\text{ for every }t\in[0,\varepsilon]\}=\operatorname{cone}(C-x),\qquad T_C(x)=\overline{D_C(x)}.\]
Thus feasible directions need not form a closed cone, whereas \(T_C(x)\) is closed. For every \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), continuity of \(d\mapsto\langle g,d\rangle\) yields
\[\langle g,d\rangle\geq0\ \text{for all }d\in D_C(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\langle g,d\rangle\geq0\ \text{for all }d\in T_C(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex set, the tangent cone is the closure of the feasible-direction cone; therefore both cones yield the same linear first-order test.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Direction versus Tangent-Cone Geometry

children.title: Variational-Inequality Optimality
children.top_down_role: The monotone affine variational-inequality representation.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\) if and only if it minimizes \(\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\) over \(C\).

notation.meaning: Monotone affine operator induced by the quadratic objective.
Variational inequality for F on C.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine monotone variational inequality equivalent to convex QP optimality.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because \(Q\succeq0\), the affine map \(F(x)=Qx+q\) is monotone:
\[\langle F(x)-F(y),x-y\rangle=(x-y)^\top Q(x-y)\geq0.\]
A point \(\bar x\in C\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\) when
\[\langle F(\bar x),y-\bar x\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }y\in C.\]
This variational inequality is equivalent to \(0\in F(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\), and therefore
\[\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\right\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\bar x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(F,C).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex QP is equivalent to a variational inequality for its monotone affine gradient map over the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Variational-Inequality Optimality

children.title: Constraint-Regularity Multiplier Geometry
children.top_down_role: Regularity notions separated according to their roles in multiplier existence, uniqueness, and sensitivity.

children.title: Polyhedral Normal-Cone Regularity
children.top_down_role: Regularity supplied by affine and polyhedral feasible-set geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\leq h\}\) is nonempty, \(\bar x\in C\), and \(I(\bar x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:G_i\bar x=h_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(\bar x)=\{A^\top\nu+G_{I(\bar x)}^\top\lambda:\nu\in\mathbb R^p,\ \lambda\in\mathbb R_+^{|I(\bar x)|}\}\) without a constraint qualification.

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities active at the feasible point.
Submatrix formed by active inequality rows.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact normal-cone formula for an affine-polyhedral feasible set.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(\bar x\in C\), the polyhedral normal cone is
\[N_C(\bar x)=\left\{A^\top\nu+G_{I(\bar x)}^\top\lambda:\nu\in\mathbb R^p,\ \lambda\in\mathbb R_+^{|I(\bar x)|}\right\}.\]
Equivalently, after extending \(\lambda\) by zeros outside \(I(\bar x)\),
\[v\in N_C(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v=A^\top\nu+G^\top\lambda,\quad \lambda\geq0,\quad \lambda_i(G_i\bar x-h_i)=0\ \text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}.\]
This representation requires neither Slater regularity nor linear independence of the active constraint normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At any point of a polyhedron, its normal cone is generated exactly by equality normals and active inequality normals, without a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Normal-Cone Regularity
