children.title: Interior-Regularity Route Family
children.top_down_role: Interior regularity routes and their proper role relative to the polyhedral QP setting.

children.title: Relative-Interior Regularity
children.top_down_role: Regularity expressed through relative interior for lower-dimensional convex domains.

assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions, and \(Ax=b\) is affine.
There exists \(x^0\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\bigcap_i\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g_i)\) with \(Ax^0=b\) and \(g_i(x^0)<0\) for every nonaffine inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex subdifferential sum and normal-cone calculus are exact, yielding Lagrange multipliers and KKT necessity at every attained optimum.

notation.meaning: Relative interior in the affine hull.
Effective domain of an extended-real-valued function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-interior qualification for finite-dimensional convex programs.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\) and \(Ax=b\). A relative-interior qualification holds if there is \(x^0\) in the common relative interior of the effective domains, satisfying \(Ax^0=b\), such that every nonaffine inequality is strict at \(x^0\). Under this condition, the convex subdifferential and normal-cone calculus used in the optimality system is exact. Consequently, at every attained optimum \(\bar x\), there exist \(\lambda\geq0\) and \(\nu\) such that
\[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial g_i(\bar x)+A^\top\nu,\qquad \lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\quad\text{for every }i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible relative-interior point, strict for nonaffine inequalities, validates exact convex calculus and guarantees KKT multipliers at an attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Regularity

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed qualification requires strict satisfaction only for nonaffine inequalities but does not explicitly require the affine inequalities to be feasible at \(x^0\). The exact relative-interior constraint-qualification theorem and its hypotheses are not supported by the cited relative-interior section alone, so source verification is required before selecting a mathematically reliable replacement.

children.title: Slater Regularity
children.top_down_role: Strict-feasibility specialization for inequality-constrained convex formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are convex and finite, and \(Ax=b\) is affine.
There exists \(x^0\) with \(Ax^0=b\) and \(g_i(x^0)<0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong Lagrange duality holds when the primal value is finite, and every attained primal optimum admits KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Slater condition for convex inequality constraints and affine equalities.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the convex program
\[\inf\{f(x):g_i(x)\leq0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m,\ Ax=b\},\]
Slater regularity is the existence of \(x^0\) satisfying \(Ax^0=b\) and \(g_i(x^0)<0\) for every inequality. If the primal optimal value is finite, this condition yields equality of the primal value and the Lagrange-dual value. If a primal optimum \(\bar x\) is attained, there exist \(\lambda\geq0\) and \(\nu\) satisfying primal feasibility, complementary slackness, and
\[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial g_i(\bar x)+A^\top\nu.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point satisfying all convex inequalities strictly and all equalities exactly guarantees strong duality and KKT multipliers for an attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Slater Regularity

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Polyhedral QP Specialization
children.top_down_role: The proper role of interior regularity within affine-constrained quadratic programming.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\leq h\}\) is nonempty, \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\), and \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is optimal if and only if it admits multipliers satisfying the affine-polyhedral KKT system; strict feasibility is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT characterization specialized to a convex QP over a polyhedron.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the polyhedral convex QP, \(\bar x\) is globally optimal if and only if there exist \(\nu\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[Q\bar x+q+A^\top\nu+G^\top\lambda=0,\qquad A\bar x=b,
\qquad G\bar x\leq h,\]
\[\lambda\geq0,
\qquad \lambda_i(G_i\bar x-h_i)=0\quad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}.\]
Existence of such a multiplier pair requires neither a strictly feasible point nor linear independence of the active constraint normals; those conditions can nevertheless affect multiplier uniqueness and stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible convex polyhedral QP, the KKT system is necessary and sufficient without Slater strict feasibility or active-normal independence.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral QP Specialization

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Relative-Interior versus Strict-Feasibility Routes
children.top_down_role: Scope differences between relative-interior and Slater-based certification.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x\in L:Gx\leq h\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron in an affine space \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict feasibility implies relative-interior feasibility, but the converse can fail when an inequality is implicit equality or redundant on \(C\).

notation.meaning: Relative interior of C in its affine hull.
Affine space containing the equality-feasible points.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of relative-interior and literal strict-inequality qualifications for polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If some \(x^0\in L\) satisfies \(Gx^0<h\), then \(x^0\in\operatorname{ri}C\); hence literal strict feasibility supplies a relative-interior route. The converse need not hold for the displayed inequality system. For example,
\[C=\{x\in\mathbb R:x\leq0,\ -x\leq0\}=\{0\}.\]
Here \(\operatorname{ri}C=\{0\}\), but no point makes both inequalities strict. Thus relative-interior regularity is representation-insensitive, whereas strict feasibility may be destroyed by encoding an implicit equality as opposing inequalities. For polyhedral QPs, exact normal-cone calculus can still yield KKT multipliers despite this failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict feasibility gives a relative-interior point, but relative-interior regularity can survive formulations where opposing or redundant inequalities make literal strict feasibility impossible.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior versus Strict-Feasibility Routes

children.title: LICQ Active-Rank Regularity
children.top_down_role: Rank regimes governing multiplier uniqueness and classical local sensitivity.

children.title: Linear Independence Constraint Qualification
children.top_down_role: Independence of active constraint normals at a candidate solution.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\leq h\}\), and \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: LICQ holds at \(\bar x\) exactly when the rows of \(A\) together with the rows of \(G_{I(\bar x)}\) are linearly independent.

notation.meaning: Matrix stacking equality and active inequality normals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: LICQ for affine equalities and inequalities at a feasible QP point.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Form the active-constraint matrix
\[M(\bar x)=\begin{bmatrix}A\\G_{I(\bar x)}\end{bmatrix}.\]
The linear independence constraint qualification holds at \(\bar x\) when
\[M(\bar x)^\top z=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad z=0.\]
Equivalently, the equality normals \(A_j^\top\) and active inequality normals \(G_i^\top\), for \(i\in I(\bar x)\), are jointly linearly independent, or \(\operatorname{rank}M(\bar x)\) equals the number of its rows. In particular, LICQ excludes redundant equality rows and active inequality normals dependent on the other active normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ holds when all equality normals and active inequality normals at the feasible point are jointly linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Independence Constraint Qualification

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Active-Constraint Rank
children.top_down_role: Rank structure of the active equality and inequality representation.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\leq h\}\), and \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active-constraint rank is \(r(\bar x)=\operatorname{rank}M(\bar x)\); LICQ is equivalent to \(r(\bar x)=p+|I(\bar x)|\).

notation.meaning: Active inequality index set at the feasible point.
Stacked equality and active inequality matrix.
Rank of the stacked active-constraint matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank statistic for the equality-active inequality system of a polyhedral QP.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\) have \(p\) rows and define
\[M(\bar x)=\begin{bmatrix}A\\G_{I(\bar x)}\end{bmatrix}.\]
The active-constraint rank at \(\bar x\) is
\[r(\bar x)=\operatorname{rank}M(\bar x).\]
It satisfies \(r(\bar x)\leq\min\{n,p+|I(\bar x)|\}\). The rank deficiency
\[p+|I(\bar x)|-r(\bar x)=\dim\ker M(\bar x)^\top\]
counts independent linear dependencies among equality and active inequality normals. Consequently, LICQ at \(\bar x\) is precisely the full-row-rank condition \(r(\bar x)=p+|I(\bar x)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-constraint rank is the rank of the stacked equality and active inequality normals; LICQ means this matrix has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Constraint Rank

children.title: Full-Rank Multiplier Geometry
children.top_down_role: Multiplier behavior associated with independent active normals.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Rank Multiplier Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of KKT multipliers for a convex QP under active-row LICQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex quadratic program \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\le b\) and \(Ex=d\), where \(Q\succeq0\). At a KKT point \(x^*\), let \(I=\{i:A_ix^*=b_i\}\). If the rows of \(G_I=\begin{bmatrix}E\\A_I\end{bmatrix}\) are linearly independent, then the stationarity equation \(Qx^*+c+E^Ty+A_I^T\lambda_I=0\) has at most one solution \((y,\lambda_I)\). Consequently, whenever KKT multipliers exist, the equality multiplier and all active inequality multipliers are unique; inactive multipliers equal zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear independence of equality and active-inequality rows makes the KKT multiplier vector unique whenever it exists.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and the constraints are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M(x^*)\) is a singleton.

notation.meaning: Active inequality index set at the KKT point.
Matrix formed from equality and active-inequality rows.
Set of KKT multipliers associated with the fixed primal point.

children.title: Rank-Sensitive Local Stability
children.top_down_role: Local sensitivity distinctions governed by active-system rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Sensitive Local Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-active-set stability under LICQ, curvature, and strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the parametrized QP with data \((c,b,d)\), fix a KKT solution with active set \(I\). If \(G_I=\begin{bmatrix}A_I\\E\end{bmatrix}\) has full row rank and \(z^TQz>0\) for every nonzero \(z\in\ker G_I\), then the active-set KKT matrix \(K_I=\begin{bmatrix}Q&A_I^T&E^T\\A_I&0&0\\E&0&0\end{bmatrix}\) is nonsingular. Hence the corresponding primal-dual solution depends affinely, and therefore locally Lipschitz continuously, on \((c,b_I,d)\). If active multipliers and inactive slacks are strictly positive, the same active set persists under sufficiently small perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full active rank and positive reduced curvature give a nonsingular KKT system; strict margins then preserve the active set locally.
assumptions_latex: Active multipliers and inactive slacks are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_I\) is nonsingular and the local primal-dual solution map is affine with unchanged active set.

notation.meaning: KKT matrix for the fixed active set.

children.top_down_role: Dependent active constraints and nonunique multiplier representations.

children.title: Constraint Redundancy
children.top_down_role: Repeated or implied active constraints within an affine representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Redundancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global redundancy of one affine inequality in a polyhedral QP feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d\}\). An inequality \(A_jx\le b_j\) is redundant relative to the remaining system if deleting it leaves the feasible set unchanged: \[P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_ix\le b_i\text{ for all }i\ne j,\ Ex=d\}.\] More generally, a collection \(R\) is redundant when deleting every row indexed by \(R\) leaves \(P\) unchanged. Redundancy concerns the feasible-set representation and does not require the redundant inequality to be inactive at every feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is redundant when removing it does not change the QP feasible set, even if it is active at some feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and the remaining constraints define a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting the redundant row or row collection preserves \(P\).

notation.meaning: Index set of constraints proposed for deletion.

children.title: Active-System Rank Deficiency
children.top_down_role: Linear dependence among active constraint normals.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-System Rank Deficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of LICQ for the equality and active-inequality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d\}\) and a feasible point \(x^*\), define \(I(x^*)=\{i:A_ix^*=b_i\}\) and \(G_I=\begin{bmatrix}E\\A_I\end{bmatrix}\). The active system is rank deficient precisely when \[\operatorname{rank}G_I<m_e+|I(x^*)|.\] Equivalently, there exists a nonzero coefficient vector \((u,v_I)\) such that \(E^Tu+A_I^Tv_I=0\). Thus the active equality and inequality normals admit a nontrivial linear dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active system is rank deficient exactly when the equality and active-inequality normals are linearly dependent.

notation.meaning: Active inequality indices at the feasible point.

children.title: Multiplier Multiplicity
children.top_down_role: Multiple dual representations associated with the same primal optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nullspace characterization of all multipliers associated with one primal KKT point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a KKT point \(x^*\) of the affine-constrained convex QP, let \(I=I(x^*)\). Its multiplier set is \[\mathcal M(x^*)=\{(y,\lambda_I):E^Ty+A_I^T\lambda_I=-(Qx^*+c),\ \lambda_I\ge0\}.\] If \((y^0,\lambda_I^0)\in\mathcal M(x^*)\), then \[\mathcal M(x^*)=\{(y^0+u,\lambda_I^0+v):E^Tu+A_I^Tv=0,\ \lambda_I^0+v\ge0\}.\] Thus all multipliers form the nonnegative-feasible part of an affine translate of \(\ker[\,E^T\ A_I^T\,]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All multipliers at a fixed primal point form the feasible part of an affine translate of the active-normal nullspace.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) is a KKT point of a convex QP with affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M(x^*)=(y^0,\lambda_I^0)+\ker[\,E^T\ A_I^T\,]\) intersected with \(\lambda_I\ge0\).

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set for the fixed primal point.

children.title: Redundancy-Induced Dual Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: How redundant active descriptions generate nonunique multiplier sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy-Induced Dual Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicated active inequalities demonstrate dual nonuniqueness despite a fixed primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\tfrac12(x-1)^2\) subject to the duplicated inequalities \(x\le0\) and \(x\le0\). The unique primal solution is \(x^*=0\). Stationarity and complementarity reduce to \(-1+\lambda_1+\lambda_2=0\) with \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\). Hence every pair \((\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\) satisfying \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1\) is a KKT multiplier vector. The primal solution is unique, but the multiplier vector is not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating an active inequality preserves the unique primal solution but permits infinitely many splits of its positive multiplier.
assumptions_latex: Both displayed inequalities are retained as distinct rows of the QP representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*=0\) is unique, whereas \(\{\lambda\ge0:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1\}\) is an infinite multiplier set.

notation.meaning: Multipliers of the two duplicated inequalities.

children.title: Complementarity-Active-Face Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relations among active constraints, multipliers, complementary faces, and degeneracy.

children.title: Complementary Active Faces
children.top_down_role: The face-level organization of primal activity and dual support.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Active Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-level correspondence between primal slacks and nonnegative dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a KKT pair \((x^*,y^*,\lambda^*)\) of \(Ax\le b\), set \(s^*=b-Ax^*\), \(I=\{i:s_i^*=0\}\), and \(J=\{i:\lambda_i^*>0\}\). Complementarity gives \(J\subseteq I\) and partitions the indices into positive-slack indices, positive-multiplier indices, and weakly active indices \(I\setminus J\). The primal face selected by the dual support is \[F_J=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d,\ A_jx=b_j\text{ for }j\in J\}.\] Thus positive dual support exposes primal equalities, while weak activity records the gap between the full active face at \(x^*\) and the face exposed by \(\lambda^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive multipliers select binding face equations; active constraints with zero multipliers measure the gap between activity and dual support.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,y^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J\subseteq I\) and \(x^*\in F_J\), with weakly active set \(I\setminus J\).

children.title: Strict Complementarity
children.top_down_role: Strictly separated primal-dual activity and its structural consequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise strict separation between inequality slack and multiplier support at a KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^*,y^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair for inequalities \(Ax\le b\), and let \(s^*=b-Ax^*\). Strict complementarity holds when \[s_i^*+\lambda_i^*>0\quad\text{for every inequality index }i.\] Because \(s_i^*\lambda_i^*=0\), this means exactly one of \(s_i^*\) and \(\lambda_i^*\) is positive for each \(i\). Equivalently, every active inequality has a positive multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity requires every inequality to have either positive slack or a positive multiplier, but not both.

notation.meaning: Slack of inequality i at the KKT point.

children.title: Weak-Activity Degeneracy Coupling
children.top_down_role: Zero multipliers, redundant activity, and nonunique active descriptions.

children.title: Weakly Active Constraints
children.top_down_role: Active inequalities carrying zero optimal multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Active Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active inequalities carrying zero multiplier at a specified KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a KKT pair \((x^*,y^*,\lambda^*)\) of a QP with inequalities \(Ax\le b\), an inequality index \(i\) is weakly active when \[A_ix^*=b_i\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_i^*=0.\] The weakly active set is \(W=\{i:A_ix^*=b_i,\ \lambda_i^*=0\}\). Its complement within the active set consists of strongly active indices \(S=\{i:A_ix^*=b_i,\ \lambda_i^*>0\}\). Both sets depend on the selected multiplier when multipliers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly active inequality is binding at the primal point but has zero multiplier at the selected KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(x^*)=S\mathbin{\dot\cup}W\).

children.title: Primal Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Nonunique or redundant active descriptions on the primal side.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-normal convention for primal degeneracy at a feasible QP point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the polyhedral feasible set \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d\}\), a feasible point \(x^*\) is primal degenerate, in the active-normal sense used here, when the equality rows together with all active inequality rows are linearly dependent: \[\operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}E\\A_{I(x^*)}\end{bmatrix}<m_e+|I(x^*)|.\] This condition depends only on the primal feasible representation and point, not on a chosen KKT multiplier. Duplicated or otherwise redundant active inequalities are a common mechanism producing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal degeneracy means the equality and active-inequality normals are linearly dependent at the feasible point.

children.title: Dual Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Nonunique multiplier representations or loss of strict complementarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-activity convention for dual degeneracy of a specified KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A KKT pair \((x^*,y^*,\lambda^*)\) is dual degenerate, in the complementarity convention used here, when at least one active inequality has zero multiplier: \[\exists i\quad A_ix^*=b_i\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_i^*=0.\] Equivalently, the positive multiplier support is a proper subset of the active inequality set. This notion is multiplier-dependent when the multiplier set is not a singleton and is distinct from multiplier nonuniqueness itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual degeneracy occurs when the selected KKT multiplier vanishes on at least one binding inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{i:\lambda_i^*>0\}\subsetneq I(x^*)\).

children.title: Weak-Activity Degeneracy Link
children.top_down_role: How zero-multiplier activity interacts with primal-dual degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Activity Degeneracy Link
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak activity simultaneously characterizes strict-complementarity failure and enlarges the critical cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a KKT pair, partition the active inequalities into \(S=\{i:\lambda_i^*>0\}\) and \(W=\{i:A_ix^*=b_i,\ \lambda_i^*=0\}\). Then strict complementarity fails exactly when \(W\ne\varnothing\). For the affine-constrained QP, the critical cone at this pair is \[\mathcal C=\{z:Ez=0,\ A_iz=0\text{ for }i\in S,\ A_iz\le0\text{ for }i\in W\}.\] Thus strongly active constraints act as local equalities in critical directions, whereas weakly active constraints retain one-sided freedom; this is the geometric link between weak activity and complementarity degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak activity exactly marks failure of strict complementarity and gives one-sided, rather than equality, restrictions in the critical cone.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,y^*,\lambda^*)\) is a KKT pair for a QP with affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W\ne\varnothing\iff\) strict complementarity fails, and \(W\) enters \(\mathcal C\) through inequalities.

notation.meaning: Critical cone at the selected KKT pair.

children.title: Second-Order Stability Condition Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Curvature refinements beyond basic convex KKT sufficiency.

children.title: Critical-Cone Second-Order Conditions
children.top_down_role: Second-order necessity and sufficiency organized on the critical cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Second-Order Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral quadratic program; necessity and strict critical-cone sufficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\). If \(x^*\) is a local minimizer, define \(C(x^*)=\{d\in T_P(x^*):\nabla f(x^*)^{\mathsf T}d=0\}\). Then \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd\ge0\) for every \(d\in C(x^*)\). Conversely, if \(x^*\) is feasible, \(\nabla f(x^*)^{\mathsf T}(x-x^*)\ge0\) for every \(x\in P\), and \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in C(x^*)\), then \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer and satisfies local quadratic growth on \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature is nonnegative along every critical direction at a local minimizer; strict positivity on all nonzero critical directions yields strict local optimality and quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd\ge0\) is necessary on \(C(x^*)\), while strict positivity there is sufficient for quadratic growth.

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone of the feasible polyhedron at the candidate point
critical cone at the candidate point
symmetric Hessian of the quadratic objective

children.title: Quadratic-Growth Isolation Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Growth and isolation regimes for locally stable optimal solutions.

children.title: Quadratic Growth
children.top_down_role: Local objective growth relative to distance from an optimal solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic growth relative to the QP feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible point \(x^*\in P\) satisfies local quadratic growth for \(f\) on \(P\) if there exist constants \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\) such that \[f(x)\ge f(x^*)+\alpha\lVert x-x^*\rVert^2\qquad\text{for every }x\in P\cap B_r(x^*).\] The constant \(\alpha\) is a local growth modulus; its normalization is conventional and may equivalently be written with the factor \(\tfrac12\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective values near the feasible minimizer exceed the minimum by at least a positive constant times squared distance from that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f(x^*)\ge\alpha\lVert x-x^*\rVert^2\) locally on \(P\).

notation.meaning: open Euclidean ball of radius r centered at the candidate point

children.title: Isolated Minimizers
children.top_down_role: Optimal solutions separated locally from other minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isolation among feasible minimizers, without an asserted growth rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a function \(f:P\to\mathbb R\), a point \(x^*\in P\) is an isolated local minimizer if there exists \(r>0\) such that \[f(x)>f(x^*)\qquad\text{for every }x\in(P\cap B_r(x^*))\setminus\{x^*\}.\] Equivalently, \(x^*\) is the unique minimizer of \(f\) over \(P\cap B_r(x^*)\) for some sufficiently small radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isolated minimizer is the only feasible minimizer in some neighborhood, although no quantitative rate of objective increase is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is the unique minimizer in \(P\cap B_r(x^*)\) for some \(r>0\).

notation.meaning: open Euclidean neighborhood of the candidate point

children.title: Growth-Induced Isolation
children.top_down_role: The connection between positive local growth and solution isolation.

knowledge_statements.title: Growth-Induced Isolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct isolation consequence of a positive local growth modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x^*\in P\) and there exist \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\) satisfying \(f(x)\ge f(x^*)+\alpha\lVert x-x^*\rVert^2\) for every \(x\in P\cap B_r(x^*)\). Then every feasible \(x\ne x^*\) in that ball satisfies \(f(x)>f(x^*)\). Hence \(x^*\) is an isolated local minimizer; indeed it is the unique minimizer over \(P\cap B_r(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any positive quadratic-growth bound forces strict objective increase at every distinct nearby feasible point, so the minimizer is isolated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is an isolated local minimizer of \(f\) on \(P\).

notation.meaning: radius on which the growth estimate holds

children.title: Isolation without Uniform Growth
children.top_down_role: Boundary regimes where isolation does not carry the strongest growth behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolation without Uniform Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A family showing that isolation does not provide a common growth modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(\varepsilon>0\), consider the unconstrained convex quadratic \(f_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\). The point \(x^*=0\) is the unique, hence isolated, global minimizer and has individual growth modulus \(\varepsilon\). Nevertheless, the family admits no constants \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\), independent of \(\varepsilon\), such that \(f_\varepsilon(x)\ge f_\varepsilon(0)+\alpha|x|^2\) for all \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(|x|<r\). Thus isolation alone supplies no uniform quadratic-growth modulus across a QP family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each scaled quadratic has an isolated minimizer, but as curvature tends to zero no positive quadratic-growth modulus works uniformly across the family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No \(\alpha>0\) is a quadratic-growth modulus uniformly for all \(\varepsilon>0\).

notation.meaning: positive curvature parameter tending toward zero

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The parameterized quadratic family is mathematically valid and the failure_boundary content kind fits the leaf, but the record supplies neither a source nor an explicit standard-field rationale. Source support is required for this nontrivial family-level boundary claim.

children.title: Flat-Direction Nonisolation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of isolated growth under singular reduced curvature.

children.title: Feasible Flat Directions
children.top_down_role: Feasible directions exhibiting zero relevant quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in C(x^*)\setminus\{0\}\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\).

notation.meaning: tangent cone of the feasible polyhedron
critical cone at the feasible point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical feasible directions carrying zero quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedral, and let \(x^*\in P\). Define the critical cone by \(C(x^*)=\{v\in T_P(x^*):\nabla f(x^*)^{\mathsf T}v=0\}\). A feasible flat direction at \(x^*\) is a nonzero vector \(d\in C(x^*)\) satisfying \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\). Thus both the first-order objective change and the quadratic curvature vanish along \(d\). If \(Q\succeq0\), the equality \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\) is equivalent to \(Qd=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible flat direction is a nonzero critical tangent direction with zero first-order objective change and zero quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Flat Directions

children.title: Nonisolated Optimal Sets
children.top_down_role: Optimal sets containing locally adjacent distinct solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonisolated Optimal Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity of the solution set and its segment consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex on a convex feasible set \(P\), and let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x)\). Then \(S\) is convex. Consequently, if distinct points \(x^0,x^1\in S\) exist, every point \((1-t)x^0+tx^1\) with \(t\in[0,1]\) also belongs to \(S\). No point in the relative interior of this optimal segment is isolated in \(S\); in particular, either a convex QP has a singleton solution set or any nontrivial optimal segment consists of nonisolated minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimizer set of a convex QP is convex; two distinct solutions generate an entire optimal segment and therefore nonisolated solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is convex, and distinct minimizers generate a nontrivial optimal segment.

notation.meaning: set of global minimizers over the feasible set
convex-combination parameter in the unit interval

children.title: Singular Reduced Curvature
children.top_down_role: Loss of strict curvature on the feasible or critical subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Reduced Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singularity of the Hessian restricted to equality-feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the equality-constrained quadratic program with \(Ax=b\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank. Let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). The reduced curvature is singular precisely when \[\det(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ)=0,\] equivalently when there exists \(p\ne0\) such that \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZp=0\). If \(Q\succeq0\), this is further equivalent to the existence of a nonzero equality-feasible direction \(d=Zp\) satisfying \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced curvature is singular when the Hessian restricted to the null space of the equality constraints has a nonzero null direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\) is singular exactly when it has a nonzero null vector.

notation.meaning: null-space basis matrix for the equality constraints
reduced Hessian or reduced curvature matrix
coordinates of an equality-feasible direction in the null-space basis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The singularity equivalences are mathematically correct, including the additional positive-semidefinite equivalence, and condition is appropriate for the leaf. However, the record has no citation or explicit standard-field rationale, so its reduced-Hessian formulation cannot pass the evidence requirement.

children.title: Flatness-Induced Nonisolation
children.top_down_role: How feasible zero-curvature directions create extended optimal sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Flatness-Induced Nonisolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact objective constancy along a locally feasible flat ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succeq0\), let \(P\) be polyhedral, and let \(x^*\) minimize \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(P\). If a nonzero \(d\in T_P(x^*)\) satisfies \(\nabla f(x^*)^{\mathsf T}d=0\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\), then some \(\delta>0\) satisfies \(x^*+td\in P\) and \[f(x^*+td)=f(x^*)\qquad\text{for every }t\in[0,\delta].\] Hence the optimal set contains a nontrivial segment issuing from \(x^*\), so \(x^*\) is not isolated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero feasible critical direction with zero curvature produces a local segment of equally optimal points, preventing isolation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x^*+td:0\le t\le\delta\}\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x)\), so \(x^*\) is nonisolated.

notation.meaning: positive length of a locally feasible optimal segment
tangent cone of the polyhedral feasible set

children.title: KKT-System Representations
children.top_down_role: Algebraic organizations of the KKT system retained here as representations rather than solver procedures.

children.title: Equality-Constrained Saddle-Point System
children.top_down_role: The coupled primal-multiplier representation for equality-constrained QP.

children.title: Full-Space KKT Representation
children.top_down_role: The unreduced primal-multiplier block representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space KKT Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unreduced primal-multiplier system for an equality-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\qquad\text{subject to }Ax=b,\] stationarity and feasibility are represented jointly by \[\begin{pmatrix}Q&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-c\\b\end{pmatrix}.\] Here \(y\) is the equality multiplier. If \(A\) has full row rank and \(Q\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), the KKT matrix is nonsingular and the displayed system has a unique primal-multiplier solution; its primal component is the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality-constrained QP optimality conditions form one symmetric saddle-point linear system in the primal variables and equality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full-space KKT system is nonsingular and determines the unique primal-multiplier pair.

notation.meaning: multiplier vector for the equality constraints

children.title: Range-Space Schur-Complement Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: The multiplier-space reduction of the equality KKT system.

children.title: Range-Space Reduction
children.top_down_role: Equality-constrained KKT structure reduced to multiplier space.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned pair \((x,y)\) solves the equality-constrained KKT system.

notation.meaning: matrix satisfying QW equals transpose A

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination of the primal variable into multiplier space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) with \(Q\succ0\), a full-row-rank matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and data \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), solve \(QW=A^{\mathsf T}\) and \(Qz=c\), and set \(S=AW=AQ^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). Solve \[Sy=-b-Az,\] recover \(x=-z-Wy\), and return \((x,y)\). The matrices \(Q\) and \(S\) are positive definite, and the returned pair satisfies \(Qx+A^{\mathsf T}y=-c\) and \(Ax=b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use solves with the positive-definite Hessian to form the multiplier-space Schur complement, solve the multiplier system, and recover the primal solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Reduction

children.title: Schur-Complement Representation
children.top_down_role: Condensed saddle-point structure expressed through a Schur complement.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block inverse representation using the multiplier-space Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succ0\), let \(A\) have full row rank, and define \(S=AQ^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(S\succ0\), and the KKT inverse is \[\begin{pmatrix}Q&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}Q^{-1}-Q^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S^{-1}AQ^{-1}&Q^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S^{-1}\\S^{-1}AQ^{-1}&-S^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.\] Equivalently, for right-hand side \((-c,b)\), the multiplier satisfies \(Sy=-b-AQ^{-1}c\), after which \(x=-Q^{-1}(c+A^{\mathsf T}y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KKT inverse and solution can be expressed through the positive-definite multiplier-space Schur complement and primal recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed block inverse and the equivalent Schur-complement solution formulas hold.

children.title: Multiplier-Space Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Numerical conditioning features of the condensed dual system.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Space Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning of the range-space Schur complement for positive-definite equality-constrained QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. The multiplier Schur complement \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) is symmetric positive definite and satisfies
\[
\frac{\sigma_{\min}(A)^2}{\lambda_{\max}(H)}\leq \lambda_{\min}(S)\leq \lambda_{\max}(S)\leq \frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)^2}{\lambda_{\min}(H)}.
\]
Consequently, in the Euclidean norm,
\[
\kappa_2(S)\leq \kappa_2(H)\,\kappa_2(A)^2,
\]
where the condition number of the full-row-rank rectangular matrix uses its nonzero singular values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier conditioning deteriorates with both Hessian conditioning and the squared conditioning of the constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\succ0\) and \(\kappa_2(S)\leq\kappa_2(H)\kappa_2(A)^2\).

notation.meaning: Smallest and largest nonzero singular values of A.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

children.title: Schur-Complement Singularity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Rank or curvature regimes limiting the condensed representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Singularity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and representative failure boundaries for the classical range-space Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(H\succ0\), then \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) is singular exactly when \(A\) lacks full row rank, because \(y^{\mathsf T}Sy=(A^{\mathsf T}y)^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}(A^{\mathsf T}y)\). If \(H\) is singular, the classical expression using \(H^{-1}\) is undefined and requires a generalized-inverse formulation with range compatibility. If positive definiteness is weakened to invertible indefiniteness, full row rank of \(A\) no longer prevents singularity: for \(H=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\) and \(A=(1,1)\), one has \(AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive-definite curvature, singularity is exactly constraint-rank failure; singular or indefinite curvature introduces additional breakdown mechanisms.
assumptions_latex: \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) is interpreted classically only when \(H\) is invertible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(H\succ0\), \(S\) is nonsingular if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\); this equivalence can fail for indefinite \(H\).

notation.meaning: Number of equality constraints, or rows of A.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

children.title: Null-Space Reduced-Hessian Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: The feasible-subspace reduction exposing reduced curvature.

children.title: Null-Space Reduction
children.top_down_role: Equality-constrained optimization represented in feasible null-space coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination of equality constraints through coordinates on the feasible affine subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where the constraint is consistent. Choose \(x_p\) with \(Ax_p=b\) and a full-column-rank matrix \(Z\) satisfying \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\). Every feasible point is uniquely representable as \(x=x_p+Zp\). After discarding constants, the problem becomes
\[
\min_p\;\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)p+p^{\mathsf T}Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+c),
\]
and its stationarity equation is \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZp=-Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible particular point plus null-space coordinates converts the equality-constrained QP into an unconstrained reduced QP.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original feasible QP is equivalent to the displayed unconstrained problem in \(p\).

notation.meaning: A basis matrix for the null space of A.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible null-space reduction and reduced-Hessian criterion for equality-constrained quadratics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space coordinates for equality-constrained quadratic problems, including the distinction between global optimality and uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), suppose \(Ax=b\) is consistent, choose \(x^F\) with \(Ax^F=b\), and let \(N\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(N)=\ker A\). Then every feasible point has the unique representation \(x=x^F+Nz\). For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^THx-g^Tx\), where \(H=H^T\), the reduced stationarity equation is \(N^THNz=N^T(g-Hx^F)\). If \(N^THN\succeq0\), every KKT point is a global minimizer; if \(N^THN\succ0\), the primal minimizer exists and is unique. In particular, when \(H\succ0\) and \(g=Hx_0\), this reduction yields the unique \(H\)-norm projection of \(x_0\) onto \(\{x:Ax=b\}\). If \(A\) has full row rank and \(A=[A^R\;A^N]P^T\) with nonsingular \(A^R\), then \(P\binom{-(A^R)^{-1}A^N}{I}\) is a fundamental null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible point is uniquely a feasible anchor plus a null-space displacement. Substitution gives a reduced quadratic whose Hessian is the reduced Hessian. Positive semidefiniteness makes any KKT point globally minimizing, while positive definiteness gives a unique primal minimizer. A nonsingular coordinate partition supplies a fundamental null-space basis.
assumptions_latex: N\text{ has full column rank and }\operatorname{range}(N)=\ker A
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x=x^F+Nz,\qquad N^THNz=N^T(g-Hx^F),\qquad N^THN\succeq0\Rightarrow\text{every KKT point is globally minimizing},\qquad N^THN\succ0\Rightarrow\text{the primal minimizer is unique}.

children.title: Reduced-Hessian Representation
children.top_down_role: Quadratic curvature expressed on the equality-feasible subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix representation of quadratic curvature restricted to equality-feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). The reduced Hessian is
\[
H_R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ.
\]
For every feasible direction \(d\in\ker A\), there is a unique \(p\in\mathbb R^r\) with \(d=Zp\), and
\[
d^{\mathsf T}Hd=p^{\mathsf T}H_Rp.
\]
Thus \(H_R\) represents precisely the restriction of the quadratic form induced by \(H\) to the feasible-direction subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced Hessian is the coordinate matrix of the Hessian quadratic form restricted to feasible directions.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\) and \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(d=Zp\), \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd=p^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)p\).

notation.meaning: Dimension of the null space of A.

children.title: Feasible-Subspace Curvature
children.top_down_role: Definiteness and singularity of the quadratic form after null-space restriction.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Subspace Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive curvature condition on equality-feasible directions and its reduced-Hessian equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a symmetric Hessian \(H\) and equality matrix \(A\), positive feasible-subspace curvature means
\[
d^{\mathsf T}Hd>0\qquad\text{for every }d\in\ker A\setminus\{0\}.
\]
If the columns of \(Z\) form any basis of \(\ker A\), this condition is equivalent to \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\). Under this condition, the quadratic objective is strictly convex on every nonempty affine feasible set \(\{x:Ax=b\}\); hence an equality-constrained stationary point, when it exists, is the unique global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive curvature is needed only along feasible directions; equivalently, the reduced Hessian is positive definite.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a basis matrix for \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd>0\) for all nonzero \(d\in\ker A\) if and only if \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\).

children.title: Null-Space Basis Dependence
children.top_down_role: Coordinate choices affecting representation while preserving intrinsic reduced curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Basis Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate dependence and invariant features of the reduced Hessian under null-space basis changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\) and \(\widehat Z\) be full-column-rank bases of the same null space. Then \(\widehat Z=ZT\) for some invertible matrix \(T\), and their reduced Hessians satisfy
\[
\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}H\widehat Z=T^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)T.
\]
Consequently, rank, inertia, and positive definiteness are independent of the chosen basis, whereas eigenvalues and spectral condition numbers generally are not. If both bases have orthonormal columns, \(T\) is orthogonal, so the two reduced Hessians are orthogonally similar and have identical eigenvalues and spectral condition numbers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing null-space coordinates gives a congruent reduced Hessian; inertia is invariant, while conditioning is basis-dependent unless both bases are orthonormal.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\operatorname{range}(\widehat Z)\), with both matrices full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat H_R=T^{\mathsf T}H_RT\); inertia is invariant, but spectral conditioning need not be.

notation.meaning: Reduced Hessians in the two bases.

children.title: Active-Face Equality Reduction
children.top_down_role: The equality-constrained system induced by a selected active face.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Face Equality Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT reduction obtained by fixing a candidate active inequality face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the convex QP with \(H\succeq0\), equalities \(Ax=b\), and inequalities \(Gx\leq h\). For a candidate active set \(I\), replace \(G_Ix\leq h_I\) by \(G_Ix=h_I\) and solve
\[
Hx+c+A^{\mathsf T}\nu+G_I^{\mathsf T}\mu_I=0,\qquad Ax=b,\qquad G_Ix=h_I.
\]
The resulting point satisfies the full KKT system exactly when \(G_{I^c}x\leq h_{I^c}\) and \(\mu_I\geq0\), with \(\mu_{I^c}=0\). Under a constraint qualification, these conditions certify global optimality of the convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected active face yields an equality-constrained KKT system; inactive feasibility and nonnegative active multipliers validate the selection.
assumptions_latex: A KKT constraint qualification holds at the candidate point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The face-reduced solution is a full KKT point precisely when \(G_{I^c}x\leq h_{I^c}\) and \(\mu_I\geq0\).

notation.meaning: Multipliers of the selected active inequalities.

children.title: Primal-Dual Slack Representation

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Slack Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint KKT representation in primal variables, inequality slacks, and dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the convex QP
\[
\min_x\;\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx\leq h,
\]
introduce \(s=h-Gx\). Its primal-dual slack KKT system is
\[
Hx+c+A^{\mathsf T}\nu+G^{\mathsf T}\mu=0,\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx+s=h,
\]
\[
s\geq0,\quad \mu\geq0,\quad S\mu=0,
\]
where \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\). Under a KKT constraint qualification, solutions of this system are exactly the primal-dual optimal solutions; primal-dual interior methods replace \(S\mu=0\) by \(S\mu=\tau\mathbf1\) for \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KKT conditions combine stationarity, primal feasibility, nonnegative slacks and multipliers, and componentwise complementarity.
assumptions_latex: The affine-constrained QP satisfies a KKT constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal-dual optimality is represented by stationarity, feasibility, \(s\geq0\), \(\mu\geq0\), and \(S\mu=0\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix formed from the slack vector.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Complementarity Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LCP obtained by eliminating primal variables when the Hessian is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_x\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Gx\leq h\), with \(H\succ0\). Stationarity gives \(x=-H^{-1}(c+G^{\mathsf T}\mu)\). Substitution into \(s=h-Gx\) yields
\[
s=q+M\mu,\qquad q=h+GH^{-1}c,\qquad M=GH^{-1}G^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Hence the QP KKT system is equivalent to the monotone linear complementarity problem
\[
0\leq\mu\perp q+M\mu\geq0.
\]
Here \(M\succeq0\); after solving the LCP, the unique primal point is recovered from the stationarity formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite curvature permits primal elimination, producing a monotone LCP in the inequality multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The QP has only inequalities \(Gx\leq h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The QP KKT system is equivalent to \(0\leq\mu\perp q+M\mu\geq0\), with \(M=GH^{-1}G^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: LCP matrix obtained after primal elimination.
Componentwise complementarity: both vectors are nonnegative and their inner product is zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual representations of a positive-definite linearly constrained QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality multipliers are unrestricted and inequality multipliers are nonnegative. The multiplier-only minimization has the same optimizers as the dual maximization because their objectives differ by sign and a multiplier-independent constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q(x)=\tfrac12x^TGx+g^Tx with G\succ0, and consider \min Q(x) subject to a_i^Tx=b_i for i\in E and a_i^Tx\ge b_i for i\in I. With A=[a_1,\ldots,a_m] and y=A\lambda-g, the dual is \max_{\lambda,y}\{b^T\lambda-\tfrac12y^TG^{-1}y:A\lambda-y=g,\ \lambda_i\ge0\ (i\in I)\}. Equivalently, it maximizes L(x,\lambda)=\tfrac12x^TGx+g^Tx-\lambda^T(A^Tx-b) subject to \nabla_xL(x,\lambda)=0 and \lambda_i\ge0 for i\in I. Eliminating y yields the optimizer-equivalent problem \min_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}\{\tfrac12\lambda^TA^TG^{-1}A\lambda-(b+A^TG^{-1}g)^T\lambda:\lambda_i\ge0\ (i\in I)\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearly constrained quadratic program with positive-definite Hessian has an equality-lifted concave quadratic dual. The same dual is obtained from Lagrangian stationarity, and eliminating the auxiliary variable gives an optimizer-equivalent convex quadratic program in the multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmax}_{\substack{A\lambda-y=g\\\lambda_i\ge0,\ i\in I}}\left(b^T\lambda-\tfrac12y^TG^{-1}y\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\substack{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\\\lambda_i\ge0,\ i\in I}}\left(\tfrac12\lambda^TA^TG^{-1}A\lambda-(b+A^TG^{-1}g)^T\lambda\right).
knowledge_statements.title: Dual representations of a positive-definite linearly constrained QP

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Unboundedness Forces Dual Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A consequence of weak duality for the stated primal and stationary Lagrangian dual pair, assuming finite Lagrangian values at feasible dual points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak duality implies \[\inf_{x'\in\mathcal F_P}f(x')\ge\sup_{(x,\lambda)\in\mathcal F_D}\mathcal L(x,\lambda).\] If \(\inf_{x'\in\mathcal F_P}f(x')=-\infty\) and \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)\in\mathbb R\) at every dual-feasible point, then \(\mathcal F_D=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the primal is unbounded below and every feasible dual point would have a finite Lagrangian value, weak duality implies that the dual has no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F_D=\varnothing
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Unboundedness Forces Dual Infeasibility

directory_assessment.rationale: The result is a general duality-status implication, while Convex QP Duality is only a legitimate specialization. No supplied candidate is a safe primary home; an A08 weak-duality and feasibility-status container should be considered with independent confirmation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian inertia, dual function, and saddle characterization for convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality multipliers are unrestricted and inequality multipliers belong to the nonnegative orthant. The proof details in the extract are omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \mathcal L(x,\lambda)=Q(x)-\lambda^T(A^Tx-b) with G\succ0, \nabla^2\mathcal L=\begin{bmatrix}G&-A\\-A^T&0\end{bmatrix} is congruent to \operatorname{diag}(G,-A^TG^{-1}A), hence has n positive, \operatorname{rank}(A) negative, and m-\operatorname{rank}(A) zero eigenvalues. Moreover, for \Lambda=\{\lambda:\lambda_i\ge0\ (i\in I)\}, \max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=Q(x) for every primal-feasible x, while \min_x\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=b^T\lambda-\tfrac12(A\lambda-g)^TG^{-1}(A\lambda-g). A primal KKT solution and its multiplier form a Lagrangian saddle point, and conversely any such saddle pair has a primal-optimal x-component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The QP Lagrangian Hessian is congruent to a positive primal block and a negative-semidefinite Schur-complement block, which determines its inertia. Maximizing the Lagrangian over admissible multipliers recovers the objective at every feasible primal point, while minimizing over the primal variable gives the quadratic dual function. Primal KKT solutions are saddle points, and saddle points recover primal minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{inertia}(\nabla^2\mathcal L)=\bigl(n,\operatorname{rank}(A),m-\operatorname{rank}(A)\bigr),\quad \max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=Q(x)\ (x\in X),\quad \inf_x\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=b^T\lambda-\tfrac12(A\lambda-g)^TG^{-1}(A\lambda-g).
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian inertia, dual function, and saddle characterization for convex QP

directory_assessment.rationale: The QP-specific result belongs primarily under convex-QP duality; the general Lagrangian saddle-model node is a legitimate cross-index, not a second primary home. The proposed container requires independent structural review.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal infeasibility is equivalent to dual unboundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The equivalence is specific to the displayed linearly constrained QP and its dual under positive-definite curvature; it is not asserted for arbitrary primal-dual pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G\succ0. For the primal problem \min\{\tfrac12x^TGx+g^Tx:a_i^Tx=b_i\ (i\in E),\ a_i^Tx\ge b_i\ (i\in I)\} and its dual \max\{b^T\lambda-\tfrac12y^TG^{-1}y:A\lambda-y=g,\ \lambda_i\ge0\ (i\in I)\}, the primal is infeasible if and only if the dual is unbounded above.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For this linearly constrained quadratic program with positive-definite Hessian, the primal feasible set is empty exactly when the associated concave quadratic dual is unbounded above.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:a_i^Tx=b_i\ (i\in E),\ a_i^Tx\ge b_i\ (i\in I)\}=\varnothing\iff\sup_{\substack{A\lambda-y=g\\\lambda_i\ge0,\ i\in I}}\left(b^T\lambda-\tfrac12y^TG^{-1}y\right)=+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal infeasibility is equivalent to dual unboundedness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal and Dual Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminology within a specified primal–dual construction; the extract does not define a particular dual construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Within a specified primal\text{--}dual construction, the original mathematical-programming problem is called the \emph{primal problem}, and its associated alternative formulation is called the \emph{dual problem}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within a specified primal–dual construction, the original mathematical-programming problem is called the primal problem and its associated alternative formulation is called the dual problem.
assumptions_latex: \text{A specified construction associates an alternative formulation with the original problem.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The original problem is primal, and the associated formulation is dual.}
knowledge_statements.title: Primal and Dual Problems

A general A08 container should be considered independently, while Convex QP Duality remains a legitimate specialization rather than a competing primary home.

children.title: Convex QP Dual Problem
children.top_down_role: The principal dual construction and its distinct explicit and singular-curvature representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual active-set algorithm for an inequality-constrained strictly convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration, stopping condition, working-set changes, and infeasibility test for the inequality-only case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x g^Tx+\tfrac12x^TGx\) subject to \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\), initialize \(x_1=-G^{-1}g\), \(\mathcal S_1=\varnothing\), and an empty multiplier vector. At iteration \(k\), set \(r_i=b_i-a_i^Tx_k\). If \(r_i\le0\) for all \(i\), stop. Otherwise choose \(p\in\arg\max_i r_i\), let \(A_k^*=(A_k^TG^{-1}A_k)^{-1}A_k^TG^{-1}\), \(d_k=G^{-1}(I-A_kA_k^*)a_p\), and \(y_k=A_k^*a_p\). Define the dual blocking step \(\alpha_k^{\rm dual}=\min_{j\in\mathcal S_k:(y_k)_j>0}(\bar\lambda_k)_j/(y_k)_j\), with value \(+\infty\) if the index set is empty. If \(d_k=0\), declare primal infeasibility when \(\alpha_k^{\rm dual}=+\infty\); otherwise take the blocking step, drop its attaining index, update the factors, and recompute the direction. If \(d_k\ne0\), define \(\widehat\alpha_k=-r_p/(a_p^Td_k)\), take \(\alpha_k=\min\{\alpha_k^{\rm dual},\widehat\alpha_k\}\), and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) and \(\bar\lambda_{k+1}=\bar\lambda_k+\alpha_k(-y_k,1)^T\). Add \(p\) to the working set when \(\alpha_k=\widehat\alpha_k\); when \(\alpha_k<\widehat\alpha_k\), drop the blocking index and continue with the same violated constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from the unconstrained minimizer and an empty working set. If every inequality is satisfied, terminate. Otherwise select a maximally violated constraint, compute its primal projected direction and the associated dual direction, and cap the step by the first existing multiplier that would reach zero. A full primal step adds the violated constraint; a blocking dual step drops the blocking constraint and recomputes the direction. If the projected direction is zero and no finite dual blocking step exists, terminate with an infeasibility declaration.
assumptions_latex: A_k^TG^{-1}A_k\text{ is nonsingular whenever }A_k^*\text{ is formed}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall i,\ r_i\le0\bigr)\Rightarrow\text{termination at a feasible QP solution};\qquad d_k=0\ \wedge\ \alpha_k^{\rm dual}=+\infty\Rightarrow\text{the original QP is infeasible.}
knowledge_statements.title: Dual active-set algorithm for an inequality-constrained strictly convex QP

directory_assessment.rationale: The listed hierarchy provides the convex-QP dual representation but no precise container for its dual active-set solver. Adding a reviewed method child would separate the algorithm from duality theory; this extraction-grounded proposal should be independently confirmed before structural adoption.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonnegative-Orthant Dual Representation of a Strictly Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual quadratic representation, its equivalent convex minimization over nonnegative multipliers, and the computational regime in which bound-constrained gradient projection is attractive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the source's inequality-sign convention, a strictly convex quadratic program with G=G^T\succ0 has the dual representation
\[
\max_{\lambda\ge0}\ \widetilde q(\lambda),\qquad
\widetilde q(\lambda)=-\tfrac12(A^T\lambda-c)^TG^{-1}(A^T\lambda-c)+b^T\lambda.
\]
Equivalently, one may solve \(\min_{\lambda\ge0}-\widetilde q(\lambda)\), whose objective is convex. This nonnegative-orthant problem is amenable to bound-constrained gradient projection and is particularly attractive when operations with \(G^{-1}\) are inexpensive, as when \(G\) is diagonal or block diagonal. By contrast, direct projection onto a general linearly constrained feasible set can require an auxiliary QP whose cost approaches that of the original QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the source's constraint-sign convention, the dual of a strictly convex quadratic program is a concave quadratic maximization over nonnegative multipliers. Negating its objective gives an equivalent convex minimization over the nonnegative orthant, to which bound-constrained gradient projection can be applied. This is most attractive when the inverse-Hessian operations are simple, such as for diagonal or block-diagonal Hessians. Direct projection onto general linear constraints can instead cost nearly as much as solving the original QP.
assumptions_latex: \text{The primal constraint convention induces the dual domain }\lambda\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{\lambda\ge0}\widetilde q(\lambda)\ \equiv\ \min_{\lambda\ge0}-\widetilde q(\lambda),\qquad -\widetilde q\text{ is convex and the feasible set is the nonnegative orthant.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual working-set correspondence and infeasibility certificate for strictly convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit dual representation, primal recovery, working-set KKT correspondence, multiplier-feasibility test, and infeasibility boundary for a strictly convex QP with affine equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[a_i]_{i\in E\cup I}\) and consider \(\min_x g^Tx+\tfrac12x^TGx\) subject to \(a_i^Tx=b_i\) for \(i\in E\) and \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\) for \(i\in I\), where \(G=G^T\succ0\). An equivalent dual minimization is \[\min_\lambda\ \tfrac12\lambda^TA^TG^{-1}A\lambda-(b+A^TG^{-1}g)^T\lambda,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0\ (i\in I),\] with \(\lambda_i\) free for \(i\in E\). Given \(\bar{\mathcal S}_k\subseteq I\), fix \(\lambda_i=0\) for \(i\in\bar{\mathcal S}_k\). If \(\lambda_k\) is a KKT point of this equality-constrained dual subproblem, then \(x_k=-G^{-1}(g-A\lambda_k)\) satisfies \(a_i^Tx_k=b_i\) for every \(i\in\mathcal S_k=(E\cup I)\setminus\bar{\mathcal S}_k\). If additionally \(\lambda_{k,i}\ge0\) for \(i\in I\cap\mathcal S_k\) and \(a_i^Tx_k-b_i\ge0\) for \(i\in\bar{\mathcal S}_k\), then \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) satisfies the KKT conditions of the original QP. When \(A_k^TG^{-1}A_k\) is nonsingular, define \(A_k^*=(A_k^TG^{-1}A_k)^{-1}A_k^TG^{-1}\). Adding an index \(p\) produces \(d_k=G^{-1}(I-A_kA_k^*)a_p\) and the dual direction \((-y_k,1)\), where \(y_k=A_k^*a_p\); multiplier nonnegativity requires \[0\le\beta_k\le\min_{j:(y_k)_j>0}\frac{(\bar\lambda_k)_j}{(y_k)_j}.\] If \(d_k=0\), \(y_k\le0\), and \(b_p-a_p^Tx_k>0\), the dual minimization is unbounded below and the primal QP is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite QP has an explicit dual with free equality multipliers and nonnegative inequality multipliers. Fixing selected inequality multipliers at zero corresponds to imposing the complementary constraints as equalities in a primal working-set subproblem. Dual multiplier feasibility and nonnegative omitted-constraint slacks certify the original KKT conditions. Adding a violated constraint gives coupled primal and dual directions with a ratio bound preserving multiplier nonnegativity. A zero projected direction, nonpositive dual direction, and persistent violation certify dual unboundedness and primal infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: A_k^TG^{-1}A_k\text{ is nonsingular whenever }A_k^*\text{ is used}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k=-G^{-1}(g-A\lambda_k)\text{ gives the primal--dual working-set correspondence; dual multiplier feasibility and }a_i^Tx_k-b_i\ge0\ (i\in\bar{\mathcal S}_k)\text{ imply the original KKT conditions, while }d_k=0,\ y_k\le0,\ b_p-a_p^Tx_k>0\text{ imply dual unboundedness and primal infeasibility.}
knowledge_statements.title: Dual working-set correspondence and infeasibility certificate for strictly convex QP

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Dual Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-function construction for a convex QP with affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_x\;\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx\leq h,
\]
with \(H\succeq0\), define
\[
L(x,\nu,\mu)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\nu^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)+\mu^{\mathsf T}(Gx-h).
\]
The dual function is \(g(\nu,\mu)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}L(x,\nu,\mu)\), and the Lagrangian dual problem is
\[
\max_{\nu\in\mathbb R^m,\;\mu\geq0}g(\nu,\mu).
\]
It supplies a lower bound on every primal feasible objective value; under Slater feasibility relative to the equality affine space, the optimal values coincide and a dual optimum is attained when finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the Lagrangian over the primal variable produces a concave dual function maximized over free equality and nonnegative inequality multipliers.
assumptions_latex: Affine constraints define the stated convex QP.
For strong duality, a relative Slater point exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual is \(\sup_{\nu,\mu\geq0}g(\nu,\mu)\); weak duality always holds, and relative Slater feasibility yields zero duality gap.

children.title: Positive-Definite Explicit Dual
children.top_down_role: The reduced dual QP representation available with invertible curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Explicit Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit multiplier-only dual QP obtained by eliminating the primal variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the affine-constrained QP with \(H\succ0\), set \(r=c+A^{\mathsf T}\nu+G^{\mathsf T}\mu\). The unique minimizer of the Lagrangian over \(x\) is \(x(\nu,\mu)=-H^{-1}r\), so the dual is
\[
\max_{\nu\in\mathbb R^m,\;\mu\geq0}
-\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}r-b^{\mathsf T}\nu-h^{\mathsf T}\mu.
\]
Equivalently, it is a convex minimization QP after negating the objective. Its multiplier Hessian is the positive-semidefinite Gram matrix formed from \(H^{-1}\) and the combined constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible positive-definite curvature allows exact primal elimination and yields an explicit concave quadratic dual in the multipliers.
assumptions_latex: Equalities are \(Ax=b\) and inequalities are \(Gx\leq h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual objective is \(-\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}r-b^{\mathsf T}\nu-h^{\mathsf T}\mu\) over \(\nu\) free and \(\mu\geq0\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian linear coefficient in the primal variable.

children.title: Singular-Hessian Dual
children.top_down_role: Dual representations requiring null-space and range-compatibility treatment.

children.title: Generalized-Inverse Dual Representation
children.top_down_role: The explicit singular-curvature representation using generalized inversion.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Inverse Dual Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit dual function for positive-semidefinite, possibly singular quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) and set \(r=c+A^{\mathsf T}\nu+G^{\mathsf T}\mu\). Using the Moore--Penrose inverse \(H^{\dagger}\), the dual function is
\[
g(\nu,\mu)=
\begin{cases}
-\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}H^{\dagger}r-b^{\mathsf T}\nu-h^{\mathsf T}\mu,&r\in\operatorname{range}(H),\\
-\infty,&r\notin\operatorname{range}(H).
\end{cases}
\]
Therefore the explicit singular-Hessian dual maximizes the finite expression over \(\nu\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\mu\geq0\), and \((I-HH^{\dagger})r=0\). When compatible, all Lagrangian minimizers are \(-H^{\dagger}r+z\) with \(z\in\ker H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For singular curvature, the pseudoinverse dual is finite only when the Lagrangian linear term lies in the Hessian range.
assumptions_latex: Equalities are \(Ax=b\) and inequalities are \(Gx\leq h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized-inverse formula is finite exactly when \(r\in\operatorname{range}(H)\), equivalently \((I-HH^{\dagger})r=0\).

notation.meaning: Arbitrary vector in the null space of H.

children.title: Dual Range-Compatibility Domain
children.top_down_role: The additional compatibility geometry governing finiteness of the singular-curvature dual.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Range-Compatibility Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finiteness domain of the Lagrange dual when the convex quadratic Hessian is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(L(x,y)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+y^\top(Ax-b)\) and \(d(y)=c+A^\top y\). Then
\[
g(y)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}L(x,y)=\begin{cases}-\tfrac12d(y)^\top Q^\dagger d(y)-b^\top y,&d(y)\in\operatorname{Range}(Q),\\-\infty,&d(y)\notin\operatorname{Range}(Q).\end{cases}
\]
Consequently, \(\operatorname{dom}g=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:d(y)\in\operatorname{Range}(Q)\}\), equivalently \((I-QQ^\dagger)d(y)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The singular-Hessian dual is finite exactly for dual vectors whose Lagrangian linear coefficient lies in the range of the Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}g=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:c+A^\top y\in\operatorname{Range}(Q)\}\).

children.title: Constraint-Specialized Dual Forms
children.top_down_role: Dual representations specialized to equality, mixed-polyhedral, and bound-constrained models.

children.title: Equality-Constrained QP Dual
children.top_down_role: The dual specialization for affine equality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained QP Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrange dual of a convex quadratic program with affine equalities only.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). For
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax=b\right\},
\]
define \(L(x,y)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+y^\top(Ax-b)\), where \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) is unrestricted. The Lagrange dual is
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{-\tfrac12(c+A^\top y)^\top Q^\dagger(c+A^\top y)-b^\top y:c+A^\top y\in\operatorname{Range}(Q)\right\}.
\]
If \(Q\succ0\), the range condition is automatic and \(Q^\dagger=Q^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality multipliers are unrestricted; eliminating the primal variable gives a concave quadratic dual with a range condition when the Hessian is singular.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed maximization over \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) is the Lagrange dual.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Standard-Form LP Dual Representation and Weak Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual construction, primal–dual KKT correspondence, optimality from complementarity, and the weak-duality gap identity for a standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), the dual is \(D=\max\{b^T\lambda:A^T\lambda\leq c\}\), equivalently \(\max b^T\lambda\) subject to \(A^T\lambda+s=c\) and \(s\geq0\). The dual KKT conditions, with \(x\geq0\) as the multiplier for \(A^T\lambda\leq c\), are identical to the primal KKT conditions. For every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \((\lambda,s)\), \(c^Tx-b^T\lambda=s^Tx\geq0\). Hence the dual value is a lower bound on the primal value; if additionally \(s^Tx=0\), then \(x\) and \(\lambda\) are optimal and have equal objective values. Taking the dual of \(D\) recovers \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual of a standard-form minimization LP maximizes b-transpose-lambda subject to A-transpose-lambda being at most c, or equivalently introduces a nonnegative dual slack. Its KKT system is the same primal–dual system obtained from the primal problem. Every feasible primal–dual pair has nonnegative gap equal to the primal variable's inner product with the dual slack; a zero gap certifies optimality of both sides. Dualizing again recovers the primal.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad b\in\mathbb R^m,\quad c\in\mathbb R^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^Tx-b^T\lambda=s^Tx\geq0;\qquad s^Tx=0\implies x\text{ and }\lambda\text{ are optimal and }c^Tx=b^T\lambda.
