children.title: Polyhedrally Constrained QP Dual
children.top_down_role: The sign-restricted multiplier specialization for mixed affine constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedrally Constrained QP Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual form for mixed affine equalities and inequalities under the less-than-or-equal convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,r\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^r\). Consider
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\right\}.
\]
With \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(z\in\mathbb R_+^r\), and \(d=c+A^\top y+G^\top z\), its Lagrange dual is
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,z\in\mathbb R_+^r}\left\{-\tfrac12d^\top Q^\dagger d-b^\top y-h^\top z:d\in\operatorname{Range}(Q)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed affine constraints produce unrestricted equality multipliers, nonnegative inequality multipliers, and the singular-Hessian range constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^r\).
The inequalities use the convention \(Gx\le h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed sign-restricted concave maximization is the Lagrange dual.

children.title: Bound-Constrained QP Dual
children.top_down_role: The lower-bound and upper-bound multiplier specialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constrained QP Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual specialization for finite componentwise lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), and \(c,\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(\ell\le u\). For
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:\ell\le x\le u\right\},
\]
associate \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^n\) with \(\ell-x\le0\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb R_+^n\) with \(x-u\le0\). Setting \(d=c-\alpha+\beta\), the dual is
\[
\sup_{\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R_+^n}\left\{\ell^\top\alpha-u^\top\beta-\tfrac12d^\top Q^\dagger d:d\in\operatorname{Range}(Q)\right\}.
\]
When \(Q\succ0\), the compatibility constraint is automatic and \(Q^\dagger=Q^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower and upper bounds have separate nonnegative multipliers whose signed difference enters the dual quadratic term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed maximization over \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R_+^n\) is the bound-constrained QP dual.

notation.meaning: vector c minus alpha plus beta

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Saddle-point theorem for positive-definite quadratic programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The primal feasible set X contains the equality and inequality constraints; equality multipliers are unrestricted and inequality multipliers are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G\succ0, Q(x)=\tfrac12x^TGx+g^Tx, \mathcal L(x,\lambda)=Q(x)-\lambda^T(A^Tx-b), and \Lambda=\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m:\lambda_i\ge0\text{ for }i\in I\}. Then x^*\in X minimizes Q over X if and only if there exists \lambda^*\in\Lambda such that \mathcal L(x^*,\lambda)\le\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)\le\mathcal L(x,\lambda^*) for every x\in X and every \lambda\in\Lambda.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linearly constrained quadratic program with positive-definite Hessian, a feasible point is a primal minimizer exactly when it can be paired with an admissible multiplier to form a saddle point of the Lagrangian over the primal feasible set and multiplier domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}Q(x)\iff\exists\lambda^*\in\Lambda\ \forall x\in X\ \forall\lambda\in\Lambda:\ \mathcal L(x^*,\lambda)\le\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)\le\mathcal L(x,\lambda^*).
knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-point theorem for positive-definite quadratic programming

children.title: Weak Duality for Convex QP
children.top_down_role: The universal primal-dual bound relationship.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Duality for Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal bound between any feasible primal point and any sign-feasible dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,r\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^r\). Define \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\),
\[
L(x,y,z)=f(x)+y^\top(Ax-b)+z^\top(Gx-h),
\]
and \(g(y,z)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}L(x,y,z)\) for \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^r\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\),
\[
g(y,z)\le L(x,y,z)\le f(x).
\]
Consequently, \(d^\star\le p^\star\), including extended-real optimal values; no constraint qualification or attainment assumption is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every sign-feasible dual value is a lower bound on every primal-feasible objective value, regardless of constraint qualifications.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), with the remaining data in the displayed finite-dimensional spaces.
\(x\) is primal feasible, \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(y,z)\le f(x)\), and hence \(d^\star\le p^\star\).

children.title: Strong Duality for Convex QP
children.top_down_role: Zero-gap and dual-attainment structure in the affine-constrained convex QP setting.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–dual optimizer correspondence for positive-definite QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The equivalence concerns primal and dual variables linked by the preceding KKT transformation. The accompanying boundary statement warns that primal infeasibility need not imply dual unboundedness for arbitrary optimization problems, although it does for the linearly constrained QP class treated here.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G\succ0 and suppose the linearly constrained primal QP is feasible. For a primal-dual triple linked by y^*=Gx^*=A\lambda^*-g, primal and dual feasibility, and complementary slackness, x^* is a primal optimizer if and only if (\lambda^*,y^*) is a dual optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible linearly constrained quadratic program with positive-definite Hessian, corresponding variables satisfying the primal-dual KKT linkage are optimal on the primal side exactly when they are optimal on the dual side. The asserted converse between primal infeasibility and dual unboundedness is special to the linearly constrained setting and is not valid for duality in general.
assumptions_latex: x^*\text{ and }(\lambda^*,y^*)\text{ satisfy the associated primal-dual feasibility and complementarity relations}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}Q(x)\iff(\lambda^*,y^*)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\substack{A\lambda-y=g\\\lambda_i\ge0,\ i\in I}}\left(b^T\lambda-\tfrac12y^TG^{-1}y\right).
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–dual optimizer correspondence for positive-definite QP

children.title: Polyhedral Strong-Duality Route
children.top_down_role: The strong-duality route specific to affine and polyhedral feasible geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Strong-Duality Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong duality and attainment for a finite convex quadratic objective over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,r\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^r\). Define
\[
p^\star=\inf\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:x\in\mathbb R^n,\ Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\right\}.
\]
If the feasible polyhedron is nonempty and \(p^\star> -\infty\), then the primal minimum is attained. Moreover, there exist \(y^\star\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(z^\star\in\mathbb R_+^r\) satisfying stationarity and complementary slackness, the Lagrange dual is attained, and
\[
d^\star=p^\star.
\]
Neither strict feasibility nor full-dimensionality of the feasible set is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible convex QP with finite value over a polyhedron attains its minimum and has an attained dual of equal value.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), with all remaining data in the displayed finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist primal and dual optimizers, and \(d^\star=p^\star\).

children.title: Relative-Interior Strong-Duality Route
children.top_down_role: The general convex-analytic route adapted to lower-dimensional feasible geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Strong-Duality Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-interior constraint qualification after affine-hull equalities and identically active inequalities are separated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,r\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^r\). Let \(H=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\), and define \(J=\{i:G_i x=h_i\text{ for every }x\in H\}\). Treat the constraints indexed by \(J\) as equalities. If there exists \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}(H)\) such that \(G_i\bar x<h_i\) for every \(i\notin J\), then the relative-interior constraint qualification holds for minimizing \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) over \(H\cap\{x:Gx\le h\}\). If the primal value is finite, then the Lagrange dual has no gap and admits optimal multipliers:
\[
d^\star=p^\star,\qquad \operatorname*{argmax}g\ne\varnothing.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After inequalities that are identities on the equality affine space are treated as equalities, strict feasibility relative to that affine space ensures zero duality gap and optimal multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), with all affine data in the displayed finite-dimensional spaces.
There exists \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}(H)\) strictly satisfying every inequality not indexed by \(J\).
The primal optimal value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^\star=p^\star\) and the dual optimum is attained.

notation.meaning: relative interior of the affine set H
indices of inequalities that are identities on H

children.title: Dual-Attainment Multiplier Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Existence and multiplicity of dual optimizers associated with attained primal solutions.

children.title: Dual Attainment
children.top_down_role: Existence of a dual optimizer realizing the dual optimal value.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment of the multiplier dual for feasible, bounded convex QPs with polyhedral constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,r\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^r\). Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\) be nonempty, and suppose the minimum of \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) over \(P\) is finite. Define
\[
g(y,z)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\bigl(f(x)+y^\top(Ax-b)+z^\top(Gx-h)\bigr).
\]
Then there exist \(y^\star\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(z^\star\in\mathbb R_+^r\) such that
\[
g(y^\star,z^\star)=\sup_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,z\in\mathbb R_+^r}g(y,z)=p^\star.
\]
Every dual optimizer and every primal optimizer form a KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible finite convex QP over a polyhedron, the dual supremum is achieved by KKT multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), with all affine data in the displayed finite-dimensional spaces.
The primal optimal value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,z\in\mathbb R_+^r}g(y,z)\ne\varnothing\), and its value equals \(p^\star\).

children.title: Optimal Multipliers
children.top_down_role: Dual optimizers associated with attained primal solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT characterization of the multiplier set associated with a fixed primal optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,r\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^r\). Let \(x^\star\in\mathbb R^n\) solve the convex QP with constraints \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\). Its optimal-multiplier set is
\[
\Lambda(x^\star)=\left\{(y,z)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R_+^r:Qx^\star+c+A^\top y+G^\top z=0,\ z_i(G_i x^\star-h_i)=0\text{ for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\right\}.
\]
Under strong duality with dual attainment, \((y,z)\in\Lambda(x^\star)\) exactly when \((y,z)\) is dual optimal and forms a primal-dual KKT pair with \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal multipliers are precisely the unrestricted equality multipliers and nonnegative inequality multipliers satisfying stationarity and complementary slackness at the chosen primal optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), with all affine data in the displayed finite-dimensional spaces.
Strong duality and dual attainment hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda(x^\star)\) is the set of dual optimizers compatible with \(x^\star\).

children.title: Optimal-Multiplier Multiplicity
children.top_down_role: Non-singleton sets of dual optimizers representing the same primal optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Multiplier Multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry and a sufficient uniqueness condition for multipliers at a fixed QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,r\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^r\). For a primal optimizer \(x^\star\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(I=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}:G_i x^\star=h_i\}\) and
\[
\Lambda(x^\star)=\left\{(y,z)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R_+^r:Qx^\star+c+A^\top y+G^\top z=0,\ z_i(G_i x^\star-h_i)=0\text{ for every }i\right\}.
\]
The set \(\Lambda(x^\star)\) is a convex polyhedron, so multiplier multiplicity occurs exactly when it contains more than one point. If the rows of \(A\), together with the active rows \(G_i\) for \(i\in I\), are linearly independent, then \(\Lambda(x^\star)\), when nonempty, is a singleton. Failure of this independence condition alone does not imply multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplier set is polyhedral; linear independence of equality and active-inequality gradients guarantees uniqueness but is not necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), with all affine data in the displayed finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linear independence of the rows of \(A\) and \(G_I\) implies \(|\Lambda(x^\star)|=1\).

children.title: Primal Attainment versus Dual Attainment
children.top_down_role: Attainment relationships across the primal and dual problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Attainment versus Dual Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction and simultaneous attainment in finite convex QPs over nonempty polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,r\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^r\). Define \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), and
\[
g(y,z)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\bigl(f(x)+y^\top(Ax-b)+z^\top(Gx-h)\bigr).
\]
Primal attainment means \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x)\ne\varnothing\), whereas dual attainment means \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,z\in\mathbb R_+^r}g(y,z)\ne\varnothing\). Equality \(p^\star=d^\star\) alone implies neither property for a general convex problem. If \(P\ne\varnothing\) and \(p^\star\) is finite, then this convex QP attains both optima and
\[
\min_{x\in P}f(x)=\max_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,z\in\mathbb R_+^r}g(y,z).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Attainment is separate from value equality, but a feasible finite convex QP over a polyhedron attains both primal and dual optima.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), with all affine data in the displayed finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both optimizer sets are nonempty and \(p^\star=d^\star\).

children.title: Saddle-Point Optimality
children.top_down_role: Optimality viewed through saddle structure of the QP Lagrangian.

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian saddle-point characterization for a convex QP with affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,r\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^r\). Define
\[
L(x,y,z)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+y^\top(Ax-b)+z^\top(Gx-h)
\]
for \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^r\). A triple \((x^\star,y^\star,z^\star)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R_+^r\) is primal-dual optimal with zero duality gap if and only if
\[
L(x^\star,y,z)\le L(x^\star,y^\star,z^\star)\le L(x,y^\star,z^\star)
\]
for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^r\). Equivalently, the triple satisfies primal feasibility, dual sign feasibility, stationarity, and complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-dual optimality with zero gap is equivalent to the Lagrangian saddle inequalities and to the KKT system.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), with all affine data in the displayed finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal-dual optimality with zero gap is equivalent to the displayed Lagrangian saddle-point inequalities.

Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x):=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\;Gx\le h.\] Suppose \(Q=Q^\top\succeq0\) and there exists \(x^s\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(Ax^s=b\) and \(Gx^s<h\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated finite-dimensional convex QP under Slater's condition, a feasible point is optimal exactly when equality and nonnegative inequality multipliers satisfy stationarity and complementary slackness.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite-dimensional convex QP with primal objective \(f\), finite primal optimal value \(p^*\), and Lagrange dual function \(q\). Let \(x\) be primal feasible and let \((\nu,\lambda)\) be dual feasible, with finite values \[U=f(x),\qquad L=q(\nu,\lambda).\] Weak duality yields \[L\le p^*\le U,\qquad 0\le f(x)-p^*\le U-L.\] Hence \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies absolute \(\varepsilon\)-suboptimality for any \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Given a declared scale \(s>0\), the condition \[U-L\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s\] certifies scaled error \((f(x)-p^*)/s\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\). One admissible declared scale is \(s=\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex QP with finite optimal value, the feasible primal-dual gap bounds the primal objective error. Comparing the gap with a declared positive scale gives a scaled-relative quality certificate.

children.title: KKT-Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Numerical optimality assessment based on residuals of the primal-dual system.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT-Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise numerical assessment of feasibility, stationarity, sign, and complementarity defects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a candidate \((x,\nu,\lambda)\), define
\[r_p=(Ax-b,(Gx-h)_+),\quad r_d=Qx+c+A^\top\nu+G^\top\lambda,\quad r_\lambda=(-\lambda)_+,\quad r_c=\lambda\odot(Gx-h).\]
Given declared norms and tolerances \((\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_\lambda,\tau_c)\), the inequalities
\[\|r_p\|\le\tau_p,\quad\|r_d\|\le\tau_d,\quad\|r_\lambda\|\le\tau_\lambda,\quad\|r_c\|\le\tau_c\]
form a reproducible KKT-residual certificate. Zero tolerances certify the exact KKT system. Positive tolerances alone measure residuals; they imply an objective or solution-error bound only with additional conditioning or error-bound assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four declared residuals quantify primal feasibility, stationarity, multiplier sign, and complementarity. Vanishing residuals certify KKT; nonzero residuals need conditioning assumptions for error bounds.
assumptions_latex: Norms and numerical tolerances are declared in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities certify the stated KKT residual levels; if every tolerance is zero, the exact KKT conditions hold.

notation.meaning: primal, stationarity, sign, and complementarity residuals

children.title: Exact-Arithmetic Certificate Verification
children.top_down_role: Independent symbolic or rational verification of candidate primal-dual certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Arithmetic Certificate Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational-arithmetic verification of a proposed convex-QP KKT or primal-dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input rational data \((Q,c,A,b,G,h)\) and a rational candidate \((x,\nu,\lambda)\). First verify exactly that \(Q=Q^\top\), that the model’s convexity certificate establishes \(Q\succeq0\), and that
\[Ax=b,[1;3H\qquad Gx\le h,[1;3H\qquad \lambda\ge0.\]
Then compute exactly
\[Qx+c+A^\top\nu+G^\top\lambda\quad\text{and}\quad \lambda_i(G_ix-h_i)\]
for every \(i\). Accept and output “verified KKT certificate” precisely when all these quantities are zero; otherwise reject and return a failed equality or inequality. Under a valid convexity certificate, acceptance proves exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using rational arithmetic, check convexity, feasibility, multiplier signs, stationarity, and complementarity exactly; accept only if every required equality and inequality holds.
assumptions_latex: All model data and candidate entries are rational.
A separately checkable certificate of \(Q\succeq0\) is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance certifies that the rational candidate satisfies the exact convex-QP KKT system and is optimal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits exact-arithmetic verification, but no source is cited, the displayed feasibility system contains corrupted text, and the representation and verification procedure for the positive-semidefinite certificate is unspecified. These issues affect the algorithm's exact inputs and acceptance guarantee, so an authoritative source is required.

children.title: Convex QP Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Alternative-system certificates for inconsistency of the affine feasible set, independent of the quadratic objective.

children.title: Equality-System Inconsistency Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates for inconsistent affine equality systems.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(A^\top y=0\) and \(b^\top y\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear-algebraic alternative certifying that an affine equality system has no solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). The system \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \[A^\top y=0,\qquad b^\top y\ne0.\] Any such certificate can be rescaled so that \(b^\top y=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional equality system is inconsistent exactly when a multiplier annihilates every column of its matrix but has nonzero inner product with its right-hand side; the multiplier may be normalized to make that inner product one.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-System Inconsistency Certificates

children.title: Farkas Certificates for Mixed Affine Systems
children.top_down_role: Alternative-system certificates for mixed equality and inequality constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system \(Ax=b,\;Gx\le h\) is infeasible if and only if the displayed alternative system has a solution \((y,z)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R_+^p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional theorem of alternatives for simultaneous affine equalities and one-sided inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\). Exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \[Ax=b,\qquad Gx\le h;\] \[A^\top y+G^\top z=0,\qquad z\ge0,\qquad b^\top y+h^\top z<0,\] where \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(z\in\mathbb R^p\). A feasible pair \((y,z)\) for the second system is an infeasibility certificate for the first. It may be positively rescaled to satisfy \(b^\top y+h^\top z=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed equality-inequality system is infeasible exactly when unrestricted equality multipliers and nonnegative inequality multipliers produce a zero aggregate normal and a strictly negative aggregate right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Certificates for Mixed Affine Systems

children.title: Bound-Box Inconsistency Certificate Family
children.top_down_role: Certificates specialized to conflicting bounds and bound-augmented affine systems.

children.title: Variable-Bound Inconsistency Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates exposing incompatible lower or upper restrictions on variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Bound Inconsistency Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-coordinate certificate for contradictory lower and upper bounds on one variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider bounds \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\) on a real variable \(x_i\). The two bounds are jointly feasible if and only if \(l_i\le u_i\). Therefore the data pair \((l_i,u_i)\), together with an index \(i\) satisfying
\[l_i>u_i,\]
is an exact inconsistency certificate: no real scalar can simultaneously obey both inequalities. Verification consists solely of comparing the two endpoints in the model’s declared exact or ordered-number representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower bound exceeding the corresponding upper bound is an exact, locally checkable certificate that the variable’s bounds are inconsistent.
assumptions_latex: Both endpoints are finite real numbers for the same variable and coordinate system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(l_i>u_i\) certifies that no \(x_i\in\mathbb R\) satisfies \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\).

notation.meaning: lower and upper bounds for coordinate i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is elementary, precise, and correctly classified as a certificate, but it has no source reference. The contract requires source support for this candidate; an authoritative optimization-modeling or interval source with a specific locator is needed.

children.title: Box-Constraint Inconsistency Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates specialized to infeasible Cartesian-product bound regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Box-Constraint Inconsistency Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise characterization and certificate of emptiness for an axis-aligned box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(l,u\in(\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\})^n\), define
\[B=[l,u]:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:l_i\le x_i\le u_i\text{ for every }i\}.\]
The box \(B\) is nonempty if and only if \(l_i\le u_i\) for every coordinate. Consequently, an index \(j\) satisfying \(l_j>u_j\) is a complete, directly verifiable certificate that \(B=\varnothing\). The certificate remains valid when other coordinates have infinite endpoints, provided endpoint comparisons use the extended-real order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An axis-aligned box is empty exactly when at least one coordinate’s lower endpoint exceeds its upper endpoint; that coordinate is a complete certificate.
assumptions_latex: No endpoint is assigned an undefined extended-real value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=\varnothing\) if and only if \(l_j>u_j\) for some coordinate \(j\).

notation.meaning: closed axis-aligned box with extended-real endpoints

children.title: Affine-System versus Bound Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Inconsistency arising from interaction between general affine constraints and variable bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty bounded box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The intersection \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}\cap B\) is empty if and only if some \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfies one of the displayed strict separation inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional separating-direction certificate that affine equalities cannot intersect a prescribed bounded variable box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(B=[l,u]=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:l_i\le x_i\le u_i\text{ for every }i\}\) be a nonempty bounded box. The system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in B\), is infeasible if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) such that either \[y^\top b>\max_{x\in B}(A^\top y)^\top x\] or \[y^\top b<\min_{x\in B}(A^\top y)^\top x.\] The maximum and minimum are finite and are computable coordinatewise from \(l\), \(u\), and \(A^\top y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine equality system fails to intersect a nonempty bounded box exactly when a direction places the transformed right-hand side strictly above or below the full range attainable over the box.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-System versus Bound Conflicts

children.title: Bound-Certificate Recovery
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of infeasibility certificates in the original bound-augmented model.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery from a presolve derivation of contradictory variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent every derived lower or upper bound by a nonnegative linear combination of the original affine inequalities. Initialize each original inequality with its unit coefficient vector; under positive scaling and addition, apply the same operations to these vectors. If the terminal derivation gives contradictory bounds \(L_i>U_i\) on one variable, subtract their affine derivations to obtain weights \(y\ge 0\) satisfying \(B^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}y<0\), where \(Bx\le d\) contains the original bound and affine rows. Return \(y\); direct substitution verifies the original-model contradiction \(0\le d^{\mathsf T}y<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagating coefficient vectors through a bound derivation converts a terminal lower–upper conflict into a Farkas certificate for the original constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(Bx\le d\) is the original affine system, including finite variable bounds.
Every presolve bound derivation records nonnegative row combinations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered vector satisfies \(y\ge0\), \(B^{\mathsf T}y=0\), and \(d^{\mathsf T}y<0\), certifying infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Original inequality matrix and right-hand side.
Derived lower and upper bounds for variable i.

children.title: Transformed-Model Certificate Recovery

knowledge_statements.title: Transformed-Model Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic pullback of certificates through recorded, sign-compatible presolve row transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original inequalities be \(F(x):=Bx-d\le0\), and suppose a lossless presolve constructs transformed inequalities \(\widetilde F=S F\le0\), with each inequality-producing row of \(S\) nonnegative; equality rows may be combined with unrestricted coefficients. If \(\widetilde y\ge0\) certifies transformed infeasibility through \(\widetilde y^{\mathsf T}\widetilde F(x)=-\varepsilon\) for all \(x\), where \(\varepsilon>0\), then \(y=S^{\mathsf T}\widetilde y\) satisfies \(y\ge0\) and \(y^{\mathsf T}F(x)=-\varepsilon\). Recover eliminated-variable and scaling contributions by reversing the recorded transformations, including equality multipliers, before reporting \(y\) in original row coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse every recorded presolve transformation; the transpose map sends a transformed contradiction to an original-model contradiction when row signs are preserved.
assumptions_latex: The presolve transformations are lossless and their complete row-combination provenance is retained.
Inequality combinations preserve nonnegativity of multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pullback \(y=S^{\mathsf T}\widetilde y\) is an original-model infeasibility certificate.

children.title: Unboundedness Certificates
children.top_down_role: Recession-based certificate families for unbounded primal descent.

children.title: Curved Recession Analysis
children.top_down_role: Recession behavior in directions affected by nonzero quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Curved Recession Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Behavior of a convex quadratic along feasible recession rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(Q\succeq0\), and let \(C\) be a nonempty polyhedron. For \(x\in C\), \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\), and \(t\ge0\),
\[f(x+td)=f(x)+t(Qx+c)^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12t^2d^{\mathsf T}Qd.\]
If \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\), then \(f(x+td)\to+\infty\); hence such a curved direction cannot certify unbounded descent. Because \(Q\succeq0\), equality \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\) is equivalent to \(Qd=0\), so only null-curvature recession directions can support finite or decreasing asymptotic behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive quadratic curvature forces objective growth along a feasible ray; unbounded descent can occur only in Hessian-null recession directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\), then \(f(x+td)\to+\infty\); any descent recession certificate must satisfy \(Qd=0\).

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the feasible polyhedron.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical expansion and content kind are appropriate, but the cited locator is a section on convex sets and does not specifically support the quadratic recession claim or its null-curvature consequence. A locator covering recession analysis for convex quadratic functions is required.

children.title: Null-Curvature Descent Certificates
children.top_down_role: Unbounded-descent certificates supported by feasible directions in the Hessian null space.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Curvature Descent Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recession-direction certificate for unbounded convex-QP descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\inf_{x\in C} f(x)\), where \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), \(Q\succeq0\), and \(C\) is a nonempty polyhedron. A vector \(d\) is a null-curvature descent certificate when \(d\ne0\), \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). For any feasible \(x\) and \(t\ge0\), one then has \(x+td\in C\) and
\[f(x+td)=f(x)+t c^{\mathsf T}d\longrightarrow-\infty.\]
Thus the displayed conditions are directly checkable and certify that the primal optimal value is \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible recession direction in the Hessian null space with negative linear cost certifies that the convex QP is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\setminus\{0\}\) with \(Qd=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\) implies \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=-\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but “Part I Convex Analysis” is not a specific section, theorem, definition, or page locator as required. A precise source for the convex-QP recession certificate is needed.

children.title: Noncoercive but Bounded Regimes
children.top_down_role: Flat recession behavior that does not yield unbounded objective descent.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncoercive but Bounded Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization for convex quadratic minimization over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty polyhedron and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succeq0\). The objective is bounded below on \(C\) exactly when
\[c^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\quad\text{for every }d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\text{ satisfying }Qd=0.\]
Within this bounded regime, \(f\) is noncoercive on \(C\) exactly when there exists \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\setminus\{0\}\) with \(Qd=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d=0\). Along that ray \(f(x+td)=f(x)\); flat recession therefore destroys coercivity without producing unbounded descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundedness excludes negative-cost null directions; noncoercivity remains precisely when a nonzero feasible recession direction has both zero curvature and zero linear cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounded noncoercive regime is characterized by nonnegative cost on every null-curvature recession direction and equality for at least one nonzero such direction.

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the feasible set.

review_flags: Exact boundedness characterization should be checked against the cited recession theorem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the bounded-but-noncoercive leaf, but both biconditionals require a precise recession/coercivity theorem. The cited part-level locator is insufficient to verify the exact characterization.

children.title: Optimal Primal-Dual Pair Status
children.top_down_role: The feasible, finite, attained regime supporting paired optimality certificates.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m_e\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m_i\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The constraints are affine and the primal optimum is attained for the converse assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT relations certify primal and dual optimality with zero duality gap, and every attained primal optimum for this polyhedral convex QP admits such multipliers.

notation.meaning: Primal optimizer, unrestricted equality multiplier, and nonnegative inequality multiplier.
The ith row of the inequality matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT certificate for a finite-dimensional convex QP with affine constraints.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), where \(Q\succeq0\). A triple \((x^*,\nu^*,y^*)\) is an optimal primal-dual certificate when
\[Ax^*=b,\qquad Gx^*\le h,\qquad y^*\ge0,\]
\[Qx^*+c+A^{\mathsf T}\nu^*+G^{\mathsf T}y^*=0,\qquad y_i^*(G_i x^*-h_i)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m_i).\]
These relations imply primal and Lagrange-dual optimality with equal objective values. Conversely, every attained minimizer of this finite-dimensional convex quadratic over the stated polyhedron admits multipliers satisfying these relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex quadratic program with affine constraints, primal feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, stationarity, and complementary slackness certify an optimal primal-dual pair with zero duality gap; every attained minimizer admits such multipliers.

children.title: Primal-Unbounded Status
children.top_down_role: Feasible primal problems admitting objective values below every finite threshold.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Unbounded Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical status of a feasible convex QP whose value is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p^*=\inf_{x\in C}\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\}\), with \(Q\succeq0\) and nonempty polyhedral \(C\), primal-unbounded status means \(p^*=-\infty\). Equivalently, there exists a sequence \((x_k)\subset C\) with \(f(x_k)\to-\infty\). For this polyhedral convex-QP model, the status is equivalently witnessed by a nonzero direction \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\) satisfying \(Qd=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). Feasibility is part of the status; an empty feasible set is instead primal infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex QP is primal unbounded when it is feasible and its objective can decrease without limit, equivalently along a negative-cost null-curvature recession direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal-unbounded status is \(p^*=-\infty\), equivalently the existence of the stated recession certificate.

notation.meaning: Primal optimal value in the extended real line.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The status definition and certificate role are plausible, but the symbol f is used in the sequence formulation without being explicitly defined, and the claimed equivalence with a single recession direction needs a precise convex-QP recession theorem. The part-level source locator is insufficient.

children.title: Dual Infeasibility under Primal Unboundedness
children.top_down_role: Dual feasibility consequences associated with certified primal unboundedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility under Primal Unboundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality implication for the Lagrange dual of a minimization QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(
u,y)=\inf_x L(x,
u,y)\) be the Lagrange-dual function for a primal minimization QP, with \(y\ge0\) for inequalities written \(Gx\le h\). Every dual-feasible pair with \(q(
u,y)>-\infty\) supplies the finite lower bound \(q(
u,y)\le f(x)\) for all primal-feasible \(x\). Consequently, if the primal problem is feasible and has value \(-\infty\), no such pair exists: the finite-valued dual feasible set is empty and the dual problem is infeasible under this convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite dual-feasible point would bound every primal objective below, so primal unboundedness forces infeasibility of the finite-valued Lagrange dual.
assumptions_latex: The primal is a minimization problem and is feasible.
Weak duality applies to the stated Lagrangian sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(p^*=-\infty\), then \(\{(\nu,y):y\ge0,\ q(\nu,y)>-\infty\}=\varnothing\).

children.title: Dual Nonattainment Status
children.top_down_role: Dual regimes lacking an attained finite optimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Nonattainment Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes an unattained dual supremum from dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dual nonattainment means that the dual feasible set \(D\) is nonempty and the finite value \(d^*:=\sup_{z\in D}q(z)\) is not achieved by any \(z\in D\). This status is logically distinct from dual infeasibility, where \(D=\varnothing\). In particular, it cannot describe the standard Lagrange dual of a feasible primal problem with value \(-\infty\), because weak duality then forces \(D=\varnothing\). Therefore an algorithmic report of “dual nonattainment” does not by itself certify primal unboundedness and requires a sequence approaching \(d^*\) plus independent verification that \(D\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual nonattainment requires feasible dual points but no maximizer; it differs from the dual infeasibility forced by genuine primal unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: \(q:D\to\mathbb R\) is the finite-valued dual objective.
The dual is a maximization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual nonattainment requires \(D\ne\varnothing\) and \(q(z)<d^*<+\infty\) for every \(z\in D\); it is not a primal-unboundedness certificate.

children.title: Recession-Certificate Status Logic

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Certificate Status Logic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision logic connecting a feasible ray certificate to primal and dual statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex QP over a nonempty polyhedron \(C\), verify a proposed direction \(d\) by checking \(d\ne0\), \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). If all checks pass, then for every \(x\in C\), \(x+td\in C\) and \(f(x+td)=f(x)+t c^{\mathsf T}d\to-\infty\). The logically justified statuses are therefore primal feasible and unbounded below, and finite-valued Lagrange-dual infeasible. If any check fails, this candidate certificate establishes neither boundedness nor infeasibility; another certificate or optimality test is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified negative-cost null-curvature recession direction establishes primal unboundedness and dual infeasibility; failure of the test establishes no opposite status.
assumptions_latex: The Lagrange dual uses finite lower bounds as its feasibility convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid \(d\) certifies \(p^*=-\infty\) and an empty finite-valued dual feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerically Indeterminate Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonmathematical solver status caused by insufficient numerical evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver result has numerically indeterminate status when the computed data establish none of the following within declared residual and arithmetic conventions: a primal-dual optimality certificate, a primal-infeasibility certificate, or a primal-unboundedness recession certificate. Typical triggers include iteration or time limits, numerical breakdown, incompatible approximate certificates, or residuals exceeding tolerances. This status makes no assertion that the exact QP is optimal, infeasible, or unbounded. Any subsequent mathematical classification must be supported by independently checked certificate inequalities, preferably against the unscaled original model and with tolerances or exact arithmetic explicitly reported.

children.title: Linear-Objective Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Perturbations of the linear objective data.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and the unperturbed feasible set \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(p)=\inf_{x\in X}\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+(c+p)^\top x\}\), with \(v(p)=-\infty\) if the objective is unbounded below on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex QPs with fixed Hessian and feasible region.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), a linear-objective perturbation is the parametric convex quadratic program
\[
v(p)=\inf_{x\in X}\left\{\frac12x^\top Qx+(c+p)^\top x\right\},\qquad X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}.
\]
Thus the parameter changes only the objective gradient, from \(Qx+c\) to \(Qx+c+p\), while the curvature and feasible set remain fixed. If the objective is unbounded below on \(X\), then \(v(p)=-\infty\). Whenever an optimizer exists, the solution mapping is \(S(p)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+(c+p)^\top x\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear-objective perturbation adds a parameter vector to the QP's linear cost coefficient while leaving its Hessian and feasible set unchanged; its value is negative infinity if the perturbed objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Objective Perturbations

children.title: Right-Hand-Side Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Translations of affine equality or inequality levels.

assumptions_latex: The value is interpreted as an extended-real infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(r)=\inf\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax\le b+r\}\).

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), the right-hand-side perturbation family is
\[
v(r)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\frac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax\le b+r\right\},\qquad r\in\mathbb R^m.
\]
The inequality is componentwise. Positive \(r_i\) relaxes constraint \(i\), whereas negative \(r_i\) tightens it. The feasible-parameter domain is \(D=\{r:\exists x,\ Ax\le b+r\}\); by the extended-value convention, \(v(r)=+\infty\) for \(r\notin D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Right-hand-side perturbations translate affine constraint levels componentwise; positive components relax constraints and negative components tighten them.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and the finite nominal bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(\ell\le u\).

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and finite bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\), variable-bound perturbations with \(s,t\in\mathbb R^n\) form the family
\[
v(s,t)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\frac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax\le b,\ \ell+s\le x\le u+t\right\}.
\]
All inequalities are componentwise, and admissible parameters satisfy \(\ell+s\le u+t\). Increasing \(s_i\) tightens the lower bound, while increasing \(t_i\) relaxes the upper bound. These bounds can equivalently be represented as rows of a right-hand-side perturbation system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-bound perturbations independently move finite lower and upper bounds, with the perturbed lower bound required not to exceed the perturbed upper bound.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A,B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with the dimension of \(B\) adjusted below to \(m\times k\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) are fixed.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times k}\) be fixed, and let \(\theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k\). The coupled constraint-level perturbation family is
\[
v(\theta)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\frac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax\le b+B\theta\right\}.
\]
Its feasible-parameter domain is \(D=\{\theta\in\Theta:\exists x\in\mathbb R^n,\ Ax-B\theta\le b\}\). If \(\Theta\) is convex, then \(D\) is convex; if \(\Theta\) is polyhedral, then \(D\) is polyhedral. A parameter component may relax some constraints and tighten others according to the signs in the corresponding column of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupling matrix maps shared parameters to simultaneous affine-level changes, allowing one parameter to tighten some constraints while relaxing others; convexity or polyhedrality of the parameter domain is inherited when the prescribed parameter set has that property.

children.title: Feasibility-Boundary Transitions
children.top_down_role: Status changes caused by constraint-level parameters crossing feasibility boundaries.

assumptions_latex: \(D=\{r\in\mathbb R^m:\exists x,\ Ax\le b+r\}\) is the feasible-parameter domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\in\partial D\) precisely marks a feasible parameter at which arbitrarily small parameter changes can leave \(D\).

notation.meaning: topological boundary of the feasible-parameter set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the feasible right-hand-side parameter domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the family with constraints \(Ax\le b+r\), define \(D=\{r:\exists x,\ Ax\le b+r\}\). This set is convex and polyhedral. A parameter \(r\in D\) lies on the feasibility boundary when \(r\in\partial D\), equivalently when every neighborhood of \(r\) contains some \(r'\notin D\). Hence a continuous parameter path crossing from \(D\) into its complement changes the extended value from finite or possibly \(-\infty\) to \(+\infty\). At such a boundary, Slater feasibility can fail, so multiplier existence, boundedness, or smooth value sensitivity cannot be inferred from interior-point results alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasibility boundary consists of feasible parameters arbitrarily close to infeasible ones; crossing it can invalidate Slater-based multiplier and smooth-sensitivity conclusions.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Boundary Transitions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary characterization is mathematically plausible, but the cited convex-sets section does not specifically support the claims about Slater failure, multiplier behavior, or smooth value sensitivity. children.title: Constraint-Normal Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Perturbations that change the orientation and rank of affine constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), and the constraint-normal perturbation preserves affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(E)=\inf\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:(A+E)x\le b\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine inequality normals vary while levels and objective remain fixed.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), a constraint-normal perturbation is
\[
v(E)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\frac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:(A+E)x\le b\right\},\qquad E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}.
\]
Row \(i\) of \(E\) changes the orientation and scaling of constraint \(i\). Unlike a level perturbation, this parameter enters the KKT equations bilinearly through \(E^\top\lambda\) and \(Ex\). Rank loss among active rows of \(A+E\) may destroy constraint qualifications and uniqueness of the associated multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-normal perturbations change rows of the affine constraint matrix and can alter active-row rank, constraint qualifications, and multiplier uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Normal Perturbations

children.title: Hessian Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Curvature perturbations within or approaching the boundary of the convex QP class.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The perturbed problem remains a convex QP exactly when \(Q+H\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature perturbations of finite-dimensional quadratic objectives.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(c,A,b\), the Hessian-perturbed family is
\[
v(H)=\inf_x\left\{\frac12x^\top(Q+H)x+c^\top x:Ax\le b\right\},\qquad H\in\mathbb S^n.
\]
The objective is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(Q+H\succeq0\); thus this semidefinite condition is the exact boundary-preserving requirement for membership in the convex-QP class. If \(Q+H\succ0\), every nonempty closed convex feasible set admits at most one minimizer. At singular boundary points, uniqueness may persist but no longer follows from strict convexity. If \(Q+H\not\succeq0\), the family generally leaves convex quadratic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric Hessian perturbation preserves the convex-QP class exactly when the perturbed Hessian is positive semidefinite; positive definiteness additionally ensures uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Perturbations

assumptions_latex: At the reference parameter, LICQ, strict complementarity, and the second-order sufficient condition hold.
The active set remains unchanged locally.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.4 Geometric Interpretation of the Second-Order Multiplier Iteration p. 139
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods
Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(Ax\le b+r\) and let \(I\) be the active set at \(r=0\). Under LICQ, strict complementarity, and a second-order sufficient condition, the local solution and active-multiplier mappings are differentiable while \(I\) is unchanged. For a direction \(d\), their derivatives satisfy
\[
\begin{pmatrix}Q&A_I^\top\\A_I&0\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\dot x\\\dot\lambda_I\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}0\\d_I\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \dot\lambda_j=0\ \text{for }j\notin I.
\]
Consequently, multiplier sensitivity is controlled by the inverse of the active KKT matrix; near singularity, small data changes can produce large multiplier changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard nondegeneracy and a fixed active set, multiplier derivatives are determined by the differentiated active-set KKT linear system.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Multiplier Sensitivity

children.title: Shadow-Price Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Economic interpretation of marginal values assigned to active constraints.

assumptions_latex: Strong duality holds at \(r=0\), and an optimal multiplier \(\lambda^*\ge0\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-\lambda^*\in\partial v(0)\), so \(v'(0;d)\ge-(\lambda^*)^\top d\), with equality when \(v\) is differentiable at \(0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal interpretation for right-hand-side inequality perturbations.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
v(r)=\inf_x\left\{\frac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax\le b+r\right\}.
\]
With the Lagrangian \(L(x,\lambda;r)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\lambda^\top(Ax-b-r)\), every optimal multiplier \(\lambda^*\ge0\) supplies the subgradient \(-\lambda^*\in\partial v(0)\). Hence
\[
v(r)\ge v(0)-(\lambda^*)^\top r.
\]
If \(v\) is differentiable at \(0\), then \(\nabla v(0)=-\lambda^*\). Thus \(\lambda_i^*\) is the first-order value decrease per unit relaxation of constraint \(i\), under this sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal multiplier measures the marginal objective reduction from relaxing its constraint; for the stated convention, the value gradient equals the negative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Shadow-Price Interpretation

children.title: Sign-Conventions for Marginal Values
children.top_down_role: How constraint orientation affects reported shadow-price signs.

assumptions_latex: Optimal multipliers exist for the displayed constraint formulation.
Perturbations enter the displayed right-hand sides additively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(Ax\le b+r\), \(\partial v(0)\) contains \(-\lambda^*\); for \(Ax\ge b+r\), it contains \(+\lambda^*\) under the corresponding nonnegative-multiplier Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of common inequality and perturbation sign conventions.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization with \(Ax\le b+r\), use \(L=f(x)+\lambda^\top(Ax-b-r)\) and \(\lambda\ge0\). Then an optimal multiplier gives \(-\lambda^*\in\partial v(0)\). If the same feasible relation is written as \(-Ax\ge-b-r\) with Lagrangian \(L=f(x)-\mu^\top(-Ax+b+r)\) and \(\mu\ge0\), the numerical multiplier satisfies \(\mu^*=\lambda^*\), but the derivative must still be taken with respect to the chosen parameter. Therefore the economically reported shadow price for a relaxation is often \(-\partial v/\partial r_i=\lambda_i^*\), whereas the mathematical marginal value is \(\partial v/\partial r_i=-\lambda_i^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier signs depend on constraint and parameter conventions; for additive relaxation of a less-than inequality, the mathematical marginal value is the negative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Conventions for Marginal Values

children.title: Nonunique Shadow Prices
children.top_down_role: Marginal-value interpretation when optimal multipliers are not unique.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Strong duality holds at \(r=0\), the optimal multiplier set \(\Lambda^*\) is nonempty, and the value function is finite on a neighborhood of \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial v(0)=\{-\lambda:\lambda\in\Lambda^*\}\); hence the shadow-price vector is unique exactly when \(\Lambda^*\) is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued marginal values caused by multiplier nonuniqueness in convex right-hand-side perturbation problems.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and define
\[
v(r)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{f(x):Ax\le b+r\}.
\]
Let \(\Lambda^*\) be the nonempty set of dual-optimal multipliers at \(r=0\). If strong duality holds at \(0\) and \(v\) is finite on a neighborhood of \(0\), then
\[
\partial v(0)=\{-\lambda:\lambda\in\Lambda^*\}.
\]
Thus redundant or linearly dependent active constraints may yield several multiplier vectors and several valid shadow-price vectors, even when the primal optimizer is unique. Moreover, for every \(d\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[
v'(0;d)=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda^*}(-\lambda^\top d).
\]
The value function is differentiable at \(0\) exactly when the displayed subdifferential is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex right-hand-side perturbation problem, the negatives of all optimal multipliers form the value-function subdifferential; nonunique multipliers therefore produce set-valued shadow prices and directional derivatives.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Shadow Prices

children.top_down_role: Global convex and piecewise behavior under affine perturbations.

children.title: Value-Function Convexity
children.top_down_role: Global curvature behavior of optimal values under selected affine perturbations.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) are fixed.
For every feasible parameter \(r\in\mathbb R^m\), the quadratic objective is bounded below on \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b+r\}\).
The value is assigned \(+\infty\) outside the feasible-parameter domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all \(r_1,r_2\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\tau\in[0,1]\), \(v(\tau r_1+(1-\tau)r_2)\le\tau v(r_1)+(1-\tau)v(r_2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proper extended-real convexity under affine right-hand-side perturbations.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
v(r)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\frac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax\le b+r\right\},
\]
where \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Assume that the objective is bounded below for every feasible parameter, and set \(v(r)=+\infty\) when the perturbed constraints are infeasible. Then \(v:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex. Explicitly, for all \(r_1,r_2\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\tau\in[0,1]\),
\[
v(\tau r_1+(1-\tau)r_2)\le\tau v(r_1)+(1-\tau)v(r_2).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every feasible perturbed QP has a finite lower value and infeasible parameters are assigned positive infinity, the optimal value is an extended-real convex function of additive right-hand-side perturbations.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Convexity
