children.title: Piecewise Value Structure
children.top_down_role: Region-dependent smooth pieces forming the parametric optimal-value function.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Value Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiparametric strictly convex QP with affine right-hand-side perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(v(\theta)=\min_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b+E\theta\}\). If \(Q\succ0\) and \(v\) is finite on a polyhedral parameter set \(\Theta\), then \(\Theta\) admits a finite polyhedral subdivision \(\{R_k\}_{k=1}^N\) such that, on every full-dimensional region \(R_k\), the optimal active face is fixed, \(x^*(\theta)=F_k\theta+g_k\), and \[v(\theta)=\tfrac12\theta^{\mathsf T}H_k\theta+h_k^{\mathsf T}\theta+\beta_k,\qquad \theta\in R_k.\] The regional formulas agree in value on common interfaces, although their gradients or Hessians need not agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly convex multiparametric QP has a finite polyhedral partition on which its optimizer is affine and its optimal value is quadratic.
assumptions_latex: The QP data depend affinely on \(\theta\) through the constraint right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\) is continuous piecewise quadratic on a finite polyhedral subdivision of \(\Theta\).
review_flags: Exact multiparametric-QP source and hypotheses are not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source establishes the finite critical-region subdivision under the stated hypotheses, particularly in degenerate cases.

children.title: Value-Function Breakpoints
children.top_down_role: Parameter locations where the active value-function piece changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Breakpoints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Breakpoints of a piecewise-quadratic parametric QP value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{R_k\}_{k=1}^N\) be the maximal polyhedral critical regions on which a parametric QP value function \(v\) has one quadratic formula. The breakpoint set is \[\mathcal B:=\Theta\setminus\bigcup_{k=1}^N\operatorname{int}_{\Theta}R_k.\] Thus \(\bar\theta\in\mathcal B\) precisely when every relative neighborhood of \(\bar\theta\) meets at least two maximal regions. At such a parameter, an active constraint may enter or leave, or the quadratic formula may change. Membership in \(\mathcal B\) does not by itself imply nondifferentiability: adjacent quadratic pieces can have equal gradients at their interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Breakpoints are parameter values lying on boundaries between maximal critical regions; the active face or quadratic formula changes there, possibly without losing differentiability.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) has finitely many maximal polyhedral critical regions on \(\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B=\Theta\setminus\bigcup_k\operatorname{int}_{\Theta}R_k\).
review_flags: A source fixing the critical-region convention is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent when interiors are relative to Theta and the closed maximal regions cover Theta. A source is needed to fix the critical-region and breakpoint conventions and support the interface claims.

children.title: Convexity across Region Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of neighboring value pieces with global convex behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity across Region Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface criterion for continuous piecewise-quadratic functions on polyhedral regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a continuous function \(v\) be convex and continuously differentiable within each of two adjacent full-dimensional polyhedra \(R_i\) and \(R_j\). Suppose their common facet lies in \(\{\theta:n^{\mathsf T}\theta=\alpha\}\), with \(n\) directed from \(R_i\) toward \(R_j\). Continuity makes the tangential derivatives coincide on the relative interior of the facet. Convexity across that facet is equivalent to \[\nabla v_j(\theta)-\nabla v_i(\theta)=\gamma(\theta)n\quad\text{with}\quad\gamma(\theta)\ge0.\] Equivalently, the one-sided directional derivative in direction \(n\) cannot decrease when the interface is crossed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two convex regional pieces remain convex across a common facet exactly when the normal component of the gradient does not decrease across it.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is continuous across the common facet.
Each regional restriction is convex and continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\) is convex across the interface if and only if \(\nabla v_j-\nabla v_i=\gamma n\) with \(\gamma\ge0\).

notation.meaning: regional restrictions of the value function

review_flags: Exact piecewise-convex interface theorem source is not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normal-gradient-jump criterion fits the condition container, but its exact equivalence requires a sourced local or convex-union formulation. The present wording does not specify the domain on which convexity across the interface is asserted.

children.title: Directional Value Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: One-sided and directional behavior at nonsmooth parameter values.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Value Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided value derivative expressed through optimal inequality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v(\theta)=\min_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b+E\theta\}\), fix \(\bar\theta\) where the optimum is finite and strong duality holds. If the optimal multiplier set \(\Lambda^*(\bar\theta)\) is nonempty and compact, then \(v\) is directionally differentiable and \[v'(\bar\theta;d)=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda^*(\bar\theta)}\bigl(-E^{\mathsf T}\lambda\bigr)^{\mathsf T}d.\] Consequently, unequal optimal multiplier images can produce distinct one-sided slopes. If \(-E^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) is identical for all optimal multipliers, then \(v\) is differentiable at \(\bar\theta\) with that common vector as its gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional derivative of the value is the support function of the shadow-price vectors induced by optimal multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) and the optimum at \(\bar\theta\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v'(\bar\theta;d)=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda^*(\bar\theta)}(-E^{\mathsf T}\lambda)^{\mathsf T}d\).
review_flags: A precise value-function subdifferential theorem and constraint qualification source are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Strong duality and compactness of the multiplier set at one parameter do not by themselves justify the displayed derivative formula for every direction. A source must supply the required domain, stability, and constraint-qualification hypotheses.

children.title: Local Primal-Dual Solution-Map Stability
children.top_down_role: Local regularity of primal solutions and multiplier mappings.

children.title: Fixed-Active-Face Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Classical local sensitivity while the optimal face remains unchanged.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Active-Face Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical derivative formula while the active inequality face remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a parametric QP with stationarity equation \(Qx+c(\theta)+A_I^{\mathsf T}\lambda_I=0\) and fixed active equations \(A_Ix=b_I(\theta)\). If \(A_I\) has full row rank and the bordered KKT matrix \[K_I=\begin{bmatrix}Q&A_I^{\mathsf T}\\A_I&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular, then the local primal-active-multiplier derivative in direction \(d\) is uniquely determined by \[K_I\begin{bmatrix}x'(d)\\\lambda_I'(d)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-Dc(\bar\theta)d\\Db_I(\bar\theta)d\end{bmatrix}.\] If inactive slacks and active multipliers retain their required signs, this derivative describes the actual local solution branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed active face and nonsingular KKT matrix, primal and active-multiplier sensitivities solve one bordered linear system.
assumptions_latex: The active index set \(I\) is locally unchanged.
The bordered KKT matrix \(K_I\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x'(d),\lambda_I'(d))\) is the unique solution of the displayed bordered KKT system.

notation.meaning: bordered KKT matrix for the active face

review_flags: A local QP sensitivity theorem with sign-stability hypotheses is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bordered KKT sensitivity system is appropriate for the leaf, but an authoritative local-sensitivity result is needed to validate the differentiability and sign-stability assumptions supporting the actual solution branch.

children.title: Strongly Regular QP KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: Stable single-valued primal-dual behavior under combined rank, curvature, and complementarity regularity.

children.title: Locally Lipschitz Solution Maps
children.top_down_role: Stable local dependence of primal-dual solutions on problem data.

knowledge_statements.title: Locally Lipschitz Solution Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong regularity of a generalized KKT equation implies Lipschitz localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the parametric QP KKT system as \(0\in F(z,p)+N_C(z)\), where \(z\) collects primal and dual variables and \(C\) encodes multiplier sign restrictions. If this generalized equation is strongly regular at \((\bar z,\bar p)\), then there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\) and \(V\) of \(\bar z\), and a single-valued map \(s:U\to V\), such that \[\{z\in V:0\in F(z,p)+N_C(z)\}=\{s(p)\}\quad\text{and}\quad\|s(p)-s(q)\|\le L\|p-q\|\] for all \(p,q\in U\) and some \(L<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong regularity makes the localized primal-dual KKT solution unique and Lipschitz continuous with respect to problem data.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable near \((\bar z,\bar p)\).
The KKT generalized equation is strongly regular at \((\bar z,\bar p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localized primal-dual solution map is single-valued and Lipschitz near \(\bar p\).

notation.meaning: normal-cone mapping of the KKT constraint set

review_flags: The authoritative strong-regularity theorem and its precise generalized-equation setting are not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem matches the terminal container and the standard consequence of strong regularity, but no cited definition or theorem fixes the generalized-equation perturbation setting and Lipschitz-localization conclusion.

children.title: Locally Differentiable Solution Maps
children.top_down_role: Classical differentiability within a stable nondegenerate regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Locally Differentiable Solution Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical differentiability inside a stable, strictly complementary active-set regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) solve a smoothly parameterized convex QP at \(\bar p\). Suppose the active gradients are linearly independent, strict complementarity holds, and the reduced Hessian is positive definite on the nullspace of the active constraint matrix. Then the active set remains fixed near \(\bar p\), the corresponding KKT Jacobian is nonsingular, and the localized primal-dual solution \(s(p)=(x(p),\lambda(p))\) is continuously differentiable. Its derivative satisfies \[D_zG(\bar z,\bar p)Ds(\bar p)=-D_pG(\bar z,\bar p),\] where \(G=0\) is the smooth KKT system restricted to the active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ, strict complementarity, and positive reduced curvature yield a locally unique differentiable primal-dual solution branch.
assumptions_latex: The reduced Hessian is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s\) is locally continuously differentiable and \(Ds(\bar p)=-D_zG(\bar z,\bar p)^{-1}D_pG(\bar z,\bar p)\).
review_flags: A parametric nonlinear-programming or QP implicit-function theorem source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is plausible for smooth finite-dimensional QPs under LICQ, strict complementarity, and positive reduced curvature. A precise source is required for active-set persistence, localized uniqueness, and continuous differentiability.

children.title: Active-Face Transition Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Directional and nonsmooth behavior when active constraints enter or leave.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Face Transition Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional behavior at boundaries between adjacent QP critical regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a strongly convex multiparametric QP have continuous piecewise-affine optimizer \(x^*\) on critical regions \(R_k\), with \(x^*(\theta)=F_k\theta+g_k\) on \(R_k\). At a boundary parameter \(\bar\theta\), define the directionally accessible regions by \(\mathcal K(d)=\{k:\bar\theta+td\in R_k\text{ for all sufficiently small }t>0\}\). Then \[x^{*\prime}(\bar\theta;d)=F_kd\quad\text{for any }k\in\mathcal K(d).\] Continuity forces these expressions to agree whenever several regions are accessible in the same direction. Different directions may select different matrices \(F_k\), so classical differentiability can fail when constraints enter or leave.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an active-face transition, each direction selects an adjacent critical region and its affine solution derivative; different directions may yield different linearizations.
assumptions_latex: Its optimizer is continuous and piecewise affine on finitely many critical regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{*\prime}(\bar\theta;d)=F_kd\) for every directionally accessible region \(R_k\).

notation.meaning: regions accessible from the reference point along direction \(d\)

review_flags: A source for directional differentiability of continuous piecewise-affine QP solution maps is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property matches active-face transition sensitivity, but the directional-accessibility convention and agreement of regional derivatives on shared boundary directions require an inspectable source.

children.title: Set-Valued Degeneracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity under nonunique primal solutions, multipliers, or active descriptions.

children.title: Set-Valued Primal Solution Maps
children.top_down_role: Perturbation maps returning multiple primal optimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Primal Solution Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Argmin mapping for a parameterized convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For parameter \(p\), let \(X(p)=\{x:A(p)x\le b(p),\ C(p)x=d(p)\}\) and \(f_p(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Q(p)x+c(p)^{\mathsf T}x\), with \(Q(p)\succeq0\). The primal solution map is the multifunction \[S(p):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X(p)}f_p(x)=\{x\in X(p):f_p(x)=\inf_{y\in X(p)}f_p(y)\}.\] It is empty when the problem is infeasible or its infimum is unattained, singleton when the minimizer is unique, and genuinely set-valued when distinct feasible points attain the same minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal solution map assigns to each parameter all feasible points attaining the convex QP's minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(p)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X(p)}f_p(x)\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports parametric QP solution multifunctions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The argmin multifunction is correctly formulated and the definition fits the leaf, but no evidence or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied.

children.title: Set-Valued Multiplier Maps
children.top_down_role: Perturbation maps returning multiple optimal multiplier vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Multiplier Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: All KKT multipliers associated with parameterized QP minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the convex QP with inequalities \(g_p(x)=A(p)x-b(p)\le0\) and equalities \(h_p(x)=C(p)x-d(p)=0\), define the multiplier map \(M(p)\) by \[M(p):=\{(\lambda,
u):\exists x\in S(p),\ Q(p)x+c(p)+A(p)^{\mathsf T}\lambda+C(p)^{\mathsf T}
u=0,\ \lambda\ge0,\ \lambda_i g_{p,i}(x)=0\  orall i\}.\] Here equality multipliers \(
u\) are unrestricted. Even when \(S(p)\) is a singleton, \(M(p)\) may contain multiple points if active constraint gradients are linearly dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplier map contains every inequality-equality multiplier pair satisfying KKT conditions with some optimal primal solution.
assumptions_latex: KKT conditions are valid at the parameter under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(p)\) is the set of all KKT multiplier pairs associated with points in \(S(p)\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports multiplier multifunctions and their degeneracy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The KKT multiplier multifunction is coherently defined, but a source is required both for the convention and for the claim that dependent active gradients can yield multiple multipliers despite a unique primal solution.

children.title: Degenerate Active Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Nonunique or rank-deficient active representations affecting local sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Active Descriptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit umbrella convention for degeneracy of an optimal active description in a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) be an optimal solution of a convex QP, let \(I(x^*):=\{i:A_i x^*=b_i\}\), let \(S\) be its primal solution set, and let \(M(x^*)\) be the set of KKT multipliers associated with \(x^*\). The active description is called active-gradient degenerate when \[\operatorname{rank}A_{I(x^*)}<|I(x^*)|.\] A pair \((x^*,\lambda)\), with \(\lambda\in M(x^*)\), is called complementarily degenerate when \[\lambda_i=0\quad\text{for some }i\in I(x^*).\] The optimum is called primal-solution degenerate when \(S\) is not a singleton. In this record, “degenerate active description” is an umbrella term meaning that at least one of these three explicitly distinguished phenomena occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal active description is treated as degenerate when its active normals are dependent, a specified KKT multiplier has a zero component on an active inequality, or the primal solution is nonunique; these are distinct forms of degeneracy.
assumptions_latex: The QP is convex and \(x^*\in S\).
KKT multipliers associated with \(x^*\) are represented by \(M(x^*)\).

children.title: Sensitivity across Nonunique Branches
children.top_down_role: Local response behavior when several primal-dual solution branches coexist.

knowledge_statements.title: Sensitivity across Nonunique Branches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of intrinsic single-valued sensitivity at a nonunique optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex parametric QP \[\min_{-1\le x\le1}\ \theta x.\] Its solution map and value are \[S(\theta)=\begin{cases}\{-1\},&\theta>0,\\[-1,1],&\theta=0,\\\{1\},&\theta<0,\end{cases}\qquad v(\theta)=-|\theta|.\] Thus no continuous single-valued selection of \(S\) exists on any neighborhood of \(0\), and a derivative of “the optimizer” at \(0\) is not intrinsically defined. Sensitivity must instead be expressed through the multifunction, graphical derivatives, or branch-dependent selections; conclusions requiring a unique Lipschitz solution branch fail without additional regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonunique optimal branch can destroy every continuous optimizer selection, so optimizer derivatives must be replaced by set-valued or branch-dependent sensitivity notions.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic term may be merely positive semidefinite rather than positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\theta=0\), \(S\) has no continuous local single-valued selection and ordinary optimizer sensitivity is undefined.
review_flags: The example is directly checkable, but no supplied source addresses graphical sensitivity across nonunique QP branches.

children.title: Hoffman-Type Feasibility Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral feasibility error bounds supporting QP residual analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Hoffman-Type Feasibility Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Hoffman bound for a nonempty polyhedron with equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\}\neq\varnothing\). For every norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), with compatible residual norms, there exists a finite constant \(H=H(A,C)\ge0\), independent of \(b,d,x\), such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,P)\le H\bigl(\|Ax-b\|+\|(Cx-d)_+\|\bigr)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^n).
\]
Here the positive part is componentwise. Thus violation of the defining affine constraints controls distance to feasibility whenever the system is consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a consistent linear system, distance to its feasible polyhedron is bounded by a matrix-dependent constant times the equality and inequality violations.
assumptions_latex: All spaces are finite-dimensional and the residual norms are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,P)\le H(A,C)(\|Ax-b\|+\|(Cx-d)_+\|)\) for every \(x\).

notation.meaning: a Hoffman constant for the fixed constraint matrices and norms

children.title: KKT Residual-Distance Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Metric error bounds for primal-dual KKT solution sets.

children.title: KKT Residual Measures
children.top_down_role: Measures of primal, dual, stationarity, and complementarity discrepancy.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT Residual Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable product residual for linearly constrained convex quadratic programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the convex QP \(\min\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\}\), where \(Q\succeq0\), define for \(w=(x,y,z)\) the KKT residual
\[
r_{\rm KKT}(w)=\left\|\begin{pmatrix}Qx+c+A^\top y+C^\top z\\ Ax-b\\(Cx-d)_+\\(-z)_+\\z\odot(Cx-d)\end{pmatrix}\right\|.
\]
The five blocks measure stationarity, equality feasibility, inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity. For any norm on the product space, \(r_{\rm KKT}(w)=0\) exactly when \(w\) satisfies the KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KKT residual aggregates stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity violations; it vanishes exactly at KKT triples.
assumptions_latex: The QP data and a norm on the residual product space are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\rm KKT}(x,y,z)=0\) if and only if \((x,y,z)\) is a KKT triple.

children.title: Distance to KKT Solution Sets
children.top_down_role: Metric distance from a candidate primal-dual point to the KKT set.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance to KKT Solution Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance in primal-dual product space to the complete KKT solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed convex-QP data, let
\[
\mathcal K=\{(x,y,z):Qx+c+A^\top y+C^\top z=0,\ Ax=b,\ Cx\le d,\ z\ge0,\ z\odot(Cx-d)=0\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal K\neq\varnothing\), the distance of \(w=(x,y,z)\) to the KKT solution set is
\[
\operatorname{dist}(w,\mathcal K)=\inf_{\bar w\in\mathcal K}\|w-\bar w\|.
\]
The definition permits nonunique primal solutions and nonunique multipliers and depends on the chosen norm on the primal-dual product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT-set distance is the smallest product-space distance from a candidate primal-dual triple to any KKT triple.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(w,\mathcal K)=\inf_{\bar w\in\mathcal K}\|w-\bar w\|\).

notation.meaning: set of all primal-dual KKT triples

children.title: Residual-to-Distance Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Quantitative control of solution-set distance by KKT residual size.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Distance Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local metric-subregularity form of a convex-QP KKT error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal K\neq\varnothing\) be the KKT set of a fixed convex QP, and let \(r_{\rm KKT}\) be a residual having zero set \(\mathcal K\). A local residual-to-distance error bound at \(\bar w\in\mathcal K\) holds when there exist \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(w,\mathcal K)\le\kappa r_{\rm KKT}(w)
\quad\text{whenever}\quad \|w-\bar w\|\le\varepsilon.
\]
The least admissible local modulus is the infimum of such \(\kappa\); a global bound results if the inequality holds for every \(w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a KKT triple, an error bound controls distance to the full KKT set by a constant times the KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(w,\mathcal K)\le\kappa r_{\rm KKT}(w)\) locally around \(\bar w\).

notation.meaning: radius of the neighborhood where the bound holds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record accurately defines a local residual-to-distance property, but no source establishes the intended metric-subregularity formulation or its applicability in the convex-QP setting.

children.title: Degenerate Error-Bound Regimes
children.top_down_role: Loss or deterioration of residual-based distance control near degenerate systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Error-Bound Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature degeneration destroys any data-uniform KKT residual error-bound modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the unconstrained convex QPs \(f_\epsilon(x)=\tfrac12\epsilon x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), with \(\epsilon>0\). Their KKT set is \(\mathcal K_\epsilon=\{0\}\), while the stationarity residual is \(r_\epsilon(x)=|\epsilon x|\). Hence
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal K_\epsilon)=|x|=\epsilon^{-1}r_\epsilon(x).
\]
Consequently, although each fixed problem has a global residual error bound, every admissible modulus is at least \(1/\epsilon\). As \(\epsilon\downarrow0\), curvature vanishes and no uniform modulus exists over this family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For quadratics with curvature approaching zero, each residual bound remains valid but its best constant diverges, so no family-uniform bound survives.
assumptions_latex: The residual is the absolute stationarity violation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{\kappa:\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal K_\epsilon)\le\kappa r_\epsilon(x)\ \forall x\}=1/\epsilon\to\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-dimensional degeneration example is mathematically consistent and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, but the nontrivial conditioning claim has no cited evidence.

children.title: Objective Gap-Growth Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Relations between objective error, growth, and distance to the optimal set.

children.title: Objective-Gap Measures
children.top_down_role: Suboptimality measured through differences from the optimal objective value.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Gap Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal objective gap for a feasible point of a convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\}\), let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) with \(Q\succeq0\), and suppose the optimal set \(X^*=\arg\min_{x\in F}f(x)\) is nonempty. With \(f^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\), define the objective-gap measure for \(x\in F\) by
\[
g(x)=f(x)-f^*\ge0.
\]
It vanishes exactly on \(X^*\). For infeasible points the primal objective gap is left undefined unless an extended-value convention is explicitly adopted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective gap is the excess objective value of a feasible point over the optimal value, and it vanishes exactly at optimal points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(x\in F\), \(g(x)=f(x)-f^*\ge0\), and \(g(x)=0\iff x\in X^*\).

children.title: Local Growth Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local objective separation from the optimal set.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Growth Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Hölder growth of the objective away from the QP optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X^*\neq\varnothing\) be the optimal set of a convex QP on its feasible set \(F\). For an exponent \(p\ge1\), the objective has local order-\(p\) growth around \(X^*\) if there exist \(\alpha>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[
f(x)-f^*\ge\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^p
\]
for every \(x\in F\) satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\varepsilon\). The cases \(p=1\) and \(p=2\) are respectively sharp and quadratic growth regimes; the condition is uniform along the portion of \(X^*\) covered by the neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local order-p growth means that the objective gap dominates the p-th power of distance to the optimal set near that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f^*\ge\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^p\) for nearby feasible \(x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local order-p growth condition is internally precise and fits the condition container, but no source supports the formulation or the sharp/quadratic terminology.

children.title: Distance to the Optimal Set
children.top_down_role: Metric proximity of feasible candidates to the full set of minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance to the Optimal Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-space distance to all minimizers, allowing nonunique convex-QP solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X^*=\arg\min_{x\in F}f(x)\neq\varnothing\) for a convex quadratic program, and fix a norm on \(\mathbb R^n\). The distance from \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) to the optimal set is
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)=\inf_{x^*\in X^*}\|x-x^*\|.
\]
Because \(X^*\) is nonempty and closed, the infimum is attained in finite dimensions. This set distance measures primal solution error without selecting a particular minimizer and equals zero exactly when \(x\in X^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solution error is the minimum distance from a point to any primal optimizer, avoiding an arbitrary choice when optimizers are nonunique.
assumptions_latex: \(X^*\neq\varnothing\) is the optimal set of a convex QP.
A norm on \(\mathbb R^n\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)=\min_{x^*\in X^*}\|x-x^*\|\), with value zero exactly on \(X^*\).

notation.meaning: primal distance to the optimal set

children.title: Gap-to-Distance Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Quantitative relationships connecting objective suboptimality to optimal-set distance.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-to-Distance Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance estimate obtained by inverting a local objective-growth inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a convex QP has nonempty optimal set \(X^*\) and satisfies local order-\(p\) growth with constants \(\alpha>0\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(p\ge1\). Then every feasible \(x\) with \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\varepsilon\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\alpha^{-1/p}\bigl(f(x)-f^*\bigr)^{1/p}.
\]
In particular, quadratic growth gives the square-root estimate \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\alpha^{-1/2}\sqrt{f(x)-f^*}\). The conclusion controls primal distance only for feasible points in the stated growth neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-p growth condition converts objective gap into a local distance bound with exponent 1/p; quadratic growth yields a square-root bound.
assumptions_latex: Local order-\(p\) growth holds with \(\alpha>0\), \(p\ge1\), and radius \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\alpha^{-1/p}(f(x)-f^*)^{1/p}\) for feasible \(x\) in the growth neighborhood.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gap-to-distance estimate correctly expresses the consequence of the assumed growth condition and the property kind fits the leaf, but the record supplies no evidence reference.

children.title: Ill-Posedness Conditioning Boundary
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity escalation near feasibility, rank, curvature, or complementarity boundaries.

children.title: Distance to Ill-Posedness
children.top_down_role: Data-space proximity to feasibility, rank, curvature, or complementarity boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance to Ill-Posedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise distance from QP data to a specified boundary of well-posed instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal D\) be a normed space of convex-QP data tuples \(D=(Q,c,A,b,C,d)\), and let \(\Sigma\subseteq\mathcal D\) be a specified closed set of ill-posed data, such as instances at which feasibility or a chosen regularity property is lost under arbitrarily small perturbations. Define
\[
\operatorname{dist}(D,\Sigma)=\inf_{\widehat D\in\Sigma}\|D-\widehat D\|_{\mathcal D}.
\]
The value depends essentially on the data representation, norm, admissible perturbations, and declared ill-posed set; it is positive precisely when \(D\) lies outside the closed boundary by a positive margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to ill-posedness is the smallest permitted normwise perturbation taking the QP data into a declared set of unstable or boundary instances.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\) is a normed QP-data space.
\(\Sigma\subseteq\mathcal D\) is the specified closed ill-posed set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(D,\Sigma)=\inf_{\widehat D\in\Sigma}\|D-\widehat D\|_{\mathcal D}\).

notation.meaning: normed space of admissible QP data

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The metric definition is coherent, but the ill-posed set, data representation, and admissible perturbation framework remain abstract and uncited, so its intended QP-specific interpretation cannot be certified.

children.title: QP Data Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of solution information to perturbations in QP data.

knowledge_statements.title: QP Data Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative condition number based on distance to a declared ill-posed data set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal D\) be a normed QP-data space, let \(\Sigma\subseteq\mathcal D\) be a fixed closed ill-posed set, and let \(D\in\mathcal D\) satisfy \(\|D\|_{\mathcal D}>0\). Define
\[
\mathcal C_\Sigma(D)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\|D\|_{\mathcal D}}{\operatorname{dist}(D,\Sigma)},&D\notin\Sigma,\\
+\infty,&D\in\Sigma.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(D\notin\Sigma\), its reciprocal is the supremal relative radius \(r\) such that every perturbation \(\Delta D\) with \(\|\Delta D\|_{\mathcal D}<r\|D\|_{\mathcal D}\) keeps \(D+\Delta D\) outside \(\Sigma\). The condition number depends on the representation, norm, perturbation model, and chosen ill-posed set. Moreover, if \(\inf_k\|D_k\|_{\mathcal D}>0\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(D_k,\Sigma)\downarrow0\), then \(\mathcal C_\Sigma(D_k)\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance-based QP conditioning compares nonzero data size with distance to a specified ill-posed set. It is infinite on that set and diverges near it when data size stays bounded away from zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\) is a normed QP-data space.
\(\Sigma\subseteq\mathcal D\) is a fixed closed ill-posed set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Off \(\Sigma\), \(\mathcal C_\Sigma(D)=\|D\|_{\mathcal D}/\operatorname{dist}(D,\Sigma)\); on \(\Sigma\), \(\mathcal C_\Sigma(D)=+\infty\).

notation.meaning: size of the represented QP data

children.title: Feasibility-Boundary Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity escalation near transitions between feasible and infeasible instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Boundary Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust-feasibility radius for feasible QP constraint data relative to infeasible systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(A,b,C,d)\) denote constraint data with nonempty feasible set \(F(G)=\{x:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\}\), and let \(\mathcal I=\{G':F(G')=\varnothing\}\) in a fixed normed perturbation model. Define the feasibility margin by
\[
\rho_{\rm feas}(G)=\operatorname{dist}(G,\overline{\mathcal I}).
\]
If \(\rho_{\rm feas}(G)>0\), every admissible perturbation \(\Delta G\) satisfying \(\|\Delta G\|<\rho_{\rm feas}(G)\) remains feasible. Because \(G\notin\mathcal I\), the equality \(\rho_{\rm feas}(G)=0\) is equivalent to \(G\in\partial\mathcal I\), meaning that infeasible constraint systems approach \(G\) arbitrarily closely in the selected data metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For feasible constraint data, the feasibility margin is the distance to the closure of infeasible systems. A positive margin gives robust feasibility, while zero margin places the feasible data on the infeasibility boundary.
assumptions_latex: Constraint data use a fixed representation and norm.
\(\mathcal I\) is the set of infeasible systems under the admissible perturbation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\rm feas}(G)>0\) gives a robust-feasibility radius, whereas \(\rho_{\rm feas}(G)=0\) is equivalent to \(G\in\partial\mathcal I\) for feasible \(G\).

notation.meaning: linear equality and inequality constraint data
distance to the closure of infeasible data

children.title: Rank-Curvature Conditioning Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditioning deterioration near singular active systems or reduced curvature.

assumptions_latex: Consider the convex quadratic program \(\min_x \tfrac12 x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) subject to \(Ax\le b\), with \(Q\succeq0\).
At a KKT point, let \(I\) be the active set, let \(A_I\) be its active-row matrix, and let the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A_I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{rank}(A_I)<|I|\quad\text{or}\quad \lambda_{\min}(Z^\top QZ)=0\] marks a rank-curvature conditioning boundary: the active-set KKT matrix can be singular, and locally unique, Lipschitz primal-dual dependence is no longer guaranteed.

notation.meaning: Null-space basis for the active constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set boundary combining constraint-rank loss and loss of reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the active KKT matrix by \[K_I=\begin{pmatrix}Q&A_I^\top\\A_I&0\end{pmatrix}.\] If \(A_I\) has full row rank and \(Z^\top QZ\succ0\), then \(K_I\) is nonsingular. Consequently, within a regime preserving the active set and strict complementarity, the primal-dual solution is locally single-valued and Lipschitz in affine data perturbations. The boundary of this regular regime is reached when either active-row rank is lost or reduced curvature vanishes. At such points \(K_I\) may become singular, so arbitrarily small data changes may cause large solution changes, multiplier nonuniqueness, or active-set transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditioning can fail when active constraint normals become dependent or the quadratic loses positive curvature along active-set feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Curvature Conditioning Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-curvature characterization is plausible, but no citation supports its conditioning and local Lipschitz claims. The formula also leaves \(\lambda_{\min}(Z^\top QZ)\) undefined when \(\ker A_I=\{0\}\); a sourced version must handle that case explicitly.

children.title: Ill-Posedness Proximity versus Condition Growth
children.top_down_role: The structural link between boundary proximity and sensitivity amplification.

assumptions_latex: Let \(K_I\) be a nonsingular active-set KKT matrix measured in the spectral norm.
Perturbations are sufficiently small that the same active-set linearization remains applicable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\kappa_2(K_I)=\frac{\lVert K_I\rVert_2}{\operatorname{dist}_2(K_I,\mathcal S)},\qquad \mathcal S=\{M:M\text{ is singular}\}.\] Thus condition growth is reciprocal to relative distance from the singular KKT boundary.

notation.meaning: Set of singular matrices of the same dimensions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-norm relation for a fixed active-set KKT linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular \(K_I\), the spectral distance to singularity is \(\operatorname{dist}_2(K_I,\mathcal S)=\sigma_{\min}(K_I)\). Hence \[\kappa_2(K_I)=\lVert K_I\rVert_2\lVert K_I^{-1}\rVert_2=\frac{\lVert K_I\rVert_2}{\sigma_{\min}(K_I)}=\frac{\lVert K_I\rVert_2}{\operatorname{dist}_2(K_I,\mathcal S)}.\] Therefore approaching a rank-curvature boundary forces the active-system condition number to diverge whenever \(\lVert K_I\rVert_2\) stays bounded away from zero. Before an active-set change, first-order primal-dual perturbation amplification is controlled by \(\lVert K_I^{-1}\rVert_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed active set, the KKT condition number grows like the reciprocal of its relative distance to singularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Posedness Proximity versus Condition Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral distance-to-singularity identity is correct for a nonsingular square matrix, but the QP-specific interpretation concerning rank-curvature boundaries and primal-dual perturbation amplification requires a cited matrix-conditioning or QP sensitivity source.

children.top_down_role: Global parameter-space organization of active-set regimes, solution maps, multiplier maps, and value functions.

children.title: Affinely Parameterized QP Models
children.top_down_role: The standard parameter placements supporting polyhedral critical-region theory.

children.title: Affine Objective Parameterization
children.top_down_role: Parameters entering the linear objective data.

assumptions_latex: The Hessian and feasible set do not depend on \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameterized linear objective coefficient is \(c(\theta)=c_0+C\theta\), while \(Q\), \(A\), and \(b\) remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Only the linear objective term varies affinely with the parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective-affine multiparametric convex quadratic program has the form \[V(\theta)=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+(c_0+C\theta)^\top x:Ax\le b\right\},\qquad \theta\in\Theta,\] where \(Q\succeq0\), \(c_0\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\) are fixed. Thus the parameter changes only the linear objective data through the affine map \(c(\theta)=c_0+C\theta\); neither the quadratic curvature nor the constraint set varies with \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parameter enters only through the linear objective coefficient, which has the affine form c0 plus C times theta.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Objective Parameterization

children.title: Affine Constraint-Level Parameterization
children.top_down_role: Parameters translating affine constraints and variable bounds.

children.title: Affine Right-Hand-Side Parameterization
children.top_down_role: Affine parameter dependence in equality or inequality constraint levels.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint system is \(Ax\le b_0+B\theta\), so each constraint level is affine in \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed constraint normals with affinely moving inequality levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A right-hand-side-affine constraint family is \[X(\theta)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b_0+B\theta\},\qquad \theta\in\Theta,\] where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b_0\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\) are fixed. Equivalently, constraint \(i\) is \(a_i^\top x\le b_{0i}+B_{i:}\theta\). The parameter translates the supporting hyperplanes without changing their normal vectors; feasibility at \(\theta\) means \(X(\theta)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each inequality right-hand side varies affinely with the parameter while all constraint normals remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Right-Hand-Side Parameterization

children.title: Affine Variable-Bound Parameterization
children.top_down_role: Affine parameter dependence in lower or upper variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Variable-Bound Parameterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise affine finite lower and upper variable bounds; absent bounds are represented by omitting the corresponding inequality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An affine variable-bound parameterization specifies \[\ell_0+L\theta\le x\le u_0+U\theta,\qquad \theta\in\Theta,\] componentwise, where \(\ell_0,u_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(L,U\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\) are fixed. It is a right-hand-side parameterization because the bounds can be written as \[\begin{pmatrix}-I\\I\end{pmatrix}x\le\begin{pmatrix}-\ell_0-L\theta\\u_0+U\theta\end{pmatrix}.\] A component without a lower or upper bound is represented by omitting the corresponding inequality row. Feasibility requires \(\ell_i(\theta)\le u_i(\theta)\) for every component having both bounds, in addition to any other constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite lower and upper variable bounds are componentwise affine functions of the shared parameter and can be represented as ordinary affine inequalities; absent bounds are omitted.
assumptions_latex: The displayed lower and upper bound data are finite; a missing bound is represented by omitting its inequality row.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite variable bounds have the affine forms \(\ell(\theta)=\ell_0+L\theta\) and \(u(\theta)=u_0+U\theta\).

children.title: Coupled Affine Constraint-Level Parameters
children.top_down_role: Shared parameters affecting general affine levels and variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single parameter vector drives multiple constraint blocks through a stacked affine right-hand side \(b_0+B\theta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One parameter vector jointly shifts several constraint families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose constraint block \(j\) is \(A_jx\le b_j+B_j\theta\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r\). Their coupled affine parameterization is the single system \[Ax\le b_0+B\theta,\qquad A=\begin{pmatrix}A_1\\\vdots\\A_r\end{pmatrix},\quad b_0=\begin{pmatrix}b_1\\\vdots\\b_r\end{pmatrix},\quad B=\begin{pmatrix}B_1\\\vdots\\B_r\end{pmatrix}.\] Coupling means that the same coordinates of \(\theta\) may occur in several rows or blocks; it does not require independent block parameters. Cross-block dependence is therefore encoded by the shared columns of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several constraint blocks are coupled when the same parameter vector shifts their right-hand sides through a stacked loading matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Affine Constraint-Level Parameters

children.title: Parameterized Feasibility Transitions
children.top_down_role: Parameter-space boundaries where constraint-level changes alter feasibility status.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameterized Feasibility Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary, relative to the parameter domain, between feasible and infeasible parameters for affine inequality levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\Theta_F=\{\theta\in\Theta:X(\theta)\ne\varnothing\}=\{\theta\in\Theta:\exists x,\ Ax-B\theta\le b_0\}.\] Because \(\Theta_F\) is the projection of a polyhedron in \((x,\theta)\), it is polyhedral. Let \(\partial_{\Theta}\Theta_F\) denote the topological boundary of \(\Theta_F\) relative to \(\Theta\). A parameter path \(\theta(t)\in\Theta\) undergoes a feasibility transition at \(t_0\) when every neighborhood of \(\theta(t_0)\) along the path contains both feasible and infeasible parameter values. Every such transition point belongs to \(\partial_{\Theta}\Theta_F\); outside this relative-to-domain boundary, feasibility status is locally constant in \(\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible parameters form a polyhedron, and feasibility can change only on its topological boundary relative to the parameter domain.
assumptions_latex: Let \(X(\theta)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b_0+B\theta\}\) with fixed finite-dimensional data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible-parameter set \(\Theta_F\) is polyhedral, and feasibility transitions occur on its boundary \(\partial_{\Theta}\Theta_F\) relative to \(\Theta\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set at parameter value theta
Topological boundary relative to the parameter domain Theta

children.title: Combined Affine Parameterization
children.top_down_role: Shared affine parameter dependence across objective and constraint data.

assumptions_latex: The Hessian \(Q\succeq0\) and constraint-normal matrix \(A\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The same parameter vector enters both objective and constraint data through \(c_0+C\theta\) and \(b_0+B\theta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared affine dependence in linear objective and inequality levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A combined affinely parameterized convex quadratic program is \[V(\theta)=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+(c_0+C\theta)^\top x:Ax\le b_0+B\theta\right\},\qquad \theta\in\Theta,\] with fixed \(Q\succeq0\), \(A\), \(c_0\), \(C\), \(b_0\), and \(B\). The same parameter vector may simultaneously alter objective slopes and constraint levels. Objective-only and right-hand-side-only models are obtained by setting \(B=0\) and \(C=0\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared parameter vector affinely changes both the linear objective coefficient and the constraint right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Affine Parameterization

children.title: Critical-Region Geometry
children.top_down_role: The parameter-space partition induced by stable optimal active faces.

children.title: Full-Dimensional Critical Regions
children.top_down_role: Parameter regions with stable nondegenerate primal-dual structure.

assumptions_latex: Consider a combined affine convex QP with \(Q\succ0\) and polyhedral parameter domain \(\Theta\).
Fix an active set \(I\) whose KKT matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The associated critical region is a polyhedron; it is full-dimensional when its interior in \(\mathbb R^p\) is nonempty.

notation.meaning: Critical region associated with the active set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondegenerate critical regions having positive parameter-space dimension \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solving the equality-constrained KKT system for active set \(I\) gives affine candidates \(x_I(\theta)\) and \(\lambda_I(\theta)\). Define \[\mathcal R_I=\{\theta\in\Theta:A_Ix_I(\theta)=b_{0I}+B_I\theta,\ A_{I^c}x_I(\theta)\le b_{0I^c}+B_{I^c}\theta,\ \lambda_I(\theta)\ge0\}.\] Since all displayed conditions are affine in \(\theta\), \(\mathcal R_I\) is polyhedral. It is a full-dimensional critical region precisely when \(\operatorname{int}(\mathcal R_I)\ne\varnothing\) in \(\mathbb R^p\). Under strict inequalities for inactive slacks and active multipliers, the primal-dual active structure is locally constant throughout its interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-dimensional critical region is a polyhedral parameter set with nonempty interior on which one nondegenerate active set remains optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Dimensional Critical Regions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The active-set construction and ambient full-dimensionality criterion are plausible and fit the leaf, but the record provides no source for the multiparametric-QP critical-region result or its nondegeneracy interpretation.

children.title: Lower-Dimensional Region Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Transition sets where adjacent active-face regimes meet.

assumptions_latex: Let \(\mathcal R_I\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be a full-dimensional polyhedral critical region.
Its defining inequalities are affine primal-slack and dual-multiplier conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Its transition boundary lies in finitely many affine hyperplanes where an inactive slack or active multiplier becomes zero.

notation.meaning: Critical region for active set I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facets and lower-dimensional intersections separating active-set regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inactive constraint \(j\notin I\), define its affine slack by \(s_j(\theta)=b_{0j}+B_{j:}\theta-a_j^\top x_I(\theta)\). The boundary of the critical region satisfies \[\partial\mathcal R_I\subseteq\bigcup_{j\notin I}\{\theta:s_j(\theta)=0\}\ \cup\ \bigcup_{i\in I}\{\theta:\lambda_i(\theta)=0\}\ \cup\ \partial\Theta.\] Each nonempty set on the right is contained in an affine hyperplane unless its defining affine function vanishes identically. Facets have dimension \(p-1\); simultaneous equalities generate lower-dimensional faces where several active-set transitions may coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Critical-region boundaries occur where an inactive constraint becomes tight, an active multiplier vanishes, or the parameter domain itself ends.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Dimensional Region Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine slack and multiplier boundary description is standard under the stated regime, but no source is supplied. The conclusion also omits parameter-domain boundary components that are included in the main statement and plain text.

children.title: Critical-Region Adjacency
children.top_down_role: Neighbor relations induced by entry, exit, and exchange of active constraints.

assumptions_latex: Let \(\mathcal R_I\) and \(\mathcal R_J\) be distinct full-dimensional critical regions in \(\mathbb R^p\).
Assume their common boundary contains a relative-interior point of a facet and no additional degeneracy occurs there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Facet-adjacent nondegenerate regions differ by one constraint entering or leaving the active set; degenerate interfaces may permit exchanges or multiple simultaneous changes.

notation.meaning: Active set on the first region
Active set on the second region

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet adjacency under a single nondegenerate active-set event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Call \(\mathcal R_I\) and \(\mathcal R_J\) facet-adjacent when \[\dim\bigl(\mathcal R_I\cap\mathcal R_J\bigr)=p-1.\] At a nondegenerate relative-interior point of their common facet, exactly one defining primal-slack or dual-multiplier inequality is tight. If an inactive slack reaches zero, then \(J=I\cup\{k\}\) for one \(k\notin I\); if an active multiplier reaches zero, then \(J=I\setminus\{k\}\) for one \(k\in I\). When several conditions vanish or active normals are dependent, adjacent descriptions can instead involve an exchange or multiple changes, so the one-index rule requires the stated nondegeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Across a nondegenerate shared facet, one constraint enters or leaves the active set; degeneracy can produce exchanges or multiple changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Region Adjacency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-index entry-or-exit rule depends on a precise nondegeneracy framework; the phrase 'no additional degeneracy' does not define sufficient hypotheses. A parametric-QP source must support the facet-adjacency rule and its exchange exceptions.

children.title: Parametric Solution-Value Correspondence
children.top_down_role: The classical piecewise structure of strictly convex affinely parameterized QPs.

children.title: Piecewise-Affine Primal Solution Map
children.top_down_role: Regionwise affine primal behavior in the standard unique-solution regime.

assumptions_latex: Let \(Q\succ0\), let \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be polyhedral, and consider affine objective and right-hand-side data.
Assume the QP is feasible for every \(\theta\) in the parameter set under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique optimizer \(x^*(\theta)\) is continuous and piecewise affine on a finite polyhedral critical-region partition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly convex finite-dimensional multiparametric QP with polyhedral constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[x^*(\theta)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+(c_0+C\theta)^\top x:Ax\le b_0+B\theta\right\}.\] Since \(Q\succ0\), every feasible instance has a unique optimizer. There exist finitely many polyhedral critical regions \(\mathcal R_1,\ldots,\mathcal R_N\) covering the feasible parameter set and matrices \(F_k\), vectors \(g_k\), such that \[x^*(\theta)=F_k\theta+g_k\qquad\text{for all }\theta\in\mathcal R_k.\] The affine formulas agree wherever regions overlap, so \(x^*\) is continuous, although its derivative may change across critical-region boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible strictly convex multiparametric QP has a unique optimizer that is continuous and affine on each of finitely many polyhedral critical regions.
knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Affine Primal Solution Map

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is standard for strictly convex finite-dimensional multiparametric QPs, but its finite polyhedral partition, regionwise affine formula, and continuity conclusion require an authoritative theorem citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Piecewise-Affine Multiplier Map
children.top_down_role: Regionwise affine multiplier behavior under stable multiplier representation.

assumptions_latex: On a full-dimensional polyhedral critical region \(R\), the active set \(I\) is fixed and \(G_I\) has full row rank.
The parametric QP is feasible for every \(\theta\in R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(L_I\in\mathbb R^{|I|\times p}\) and \(\ell_I\in\mathbb R^{|I|}\) such that the unique KKT multiplier representation satisfies \(\lambda_I^*(\theta)=L_I\theta+\ell_I\) and \(\lambda_{I^c}^*(\theta)=0\) for all \(\theta\in R\).

notation.meaning: Active constraint index set and its row submatrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly convex mpQP with a fixed LICQ active set on each critical region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(V(\theta)=\min_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+(f+F\theta)^{\mathsf T}x:Gx\leq w+S\theta\}\). On a critical region \(R\) with fixed active set \(I\), the KKT equalities are \(Hx+f+F\theta+G_I^{\mathsf T}\lambda_I=0\) and \(G_Ix=w_I+S_I\theta\). If \(H\succ0\) and \(G_I\) has full row rank, their coefficient matrix is nonsingular. Consequently, throughout \(R\), \(\lambda_I^*(\theta)=L_I\theta+\ell_I\), while \(\lambda_{I^c}^*(\theta)=0\); dual feasibility restricts \(R\) by \(L_I\theta+\ell_I\geq0\). Thus the selected multiplier map is affine on every such region and piecewise affine over their union.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed linearly independent active set, the KKT system has an affine right-hand side, so its unique multiplier is affine in the parameter on that critical region.
knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Affine Multiplier Map

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is mathematically coherent under positive definiteness and LICQ and fits the multiplier-map container, but no inspectable source supports the stated mpQP regularity and piecewise-affine conclusion.

children.title: Piecewise-Quadratic Value Function
children.top_down_role: Regionwise quadratic optimal-value behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(H\succ0\), and the feasible parameter domain is covered by finitely many polyhedral critical regions.
On each critical region, the primal optimizer is affine in \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every critical region \(R_j\), there are a symmetric matrix \(Q_j\), vector \(q_j\), and scalar \(r_j\) such that \(V(\theta)=\tfrac12\theta^{\mathsf T}Q_j\theta+q_j^{\mathsf T}\theta+r_j\) for all \(\theta\in R_j\).

notation.meaning: Affine optimizer coefficients on region j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regionwise value representation for a strictly convex mpQP with affine parameter dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(V(\theta)=\min_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+(f+F\theta)^{\mathsf T}x:Gx\leq w+S\theta\}\), suppose \(H\succ0\) and \(x^*(\theta)=K_j\theta+k_j\) on a critical region \(R_j\). Substitution gives \[V(\theta)=\tfrac12(K_j\theta+k_j)^{\mathsf T}H(K_j\theta+k_j)+(f+F\theta)^{\mathsf T}(K_j\theta+k_j).\] Hence suitable \(Q_j=Q_j^{\mathsf T}\), \(q_j\), and \(r_j\) satisfy \(V(\theta)=\tfrac12\theta^{\mathsf T}Q_j\theta+q_j^{\mathsf T}\theta+r_j\) on \(R_j\). Therefore \(V\) is piecewise quadratic on the feasible parameter domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting each region's affine optimizer into the quadratic objective yields a quadratic formula for the optimal value on that region.
knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Quadratic Value Function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Substitution of a regionwise affine optimizer correctly produces a regionwise quadratic value formula, and representation is the appropriate knowledge kind. No source is cited for the mpQP assumptions or finite critical-region conclusion.

children.title: Critical-Region Interface Regularity
children.top_down_role: Continuity and derivative changes across critical-region boundaries.

children.title: Continuity Across Critical-Region Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Preservation of primal, multiplier, or value behavior when adjacent critical regions meet.

assumptions_latex: \(H\succ0\), and the QP data depend continuously and affinely on \(\theta\).
Two closed critical regions \(R_i\) and \(R_j\) share a feasible boundary point \(\bar\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regionwise optimizer and value formulas agree at \(\bar\theta\): \(K_i\bar\theta+k_i=K_j\bar\theta+k_j=x^*(\bar\theta)\) and \(V_i(\bar\theta)=V_j(\bar\theta)=V(\bar\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity of the unique primal solution and value, not necessarily of a nonunique multiplier selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_i\) and \(R_j\) be closed critical regions of the strictly convex parametric QP, with affine optimizer formulas \(x_i(	heta)=K_i\theta+k_i\) and \(x_j(	heta)=K_j\theta+k_j\). If \(\bar\theta\in R_i\cap R_j\), both formulas solve the same QP at \(\bar\theta\). Since \(H\succ0\), that QP has at most one minimizer, so \(K_i\bar\theta+k_i=K_j\bar\theta+k_j=x^*(\bar\theta)\). Evaluating the common objective at this point also gives \(V_i(\bar\theta)=V_j(\bar\theta)=V(\bar\theta)\). Thus the assembled primal solution and value maps are continuous across the interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a shared region boundary, both regional formulas solve the same strictly convex QP; uniqueness makes the primal solutions, and hence the values, coincide.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuity Across Critical-Region Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The continuity claim is appropriately restricted to the unique primal optimizer and value, but the required closed-region validity and interface-continuity result have no cited source.

children.title: Derivative Changes at Region Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Changes in local sensitivity behavior across critical-region boundaries.

assumptions_latex: Adjacent critical regions \(R_i\) and \(R_j\) carry affine solution formulas and quadratic value formulas.
Their formulas agree in value on the common interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The one-sided Jacobians are \(D x^*|_{R_i}=K_i\) and \(D x^*|_{R_j}=K_j\); differentiability across a relative-interior interface point requires agreement on feasible transverse directions. Likewise, value differentiability requires agreement of the limiting gradients.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided derivatives at an interface between two full-dimensional critical regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x^*(\theta)=K_i\theta+k_i\) on \(R_i\) and \(x^*(\theta)=K_j\theta+k_j\) on \(R_j\). At a relative-interior interface point \(\bar\theta\), the one-sided Jacobians are \(K_i\) and \(K_j\); a derivative crossing the interface can exist only when the two linearizations agree on admissible crossing directions, and full differentiability requires \(K_i=K_j\). If \(V_\ell(\theta)=\tfrac12\theta^{\mathsf T}Q_\ell\theta+q_\ell^{\mathsf T}\theta+r_\ell\), then the limiting gradients are \(Q_i\bar\theta+q_i\) and \(Q_j\bar\theta+q_j\). Continuity therefore does not preclude a change of primal Jacobian or value gradient at the interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjacent affine and quadratic pieces may meet continuously while their one-sided Jacobians or gradients differ; differentiability requires the relevant limiting derivatives to agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative Changes at Region Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between continuity and agreement of one-sided derivatives fits the container, but the characterization of crossing directions and full differentiability needs an authoritative source and more contextual verification.

children.title: Multiple-Region Boundary Intersections
children.top_down_role: Nonsmooth behavior where several critical-region closures share a parameter boundary.

assumptions_latex: A feasible parameter \(\bar\theta\) belongs to the closures of critical regions \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\).
Each region has a valid affine primal formula, and \(H\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All incident primal formulas have the common value \(x^*(\bar\theta)\), although their active sets and one-sided Jacobians may differ; the local directional behavior is determined region by region.

notation.meaning: Affine solution data of incident region j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of primal formulas where three or more critical-region closures meet.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar\theta\in\bigcap_{j=1}^m R_j\), where the closed critical regions \(R_j\) have formulas \(x_j(\theta)=K_j\theta+k_j\). Every \(x_j(\bar\theta)\) is optimal for the same QP. Strict convexity implies \[K_1\bar\theta+k_1=\cdots=K_m\bar\theta+k_m=x^*(\bar\theta).\] The incident regions may nevertheless have different active sets, matrices \(K_j\), and multiplier representations. For a direction \(d\) entering \(R_j\), the one-sided primal directional derivative is \(K_jd\). Thus a multiple-region intersection preserves the common primal value while permitting several distinct directional linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a point shared by several region closures, strict convexity forces every regional primal formula to agree, though active sets and directional derivatives may differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Region Boundary Intersections

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The common primal value follows plausibly from strict convexity when every closed-region formula remains valid at the intersection. No citation establishes those boundary-validity hypotheses or the stated directional behavior.

children.title: Multiparametric Degeneracy-Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Failures of unique active-set, multiplier, region, or solution representations and the resulting combinatorial burden.

children.title: Primal-Dual Degeneracy Classes
children.top_down_role: Parameter regions with redundant activity or nonunique multipliers.

children.title: Primal-Degenerate Regions
children.top_down_role: Parameter regions exhibiting redundant active constraints or nonunique active-set representations.

assumptions_latex: The active set at \(\theta\) is \(I(\theta)=\{i:G_i x^*(\theta)=w_i+S_i\theta\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A parameter is primal-degenerate exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}G_{I(\theta)}<|I(\theta)|\); a primal-degenerate region consists of parameters for which this dependence persists under its active-set description.

notation.meaning: Active constraint set at the optimizer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal degeneracy is fixed here as failure of LICQ for active inequality normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the inequality-constrained parametric QP, define \(I(\theta)=\{i:G_i x^*(\theta)=w_i+S_i\theta\}\). The parameter \(\theta\) is primal-degenerate when the active constraint normals are linearly dependent, equivalently \[\operatorname{rank}G_{I(\theta)}<|I(\theta)|.\] A critical-region description is primal-degenerate when this rank deficiency holds throughout its relative interior for the represented active set. The definition concerns the geometry of active primal constraints: it may hold even though \(H\succ0\) makes \(x^*(\theta)\) unique, and it generally destroys uniqueness of the active multiplier representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-degenerate parameter has linearly dependent active constraint normals; this can occur despite a unique primal optimizer and typically makes active multipliers nonunique.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Degenerate Regions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record consistently defines primal degeneracy as LICQ failure and its definition kind fits the leaf, but this terminology is convention-dependent in multiparametric QP and requires a specific source.

children.title: Dual-Degenerate Regions
children.top_down_role: Parameter regions exhibiting nonunique multiplier representations.

assumptions_latex: At \(\theta\), at least one KKT multiplier exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameter is dual-degenerate when every KKT multiplier has at least one active zero component; under unique multipliers this reduces to \(\lambda_i^*(\theta)=0\) for some \(i\in I(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual degeneracy is defined as failure of strict complementarity for every available multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda^*(\theta)\) be the set of KKT inequality multipliers and \(I(\theta)\) the active set. The parameter \(\theta\) is dual-degenerate when no optimal multiplier is strictly positive on every active constraint: \[\{\lambda\in\Lambda^*(\theta):\lambda_i>0\ \text{for all}\ i\in I(\theta)\}=\varnothing.\] If LICQ makes the multiplier unique, this is equivalent to \(\lambda_i^*(\theta)=0\) for at least one \(i\in I(\theta)\). A dual-degenerate region is a parameter set on whose relative interior this failure of strict complementarity persists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual degeneracy means no KKT multiplier is positive on every active constraint; with unique multipliers, some active constraint has zero multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Degenerate Regions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantified definition handles nonunique multipliers carefully, but whether dual degeneracy is defined as failure of strict complementarity for every multiplier is terminology-dependent and unsupported here.

children.title: Simultaneous Primal-Dual Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Regions where redundant activity coincides with multiplier nonuniqueness.

assumptions_latex: The QP admits KKT points throughout the parameter set under consideration.
Primal and dual degeneracy use the definitions of active-normal dependence and failure of strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Simultaneous primal-dual degeneracy holds where both \(\operatorname{rank}G_{I(\theta)}<|I(\theta)|\) and \(\{\lambda\in\Lambda^*(\theta):\lambda_{I(\theta)}>0\}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection of the stated primal- and dual-degeneracy predicates at one parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible parameter \(\theta\) exhibits simultaneous primal-dual degeneracy precisely when \[\operatorname{rank}G_{I(\theta)}<|I(\theta)|\quad\text{and}\quad\{\lambda\in\Lambda^*(\theta):\lambda_i>0\ \text{for every}\ i\in I(\theta)\}=\varnothing.\] The first predicate records linear dependence among active constraint normals; the second records failure of strict complementarity for every KKT multiplier. For a parameter region, simultaneous degeneracy means that both predicates hold throughout its relative interior. Neither primal uniqueness from \(H\succ0\) nor mere existence of multipliers excludes this joint condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous primal-dual degeneracy combines dependent active normals with the absence of any multiplier that is positive on all active constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Primal-Dual Degeneracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly combines the two stated degeneracy predicates and fits the terminal container, but both predicates rely on an uncited mpQP terminology convention.

children.title: Degeneracy Transitions Across Region Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Changes in primal or dual degeneracy status at neighboring region interfaces.

assumptions_latex: Adjacent critical regions have fixed active-set descriptions on their relative interiors.
The primal solution is continuous across their common boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal or dual degeneracy can arise or disappear only where an active-set rank condition changes or an active multiplier reaches or leaves zero; these events may alter region descriptions without discontinuity of the unique primal solution.

notation.meaning: Active sets on two adjacent regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary events changing LICQ or strict-complementarity status between adjacent active-set regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_-\) and \(R_+\) be adjacent active-set regions meeting at \(\bar\theta\). A primal-degeneracy transition occurs when the boundary active set gains or loses constraints so that the truth of \(\operatorname{rank}G_I=|I|\) changes. A dual-degeneracy transition occurs when an active multiplier component reaches zero at \(\bar\theta\) and is positive on only one incident region, or when no strictly complementary multiplier exists at the boundary. Such transitions may change the valid KKT basis, multiplier selection, and regional derivative while the unique primal solution remains continuous across \(\bar\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Across a region boundary, degeneracy changes when active-normal rank changes or an active multiplier crosses zero, even though the unique primal solution can remain continuous.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Transitions Across Region Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary-event description is plausible but not sufficiently reliable without a source, especially where multipliers are nonunique and a component reaching zero depends on the selected multiplier representation.

children.title: Redundant Region Representation Classes
children.top_down_role: Nonunique polyhedral descriptions caused by degeneracy.

children.title: Overlapping Region Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Distinct critical-region descriptions covering common parameter subsets.

assumptions_latex: Each region description is a polyhedron in the same parameter space.
Each description is paired with a valid optimizer formula on its represented set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The descriptions overlap nontrivially when \(\operatorname{relint}(R_1)\cap\operatorname{relint}(R_2)\neq\varnothing\); on that overlap, valid formulas must yield optimal solutions of the same QP, and unique primal solutions force their equality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlap means shared relative-interior parameters, distinguishing redundancy from ordinary shared faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two polyhedral critical-region descriptions \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are overlapping when \[\operatorname{relint}(R_1)\cap\operatorname{relint}(R_2)\neq\varnothing.\] This excludes the ordinary case in which distinct full-dimensional regions meet only on proper faces. If affine formulas \(x_1(\theta)\) and \(x_2(\theta)\) are both valid on their respective descriptions, then every \(\theta\in R_1\cap R_2\) makes both formulas optimal for the same QP. Under strict convexity, \(x_1(\theta)=x_2(\theta)\) throughout the overlap, although the descriptions or associated active sets may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two region descriptions overlap when their relative interiors intersect; with a unique optimizer, their solution formulas must agree wherever both descriptions apply.
knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping Region Descriptions

children.title: Nonminimal Region Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Critical-region representations containing redundant inequalities, faces, or subdivisions.

assumptions_latex: A critical region is represented as \(R=\{\theta:A\theta\leq b\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The description is nonminimal exactly when some indexed inequality can be deleted without changing \(R\), equivalently when \(\{\theta:A_{-i}\theta\leq b_{-i}\}\subseteq\{\theta:a_i^{\mathsf T}\theta\leq b_i\}\) for some \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimality concerns the inequality description, not the geometric or optimization-theoretic uniqueness of the region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=\{\theta\in\mathbb R^p:A\theta\leq b\}\), with rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\). This inequality description is nonminimal if there exists \(i\) such that \[\{\theta:A_{-i}\theta\leq b_{-i}\}=R.\] Equivalently, the remaining inequalities imply \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\theta\leq b_i\). Repeated inequalities, inequalities implied by nonnegative combinations of others, and inequalities that never support a facet are possible sources of nonminimality. Removing redundant inequalities changes the description but neither the represented critical region nor its associated optimizer formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region description is nonminimal when at least one inequality can be removed without changing the represented polyhedron or its optimizer formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonminimal Region Descriptions

children.title: Equivalent Polyhedral Representations
children.top_down_role: Alternative polyhedral descriptions encoding the same parametric solution behavior.

assumptions_latex: Two finite inequality systems describe subsets of the same parameter space.
Both systems are interpreted as closed polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representations are equivalent exactly when \(\{\theta:A\theta\leq b\}=\{\theta:C\theta\leq d\}\), or equivalently when each system implies every inequality of the other.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence is equality of represented parameter sets, regardless of row count, scaling, or redundancy.
